Initially created: 2025-11-27T18:04:01.992+09:00 by CHYou are a precise translator from Classical Chinese to $lang. Your task is to produce faithful, fluent $lang translations while preserving all formatting constraints exactly. Translate the following text from Classical Chinese into $lang.
Requirements: 1. The text contains page numbers in square brackets, such as [01], [02], etc. - These must be passed through unchanged. - Each page number must appear in exactly the same position in the translation as in the source. - The number of page markers in the output must match the input exactly.
2. Personal names, place names, titles, and other proper nouns should be rendered in Hànyǔ Pīnyīn with tone marks.
3. Do NOT transcribe the full Classical Chinese text into Pinyin.
4. Do NOT include explanatory notes, annotations, or commentary — output only the $lang translation.
5. The target language is $lang.
Input text:

p.seg: First year, spring, royal first month.
What is the “first year”?
It is the ruler’s inaugural year.
What is “spring”?
It is the beginning of the year.
Who is called the “king”?
It refers to Wénwáng.
Why is “king” stated first and “first month” thereafter?
It is the king’s first month.
What does it mean to say “the king’s first month”?
It is the grand unity.
Why does the lord not say “ascended the throne”?
It is the intention of Chénggōng.
What is accomplished in the intention of Chénggōng?
The lord was about to settle the state and restore it to Huán.
Why return it to Huán?
Huán was young yet honored,
Yǐn was elder yet lowly,
and their states of honor and humble were subtle;
the people of the state did not know.
Yǐn, being elder, was also virtuous,
and the great officers all supported Yǐn and set him up.
Yǐn thus declined to accept the rule,
so it was not yet known that Huán would necessarily be established.
And if Huán was to be established,
there was fear that the great officers could not support a young ruler,
therefore, Yǐn’s accession was for the sake of establishing Huán.
Yǐn, who was the elder and virtuous,
why was it unsuitable to establish him?
The proper heir is established by seniority, not by virtue;
the son is established by nobility, not by seniority.
Why was Huán noble?
It was because his mother was noble.
If the mother is noble, why is the son noble?
The son’s nobility comes from the mother,
the mother’s from the son.
Third month,
the lord and Yí Fù of Zhūlóu swore an alliance at Mèi.
What does “with” mean?
It means “together with,”
Huì, Jí, and Jì all mean “together with.”
Why is it sometimes called Huì,
sometimes Jí,
sometimes Jì?
Huì is like “all gathering”;
Jí implies urgency;
Jì suggests mutual effort.
To “join,” one desires it;
to “reach,” it is not by choice.
Who is Yí Fù?
He is the ruler of Zhūlóu.
Why is his name given?
It is his courtesy name.
Why refer to his courtesy name?
To praise him.
Why is he praised?
Because he allied with the lord.
Many swore an alliance with the lord;
why praise only this one?
Because he was praiseworthy, so he is praised.
How is he praiseworthy?
He advanced gradually.
What is Mèi?
It is the location of the meeting.
In summer, fifth month,
the Earl of Zhèng subdued Duàn at Yān.
What is meant by “subdued”?
It means “killed.”
If killed, why say “subdued”?
To magnify the wickedness of the Earl of Zhèng.
Why magnify his wickedness?
Because his mother wished to establish him,
yet he killed him;
it would have been better not to give, and that would suffice.
Who is Duàn?
He is the Earl of Zhèng’s younger brother.
Why is he not called “younger brother”?
Because he held the fief.
What of his position?
He held the fief.
When the men of Qí killed Wúzhī, why is the fief not given?
He was within.
When within, even if holding the fief, it is not stated;
when not holding the fief, even if outside, it is likewise not stated.
In autumn, seventh month,
the Heavenly King sent Zǎi Xuǎn to come and return the burial gifts for Huìgōng’s wife Zhòngzǐ.
Who is the Zǎi?
An official.
Who is Xuǎn?
It is his name.
Why use the official’s title and clan?
He was an officer.
Who is Huìgōng?
He is Yǐn’s father.
Who is Zhòngzǐ?
She is Huán’s mother.
Why is she not called “the wife”?
Because Huán was not yet ruler.
What is “burial gift”?
A funeral ceremony includes burial gifts.
Burial gifts are usually horses, or horses with bundles of silk;
carriages and horses are called fēng;
goods and wealth are called fù;
clothes and bedding are called suí.
If Huán was not yet ruler, why did the feudal lords come with burial gifts?
Because Yǐn established Huán,
so he informed the feudal lords of the mourning for Huán’s mother.
Then what does the record mean?
It is the intention of Chénggōng.
Why say “came”?
Because he did not actually perform the duty.
Why say “Huìgōng’s wife Zhòngzǐ”?
It is inclusive.
To be inclusive is not according to ritual.
Why not say “and Zhòngzǐ”?
Zhòngzǐ’s position was humble.
In the ninth month,
an alliance was sworn with the men of Sòng at Sù.
Who are “with”?
It refers to one of low rank within.
In winter, twelfth month,
the Earl of Jì came.
Who is the Earl of Jì?
He is a grandee of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he not called an envoy?
He came as a fugitive.
If a fugitive, why not say “fled”?
For the king there is no outside;
to say “fled” implies an outside.
Prince Yìshī died.
Why is there no specific date?
He was far away.
What is seen, what is heard,
what is passed on—all give different accounts.
Second year, spring,
the lord assembled with the Róng at Qián.
In summer, fifth month,
the people of Jǔ entered Xiàng.
What does “entered” mean?
They gained it but did not occupy it.
Wúhài led the army and entered Jí.
Who is Wúhài?
Zhǎn Wúhài.
Why is the clan name omitted?
It is a demotion.
Why a demotion?
It marks the beginning of extinction.
Did the extinction begin here?
It was before this.
If before this, why call this the beginning?
This is where the account begins.
Why is it narrated as beginning here?
It is the beginning in the “Chūnqiū.”
This is the extinction;
why is it stated “entered”?
It is to conceal a great fault.
In autumn, eighth month, on day Gēngchén,
the lord and the Róng swore an alliance at Táng.
In the ninth month,
Jǐ Lǚqiú came to meet the bride.
Who is Jǐ Lǚqiú?
He is a Dàfū of Jǐ.
Why is he not called an envoy?
In marriage rites, the host is not named.
Then by what title is one called?
They are referred to as father, elder brother, teacher, or friend.
When the Duke of Sòng sent Gōngsūn Shòu to present betrothal gifts,
then what is the reason for referring to the host?
Because the language was at a loss.
What does ‘language was at a loss’ mean?
There was no mother.
Then did Jǐ have a mother?
It is said: he did.
If so, why was the mother not named?
The mother did not communicate.
When a woman is met outside, it is not written,
why is it written here?
It is a reproach.
What is reproached?
It reproaches that there was no personal reception at first.
Did the lack of personal reception start here?
It existed before.
If it was before, why is it said to start here?
The start is only attributed here.
Why is it attributed here?
It is the beginning of “Chūnqiū.”
Why is the bride at times called “nǚ,”
at times “fù,”
and at times “fūrén”?
In her own state, she is called “nǚ”;
on the journey, she is called “fù”;
when entering the other state, she is called “fūrén.”
In the tenth month of winter,
Bó Jī returned to Jǐ.
Who is Bó Jī?
She is an internal daughter.
Why use the term “return”?
For a woman, marrying is called “return.”
Jǐ Zǐbó and Jǔ Zǐ took oaths at Mì.
Who is Jǐ Zǐbó?
There is nothing else notable.
On yǐmǎo day in the twelfth month,
Fūrén Zǐshì passed away.
Who is Fūrén Zǐshì?
She was the mother of Duke Yǐn.
Why is the burial not recorded?
It was Duke Chéng’s intention.
Why did Duke Chéng intend so?
Zǐ would not finish as sovereign,
so his mother would not finish as consort.
The people of Zhèng attacked Wèi.
In the third year, in spring, the King’s second month, on jǐsì,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
Why is it recorded?
To record the strange.
Then why is it sometimes named by day and sometimes not?
Why does it sometimes mention “shùo,” or not?
Saying a certain month, certain day, “shùo,”
and then “there was an eclipse,”
means the eclipse coincided with “shùo.”
As for sometimes naming the day, sometimes not,
sometimes it was missed before, sometimes after.
To miss before means “shùo” was before;
to miss after means “shùo” was after.
On gēngxū in the third month,
the Heavenly King passed away.
Why is burial not recorded?
For the Son of Heaven, death is recorded, not burial,
because the time can be ascertained.
For feudal lords, both death and burial are recorded,
for there is a living Son of Heaven,
whose time cannot always be ascertained.
Why is “bēng” sometimes used, and sometimes “hōng”?
For the Son of Heaven, “bēng”;
for feudal lords, “hōng”;
for Dàfū, “died”;
for shì, “did not receive stipend.”
In the fourth month of summer, on xīnmǎo,
Yǐn family died.
Who is the Yǐn family?
Dàfū of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he called by the family name?
It is a demotion.
Why a demotion?
To censure hereditary ministers.
Hereditary ministers are contrary to ritual.
An external Dàfū would not be recorded as “died,”
why is it so here?
The Heavenly King passed away; he was the feudal lord of the nobles.
In autumn,
the son of Wǔ family came to request funeral gifts.
Who is the son of Wǔ family?
A Dàfū of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he called the son of Wǔ family?
It is a reproach.
Why a reproach?
The father had died, and the son had not yet received his commission.
Why is he not called an envoy?
He was not yet enthroned during mourning.
Why was “the son of Wǔ family came to request gifts” recorded?
It is a reproach.
What is reproached?
It is not ritual to request in mourning matters;
to ask for gifts is contrary to propriety.
It shows he communicated with those below.
On gēngchén, the eighth month,
Duke Hé of Sòng died.
In the twelfth month of winter,
the Marquis of Qí and the Earl of Zhèng took oaths at Shímén.
On guǐwèi,
Duke Miù of Sòng was buried.
As for burials, why is the date sometimes given, sometimes not?
If not at the proper time and the date is given,
it is a hasty burial.
If not at the proper time and no date is given,
it is a slow burial.
If after the proper time and the date is given,
it is concealment.
If after the proper time and no date is given,
it is said to be “unable to bury.”
If at the proper time and the date is not given, it is correct.
If at the proper time and the date is given, it indicates a danger of being unable to bury.
At this time, what was the danger?
Duke Xuān said to Duke Miù:
“If it is a matter of loving my daughter,
then my love for Yǔyí is not as great.
If it is a matter of making her the ruler for the altars and ancestral temple,
then Yǔyí is not as fitting as my daughter.
Why not have you finally become ruler?”
Duke Xuān died,
Duke Miù came to power,
Duke Miù banished his two sons, Duke Zhuāng Féng and Zuǒshī Bó,
saying:
“You are my sons;
while alive, do not see each other;
when dead, do not mourn for each other.”
Yǔyí responded, saying:
“The late ruler entrusted his state, giving it to someone who could be lord of the altars and temple.
Now, you banish your two sons and will give the state to Yǔyí;
this was not the intent of the late ruler.
Moreover, if sons can be banished,
then the late ruler should have banished me.”
Duke Miù said:
“That the late ruler did not banish you can be readily known;
I hold this position as regent.”
In the end, the state was given to Yǔyí.
Duke Zhuāng Féng killed Yǔyí.
Therefore, the gentleman greatly values uprightness;
the calamity of Sòng was caused by Duke Xuān.
In the fourth year, spring, King’s second month.
The people of Jǔ attacked Qǐ,
and took Móulóu.
What is Móulóu?
It is a town of Qǐ.
When outer towns are taken, it is not recorded;
why is it recorded here?
Because it was the first time a town was seized.
On wùshēn,
Zhōu Xū of Wèi murdered his lord Wán.
Why is the state surname used?
Because he was serving his own state.
In summer,
the Duke and the Duke of Sòng met at Qīng.
What does “met” mean?
It was not previously arranged.
One lord went out,
another invited him.
The Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, the people of Cài, and the people of Wèi attacked Zhèng.
Autumn,
Huī led the army and met with the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, the people of Cài, and the people of Wèi to attack Zhèng.
Who is Huī?
He is Prince Huī.
Why is he not called "Prince"?
It is a demotion.
Why is he demoted?
He was involved in the murder of the Duke.
How was he involved in the murder of the Duke?
Prince Huī flattered Yǐn Gōng,
and said to Yǐn Gōng:
"The common people are at peace because of you,
the various lords are pleased with you.
Why not finally become the ruler?"
Yǐn said,
"Not so.
I have ordered the trimming of my fur coat;
I will grow old there."
Prince Huī feared that these words would reach Huán,
so he said to Huán:
"I have spoken to Yǐn on your behalf.
Yǐn said:
'I will not return.'"
Huán said:
"If so, what should be done?"
He said:
"Let us create disorder
and assassinate Yǐn Gōng."
At the sacrifice at Zhōngwū, they killed Yǐn Gōng.
In the ninth month,
the people of Wèi killed Zhōuyū at Pú.
Why is it said 'people'?
It is phrasing used for punishing traitors.
Winter, twelfth month,
the people of Wèi established Jìn.
Who is Jìn?
He is Prince Jìn.
What does "establish" mean?
To establish when one ought not to be established.
Why is it said 'people'?
It is phrasing to indicate that the multitude established him.
Then who established him?
Shí Què established him.
Since Shí Què established him,
why say 'people'?
Because it was what the multitude wanted to do.
Even though the multitude wished to establish him,
their establishing him was not proper.
In the fifth year, spring,
the Duke viewed fish at Táng.
Why is this recorded?
It is criticism.
What is being criticized?
That it was distant.
Why did the Duke go far to view fish?
It was because of the arrival of Lái.
The Duke displayed fish worth a hundred gold pieces.
What does "the arrival of Lái" mean?
It is a way of praising its greatness and beauty.
What is Táng?
It is a settlement above the Jì.
In summer, fourth month,
burial of Wèi Huán Gōng.
In autumn,
the army of Wèi entered Shèng.
Why is it sometimes said "led the army" and sometimes not said?
When the general is esteemed and many, it is said so-and-so led the army;
when the general is esteemed and few, it is said "general";
when the general is low and many, it is said "army";
when the general is low and few, it is said "people."
When the ruler is the general, it is not said "led the army,"
for the Chronicle records what is weighty.
In the ninth month,
they inspected the palace of Zhòngzǐ.
What does it mean to inspect a palace?
To inspect is like entering the residence;
it is the first sacrifice to Zhòngzǐ.
Why was the sacrifice to Zhòngzǐ performed before Huán Gōng became ruler?
Yǐn performed it for Huán,
and so performed the sacrifice to his mother for Huán.
Then why is it mentioned?
It was the intention of Chéng Gōng.
At the initial offering, six feathers.
What does "initial" mean?
It means the beginning.
What are six feathers?
They are part of the dance.
Why is it recorded that six feathers were offered in the beginning?
It is criticism.
What is criticized?
Criticism of the beginning of usurpation among the Gōng.
How is using six feathers usurpation?
The Son of Heaven uses eight rows of dancers,
the gōng use six,
the feudal lords use four.
Who are the gōng?
Who are the feudal lords?
The three gōng of the Son of Heaven are called gōng,
the descendants of kings are called gōng,
the other large states are called hóu,
the small states are called bó, zǐ, or nán.
Who are the three gōng of the Son of Heaven?
They are ministers of the Son of Heaven.
If they are ministers of the Son of Heaven, why are there three?
East of Shǎn is presided over by Zhōu Gōng,
west of Shǎn is presided over by Zhào Gōng,
one minister stays inside.
Did the usurpation among the gōng begin here?
It was before this.
If it was before this, why say it began here?
Usurpation among the gōng may yet be spoken of,
but usurpation of the Son of Heaven may not be spoken of.
The people of Zhūlóu and the people of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
Borer insect.
Why is it recorded?
To record a disaster.
Winter, twelfth month, Xīnsì day,
Prince Kōu died.
The people of Sòng attacked Zhèng,
and besieged Chánggě.
When a town is attacked, it is not called 'besieged,'
why is 'besieged' used here?
Because it was powerful.
In the sixth year, spring,
the people of Zhèng came and surrendered Píng.
What does "surrender Píng" mean?
"Surrender Píng" is like abandoning the wall.
Why speak of 'abandoning the wall'?
They failed to defend it.
They said, "We completed and failed."
We had not come to a settlement with the people of Zhèng.
Then why had we not come to a settlement with the people of Zhèng?
In the battle of Húrǎng,
Yǐn Gōng captured it.
Then why is 'battle' not mentioned?
Because to mention it would be taboo.
In summer, fifth month, Xīnyǒu day,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí and swore an alliance at Ài.
In autumn, seventh month.
Why is this recorded when nothing happened?
Even when there is nothing to record,
if a season is skipped, it is recorded.
Why record seasons skipped?
The Spring and Autumn Annals are arranged by year,
only when all the four seasons occur does it become a year.
In winter,
the people of Sòng took Chánggě.
When an outer state takes a town, it is not recorded,
why is it recorded here?
Because it was a long time.
In the seventh year, in the third month of the King,
Shū Jī married to Jì.
The Marquis of Téng died.
Why is his personal name not given?
Because it is a minor state.
If a minor state, why still call him marquis?
It is not avoided.
The Spring and Autumn Annals do not avoid giving the same titles to noble or base,
nor avoid using the same words for good or bad.
In summer,
they walled Zhōngqiū.
What is Zhōngqiū?
It is an inner settlement.
Why is "walled Zhōngqiū" recorded?
Because it is important enough to record again.
The Marquis of Qí sent his younger brother Nián to present gifts.
Why is it said 'younger brother'?
The younger brother of the same mother is called 'younger brother,'
the elder brother of the same mother is called 'elder brother.'
In autumn,
the Duke attacked Zhūlóu.
In winter,
the King sent Fán Bó to come for a diplomatic visit.
The Róng attacked Fán Bó at Chǔqiū
and took him away.
Who is Fán Bó?
He is a great officer of the Son of Heaven.
As for this diplomatic visit,
why does it say “attacked him”?
It means he was seized.
If he was seized, why describe it as “attacked”?
To magnify the event.
Why magnify it?
To show that the Chinese are not to be seized by the Yi and Dí barbarians.
What about the territory?
The same reason, to magnify the event.
In the eighth year, spring,
the Dùke of Sòng and the Marquess of Wèi met at Chuí.
In the third month,
the Duke of Zhèng sent Wǎn to bring back Bǐng.
Who is Wǎn?
A minor figure of Zhèng.
What is Bǐng?
A fief of Zhèng used for soup and bath offerings.
The Son of Heaven had business at Tàishān,
and all the feudal lords followed.
At the foot of Tàishān,
all the feudal lords had towns for soup and bath offerings.
On the day Gēngyín,
I entered Bǐng.
Why does it say “entered”?
It was difficult.
Why specify the day?
It was difficult.
Why use “I”?
“I” does not mean only us;
Qí also desired it.
In summer, the sixth month, Jǐhài,
the Marquess of Cài, Kǎofù, died.
Xīnhài,
the lord of Sù died.
In autumn, seventh month, Gēngwǔ,
the Duke of Sòng, the Marquess of Qí, and the Marquess of Wèi swore an oath at Wǎwū.
In the eighth month,
Cài Xuān Gōng was buried.
Why is the name given at death, but not at burial?
The death follows the official title,
while the burial follows the master of the household.
Why is the date given at death but not at burial?
Death is reported immediately; burial is not formally announced.
Ninth month, Xīnmǎo,
the Duke and the people of Jǔ swore an oath at Bāolái.
Why did the Duke make an oath with minor states?
Because when referring to “people,” there is no doubt.
Locusts.
In winter, the twelfth month,
Wú Hài died.
This is Zhǎn Wú Hài.
Why no surname?
The clan was extinct,
so for his whole life he had no clan name.
In the ninth year, spring,
the King sent Nán Jì for a diplomatic visit.
Third month, Guǐyǒu,
there was heavy rain, thunder, and lightning.
Why is it recorded?
To record anomalies.
What is anomalous about it?
It was out of season.
Gēngchén,
there was heavy rain and snow.
Why is it recorded?
To record anomalies.
What is anomalous about it?
It was extremely unseasonable.
Xiá died.
Who is Xiá?
One of our great officers not yet formally appointed.
Summer,
the city walls of Láng were built.
Autumn, seventh month.
Winter,
the Duke met the Marquess of Qí at Bǐng.
In the tenth year, spring, king’s second month,
the Duke met the Marquess of Qí and the Duke of Zhèng at Zhōngqiū.
In summer,
Huī led the army and joined the people of Qí and Zhèng to attack Sòng.
This is Prince Huī,
why is he not called Prince?
It is a demotion.
Why demoted?
He was a criminal in the reign of Yǐn Gōng.
Therefore, throughout the Annals of Yǐn, he is demoted.
Sixth month, Rénxū,
the Duke defeated the army of Sòng at Jiān.
Xīnwèi, took Gào.
Xīnsì, took Fáng.
Why is the date given for taking towns, when usually it is not?
Because two towns were taken in one month.
Why note that two were taken in one month?
To show the seriousness.
For great evils within a state, they are avoided.
Why then emphasize it?
The **Chūnqiū** records internal matters in brief, external matters in detail.
Major external wrongdoings are recorded,
minor ones are not;
for major internal wrongs, they are veiled,
minor ones are recorded.
In autumn,
the people of Sòng and Wèi entered Zhèng.
The people of Sòng, Cài, and Wèi attacked Zài;
the Duke of Zhèng attacked and took it.
Why is it said “attacked and took”?
Because it was easy.
Why was it easy?
He relied on their strength.
Whose strength?
The strength of the people of Sòng, Cài, and Wèi.
Winter, tenth month, Rénwǔ,
the people of Qí and Zhèng entered Shèng.
In the eleventh year, spring,
the Marquess of Téng and the Marquess of Xuē came for an audience.
Why is it called “audience”?
When feudal lords visit, it is called “audience”;
when great officers visit, it is called “diplomatic visit.”
Why are both terms used?
Because they are petty states.
Summer, fifth month,
the Duke met the Duke of Zhèng at Qílí.
Autumn, seventh month, Gēngwǔ,
the Duke, the Marquess of Qí, and the Duke of Zhèng entered Xǔ.
Winter, eleventh month, Gēngchén,
the Duke died.
Why is his burial not recorded?
It is concealed.
Why conceal it?
He was murdered.
If murdered, why no record of burial?
In the **Chūnqiū**, if a ruler is murdered and his killer is not avenged,
the burial is not recorded,
because it is as though he had no ministers or sons.
Zǐ Shěnzi said:
“If a ruler is murdered
and his ministers do not avenge him,
they are not true ministers.
If a son does not take vengeance
he is not a true son.
Burial is the business of the living.
In the **Chūnqiū**, if a ruler is murdered and the killer is not avenged,
the burial is not recorded,
to show it is not related to ministers or sons.”
Why is the Duke’s place of death not recorded?
It could not be spoken of.
Why does Yǐn have no first month?
Yǐn wished to yield to Huán,
so did not keep the first month as his own.
In the first year, in spring, in the King's first month,
the Gōng assumed the throne.
When one succeeds in slaying the ruler, it is not stated "assumed the throne";
why, then, does it state "assumed the throne" here?
It accords with his intentions.
In the third month,
the Gōng met with Zhèng Bó at Chuí.
Zhèng Bó, with a jade disk, requested to borrow Xǔ Field.
Why does it say "with a jade disk, requested to borrow"?
It was an exchange.
If it was an exchange, then why say "requested to borrow"?
Out of respect.
Why out of respect?
Because when the Son of Heaven remains,
the feudal lords may not possess land arbitrarily.
What is Xǔ Field?
It is the lodging fief for Lǔ’s envoys upon audience.
The feudal lords occasionally have audience with the Son of Heaven;
in the Son of Heaven's suburbs,
all the lords have a lodging fief there.
This is Lǔ’s lodging fief,
so why call it Xǔ Field?
To avoid the name of taking Zhōu’s land.
To avoid naming the taking of Zhōu’s land,
then why call it Xǔ Field?
Because it is attached to Xǔ.
Why is it attached to Xǔ?
Because it is near Xǔ.
As for this settlement,
why is it called "field"?
When there are many fields and few settlements, it is called "field";
when there are many settlements and few fields, it is called "settlement".
In summer, the fourth month, on Dīngwèi day,
the Gōng and Zhèng Bó swore an oath at Yuè.
In autumn, there was a great flood.
Why is it recorded?
To record calamity.
In winter, the tenth month.
In the second year, in spring, in the King's first month, on Wùshēn day,
Sòng Dū murdered his ruler Yǔ Yí and his minister Kǒng Fù.
What does "and" mean?
It means implicated.
Many have murdered their rulers,
were there none others implicated?
It is answered: There were.
Qiú Mù and Xún Xī,
both were implicated.
Other than Qiú Mù and Xún Xī, were there none others not implicated?
It is answered: There were.
If so, why is it recorded here?
Because of their worthiness.
How was Kǒng Fù worthy?
Kǒng Fù can be said to have righteousness manifest in his countenance.
How was his righteousness manifest in his countenance?
Dū wished to murder Shāng Gōng.
If Kǒng Fù were alive and present, Shāng Gōng could not be murdered.
Therefore, he first attacked Kǒng Fù’s family.
Shāng Gōng, knowing that with Kǒng Fù’s death, he too would die,
hurried to rescue him;
both died.
When Kǒng Fù stood with upright countenance in the court,
none dared offend to harm their ruler;
Kǒng Fù can be said to have righteousness manifest in his countenance.
The Téngzǐ came to audience.
In the third month,
the Gōng met the Qí Hóu, Chén Hóu, and Zhèng Bó at Jì,
to resolve Sòng’s disorder.
Among internal matters, grave wickedness is avoided by euphemism;
why use the term directly here?
Because it is remote.
That which is heard differs in statement;
what is seen differs in statement;
what is heard by report differs in statement.
Yǐn was also distant,
so why euphemize it?
Because Yǐn was virtuous and Huán was ignoble.
In summer, the fourth month,
the great Gào tripod was taken from Sòng.
Since it was taken from Sòng,
why is it called the Gào tripod?
Vessels follow their name;
territories follow their owner.
Why do vessels follow their name?
Why do territories follow their owner?
As for vessels and people,
it is not immediately theirs.
Sòng first took it unrighteously,
therefore it is called the Gào tripod.
But as for territory and people, it is not so;
soon, one may call it theirs.
If so, can taking make it theirs?
Answer: No.
Why not?
Like the wife of the King of Chǔ, Wèi,
at no time could it be so.
On the Wùshēn day,
it was placed in the ancestral temple.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What criticism?
They thereby perpetuated disorder and accepted bribes,
placing it in the ancestral temple,
which is not in accordance with ritual propriety.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the Jì Hóu came to audience.
The Cài Hóu and Zhèng Bó met at Dèng;
when relations are severed, it is not stated as a meeting;
why, here, is it called a meeting?
Perhaps because Dèng participated in the meeting.
In the ninth month,
they entered Qǐ.
The Gōng and the Róng swore an oath at Táng.
In winter,
the Gōng returned from Táng.
In the third year, in spring, in the first month,
the Gōng met the Qí Hóu at Yíng.
In summer,
the Qí Hóu and the Wèi Hóu gave mutual commands at Pú.
What does "mutual commands" mean?
It means they gave commands to each other.
Why state "mutually gave commands"?
Because it approaches correctness.
How does this approach correctness?
In antiquity, there were no oaths,
one settled matters by agreement and then withdrew.
In the sixth month,
the Gōng met the Jì Hóu at Shèng.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on Rénchén, the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse,
total.
What does "total" mean?
It means complete.
Gōngzǐ Huī went to Qí to welcome the bride.
In the ninth month,
the Qí Hóu escorted Jiāng Shì to Huān.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
That a feudal lord crossed state borders to escort the woman,
which is not in accord with ritual propriety.
Now she was entering the state,
so why not call her "Lady"?
From our perspective, this refers to Qí;
for parents to their daughter,
though she become lady of a neighboring state,
they still say "our Jiāng Shì".
The Gōng met the Qí Hóu at Huān,
Lady Jiāng Shì arrived from Qí.
Why did Huī not accompany her?
He was able to meet with the Gōng.
In winter,
the Qí Hóu sent his younger brother Nián as envoy.
There was a year of abundance.
Why is abundance recorded?
It is recorded as a thing of joy.
Why is "great abundance" recorded?
It is likewise recorded as a thing of joy.
Why does it state "abundance" here?
It was only a year of modest abundance.
Why, there, "great abundance"?
It was an extremely fruitful year.
But is a year of only modest abundance sufficient to merit joy?
There is reliance upon abundance.
In the fourth year, in the first month of spring,
the Duke hunted at Láng.
What is “hunt”?
It is field hunting.
In spring it is called “miáo,”
in autumn “sōu,”
and in winter “shòu.”
Routine matters are not recorded;
why is this written?
It is to censure.
Why censure?
It was distant.
Why must the feudal lords perform field hunts?
First, to offer dried meat;
second, to receive guests;
third, to replenish the lord’s kitchen.
In summer,
the King of Heaven sent Zǎi Qú Bó Jiū to present gifts.
Who is Zǎi Qú Bó Jiū?
He is a grandee of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he referred to as Zǎi Qú Bó Jiū?
He is a lower grandee.
In the fifth year, in the first month of spring, on jiǎxū and jǐchǒu days,
the Marquis of Chén, Bào, died.
Why record two days?
Because of the confusion at his death.
On jiǎxū day he was lost,
on jǐchǒu day he died and was found.
The gentlemen doubted,
therefore two dates are given for his death.
In summer,
the Marquis of Qí and the Earl of Zhèng went to Jì.
Such mutual visits are not recorded;
why is this written?
Because they meet apart, it is not called an “assembly.”
The King of Heaven sent the son of Réng Shū to present gifts.
Who is the son of Réng Shū?
He is a grandee of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he referred to as the son of Réng Shū?
It is a censure.
Why censure?
It censures the old father, while the son takes his place in government.
Interred Chén Huán Gōng.
Fortified Zhùqiū.
In autumn,
the Cáiy people, Wèi people, and Chén people followed the king to attack Zhèng.
Why does it say “followed the king to attack Zhèng”?
To follow the king is to be correct.
Great yú ceremony.
What is the great yú ceremony?
It is a drought sacrifice.
Then why not mention the drought?
If “yú” is said, drought is implied;
if drought is said, “yú” is not.
Why is it recorded?
To record calamity.
Locusts.
Why is it recorded?
To record calamity.
In winter,
Zhōu Gōng went to Cáo.
Such mutual visits are not recorded;
why is this written?
Because he passed through our land.
In the sixth year, in the first month of spring,
there came “Shí.”
What is “Shí” coming?
It is as if to say, “this person comes.”
Who is meant?
It refers to Zhōu Gōng.
Why is he called “Shí comes”?
It is to slight him.
Why slight him?
Because he transformed us.
In the fourth month of summer,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Jì at Chéng.
On rénwǔ day, the eighth month of autumn,
a grand review was held.
What is a grand review?
It is an inspection of chariots.
Why is it recorded?
Presumably because it is rarely written.
The Cáiy people killed Chén Tuó.
Who is Chén Tuó?
He is the lord of Chén.
Since he is the lord of Chén, why is he called Chén Tuó?
He was cut off.
Why was he cut off?
He was despised.
Why was he despised?
Because he was licentious abroad.
Where was he licentious?
He was licentious in Cáiy;
the Cáiy people killed him.
On dīngmǎo day, the ninth month,
a legitimate son was born.
Who was the legitimate son?
It refers to Zhuāng Gōng.
Why call it a legitimate son?
It is joy at having an heir.
Never before has there been an expression of joy at having an heir;
why is it said so here?
Because there had long been no heir.
Zǐ Gōngyáng Zǐ said:
“Is it perhaps because Huán was ill?”
In winter,
the Marquis of Jì came to court.
In the seventh year, in the second month of spring, on jǐhài day,
Xiánqiū was burned.
Who burned it?
Woodcutters did.
Who are the woodcutters?
They attacked with fire.
Why mention attacking with fire?
Each earlier time, it was attacked with fire.
What is Xiánqiū?
It is a town of Zhūlóu.
Why is it not attached to Zhūlóu?
It became a state.
Why did it become a state?
Because the ruler survived there.
In summer,
Gǔ Bó Suí came to court.
The Marquis of Dèng, Wú Lí, came to court.
Why are their personal names recorded?
They are rulers who lost their lands.
Why is it said “Marquis came to court”?
Among the high nobility, if there is no successor,
they are treated as when they first took their title.
In the eighth year, in the first month of spring, on jǐmǎo day,
zhēng sacrifice was performed.
What is zhēng?
It is the winter sacrifice.
In spring it is called cí;
in summer, yuè;
in autumn, cháng;
in winter, zhēng.
Routine matters are not recorded;
why is this written?
It is to censure.
Why censure?
It is to censure for frequency.
If frequent, it becomes profane;
if profaned, it ceases to be reverent.
The gentleman, in sacrifice,
is reverent but not profane.
If too infrequent, it leads to negligence;
if negligent, it leads to forgetfulness.
If the gentleman falls short of these four things,
then in winter he has no fur,
in summer no linen.
The King of Heaven sent Jiā Fù to present gifts.
In the fifth month of summer, on dīngchǒu day,
zhēng sacrifice was performed.
Why record it?
It is to censure for frequency.
In autumn,
attacked Zhūlóu.
In the tenth month of winter,
it snowed.
Why is it recorded?
To record an anomaly.
What was the anomaly?
It was out of season.
Jì Gōng came,
and so received the Queen on behalf of the King at Jì.
Who is Jì Gōng?
He is one of the Three Excellencies of the Son of Heaven.
Why is it not said that he was sent as an envoy?
In marriage rituals, the host is not named.
What does "so" (suì) mean?
It means the living affairs.
Great officers do not handle living affairs,
so why mention "so" here?
Because the one who accomplished the mission was myself.
How is it that the accomplishment of the mission lies with me?
I was made the matchmaker;
if it was proper, I then used that opportunity to go and receive her.
When a woman is in her own state, she is called "the lady";
why is she called "the Queen" here?
Because for a king, there is no "outside."
Thus, the wording is complete.
2.9.1 In the ninth
year, in spring,
Jì Jì Jiāng returned to the capital.
Since the wording is complete,
why is she called Jì Jì Jiāng?
Speaking from our standpoint, Jì;
as for parents speaking of their child,
even if she becomes Queen of the Son of Heaven,
they would still say, "our Jì Jiāng."
What is the capital?
It is the residence of the Son of Heaven.
What does "capital" (jīng) mean?
It means "great."
What does "shī" (master) mean?
It means "multitude."
The residence of the Son of Heaven
must be described with words meaning multitude and greatness.
In the fourth month of summer.
In the seventh month of autumn.
In winter,
the Earl of Cáo sent his heir Shè Gū to present tribute.
When feudal lords come, it is called "presenting tribute";
but this was the heir,
so why use the term "present tribute"?
The Spring and Autumn Annals reprimands elder statesmen who allow their sons to replace them in affairs of state;
therefore, it is not clear whether this was in Qí
or in Cáo.
In the tenth year, in spring, in the royal first month, on Gēngshēn day,
the Earl of Cáo Zhōngshēng died.
In the fifth month of summer,
Cáo Huán Gōng was buried.
In autumn,
our lord met with the Marquess of Wèi at Táoqiū,
but did not encounter each other.
What does "meet" (huì) mean?
It means they agreed to meet.
Why does it say, "did not encounter"?
Because our lord did not see the other as essential.
In winter, in the twelfth month, on Bǐngwǔ day,
the Marquess of Qí, the Marquess of Wèi, and the Earl of Zhèng came to fight at Láng.
What is Láng?
It is a town near us.
If it is our neighboring town, why does it say, "came to fight at Láng"?
Because it was near.
How was it near?
It was near to being encircled.
This was a partial battle;
why does it not mention the defeat of the army?
When it is internal, it is not called a battle;
to say "battle" is itself to mean defeat.
In the eleventh year, in spring, in the first month,
the men of Qí, Wèi, and Zhèng swore an alliance at Ècáo.
In the fifth month of summer, on Guǐwèi day,
the Earl of Zhèng Wùshēng died.
In the seventh month of autumn,
Duke Zhuāng of Zhèng was buried.
In the ninth month,
the men of Sòng seized Zhèng Jì Zhòng.
Who is Jì Zhòng?
He is the Chancellor of Zhèng.
Why is his personal name not given?
Because he is virtuous.
Where does the virtue of Jì Zhòng lie?
He is known for his wisdom in matters of expediency.
How did he show his sense of expediency?
In ancient times, the state of Zhèng was located at Liú.
A predecessor of the Earl of Zhèng was favored by the Duke of Guài,
made connections through his lady to acquire that state,
and moved Zhèng there,
making Liú a country estate.
After Duke Zhuāng died,
and was buried,
Jì Zhòng was going to carry out memorial offerings at Liú;
the road passed through Sòng,
and the men of Sòng seized him.
They said to him:
“Depose Hù for us and install Tú.”
Jì Zhòng did not agree;
then, his lord would surely die
and the state would be lost.
If he did as they asked,
his lord could be changed from death to life,
the state from destruction to survival.
If he delayed for a while,
Tú could still be sent out,
and Hù could still return,
but if that could not be achieved, he would be troubled,
and then there would be the state of Zhèng.
Those in ancient times who had a sense of expediency,
Jì Zhòng’s expediency was of this kind.
What is expediency (quán)?
Expediency means to go against the normal order
in order for good to be achieved.
The use of expediency
is found only in matters of life and death.
To exercise expediency has a proper way:
to lower oneself in order to carry it out,
not to harm others,
not to kill others to save oneself,
not to ruin others to preserve oneself.
A gentleman does not act thus.
Tú returned to Zhèng.
Why is the personal name used for Tú?
Because he was carried along by Jì Zhòng.
Why does it say "returned"?
To indicate compliance with Jì Zhòng.
Zhèng Hù fled to Wèi.
Why is the personal name used for Hù?
In the Spring and Autumn Annals, “Earl, Viscount, Baron” are equal,
and no derogatory words are used.
Róu met with the Duke of Sòng, the Marquess of Chén, and Lord Cài, forming an alliance at Zhé.
Who is Róu?
He is our great officer who had not yet been granted a title.
Our lord met the Duke of Sòng at Fūtóng.
"The Eleventh Year of Duke Huán"
2.11.8 In the twelfth month of winter, our lord met the Duke of Sòng at Kǎn.
In the twelfth year, in spring, in the first month.
In the sixth month of summer, on Rényín day,
our lord met the Marquess of Jì and the Viscount of Jǔ,
and swore an alliance at Ōushé.
In the seventh month of autumn, on Dīnghài day,
our lord met the Duke of Sòng and the men of Yān, and swore an alliance at Gǔqiū.
In the eighth month, on Rénchén day,
the Marquess of Chén Yuè died.
Our lord met the Duke of Sòng at Tán.
In winter, in the eleventh month,
our lord met the Duke of Sòng at Guī.
On Bǐngxū day,
our lord met the Earl of Zhèng,
and swore an alliance at Wǔfù.
On Bǐngxū day,
the Marquess of Wèi Jìn died.
In the twelfth month,
the troops of Zhèng attacked Sòng.
On Dīngwèi day,
they fought at Sòng.
When fighting occurs, it is not termed "to attack";
why does it use the term "attack" here?
To avoid suspicion.
What suspicion is avoided?
Suspicion of Zhèng men fighting each other.
This was a partial battle;
why does it not mention defeat of the army?
When internal, it is not called a battle;
to say "battle" is itself to mean defeat.
In the spring, second month, of the thirteenth year,
the Duke assembled with Jì Hóu and Zhèng Bó.
On Jǐsì day,
they, together with Qí Hóu, Sòng Gōng, Wèi Hóu, and the Yān people, engaged in battle.
The armies of Qí, Sòng, Wèi, and Yān were defeated.
Why was it noted as an event of a later date?
Because they relied on external forces.
How did they rely on external forces?
Only by acquiring Jì Hóu and Zhèng Bó were they able to settle the date.
Internally, war is not mentioned;
why is war mentioned here then?
Because they followed outsiders.
Why follow outsiders?
Because they relied on outsiders, therefore followed them.
Why is the location not recorded?
Because it was nearby.
Where was it near to?
Near to the encirclement.
Láng was also near;
for what reason is the location recorded for Láng?
Láng could still be recorded for its location.
In the third month,
Duke Xuān of Wèi was buried.
In summer,
there was a great flood.
In autumn, seventh month.
In winter, tenth month.
In the spring, first month, of the fourteenth year,
the Duke assembled with Zhèng Bó at Cáo.
There was no ice.
Why was this recorded?
To record the extraordinary.
In the fifth month,
Zhèng Bó sent his younger brother Yǔ to come and swear alliance.
What is "the fifth month"?
It is only that nothing more is heard of it.
On the rénshēn day of the eighth month in autumn,
the imperial granary was damaged by disaster.
What is the imperial granary?
It is where sacrificial grains are stored.
Why record the disaster at the imperial granary?
To record the calamity.
On yǐhài day,
there was a tasting of offerings.
Ordinary matters are not recorded;
why is this recorded?
It is a criticism.
What is the criticism?
It is to criticize the tasting.
It is said: was it worth tasting?
The imperial granary suffered disaster,
it would have been better not to taste at all.
In winter, twelfth month, on dīngsì day,
Lù Fù, Duke of Qí, died.
The people of Sòng, together with Qí, Wèi, Cài, and Chén, attacked Zhèng.
What does "together with" mean?
It means they acted according to their intent.
In the spring, second month, of the fifteenth year,
the Son of Heaven sent Jiā Fù to request chariots.
Why is this recorded?
It is a criticism.
What is the criticism?
The king should not make requests;
to request chariots is not accordance with ritual.
In the third month, yǐwèi day,
the Son of Heaven passed away.
In the summer, fourth month, jǐsì day,
Duke Xī of Qí was buried.
In the fifth month,
Zhèng Bó, Tú, fled to Cài.
Why is Tú specifically named?
Because he was deprived of rightful position.
Zhèng Shìzǐ Hū returned again to Zhèng.
Why refer to him as Shìzǐ?
Because he restored the rightful position.
Why is it sometimes called "returned" and sometimes "returned again"?
To "return again" means one fled from evil and returned without evil;
to "re-enter"
means to depart without evil and enter with evil;
to "enter"
means evil both leaving and entering;
to "return"
means none is evil either going or coming.
Xǔ Shū entered Xǔ.
The Duke assembled with Qí Hóu at Hào.
People of Zhūlóu, Móu, and Gé came to court.
Why are they all called “people”?
Because they were among the yí and dí (barbarians).
In autumn, ninth month,
Zhèng Bó Tú entered Yù.
What is Yù?
A town of Zhèng.
Why is it not said, "entered Zhèng"?
It is simply not mentioned.
Why is it simply not mentioned?
Because Jì Zhòng has died.
Then why is it not said that Hū has fled?
To say "Hū" was to refer to the slight status of the lord;
with Jì Zhòng present, all was preserved;
with Jì Zhòng gone, all was lost.
In winter, eleventh month,
the Duke assembled with Qí Hóu, Sòng Gōng, Wèi Hóu, and Chén Hóu at Chǐ,
and attacked Zhèng.
In the spring, first month, of the sixteenth year,
the Duke assembled with Sòng Gōng, Cài Hóu, and Wèi Hóu at Cáo.
In the summer, fourth month,
the Duke assembled with Sòng Gōng, Wèi Hóu, Chén Hóu, and Cài Hóu to attack Zhèng.
In autumn, seventh month,
the Duke returned from attacking Zhèng.
In winter,
a wall was built at Xiàng.
In the eleventh month,
Wèi Hóu Shuò fled to Qí.
Why specifically name Wèi Hóu Shuò?
Because his line was severed.
Why was it severed?
Because he offended the Son of Heaven.
How did he offend the Son of Heaven?
He was appointed to guard Wèi Shuò,
but could not make Wèi small and obedient,
and thus crossed over to Dàiyīn in Qí.
He was entrusted with this,
but fled rather than bear responsibility for his crime.
In the spring, first month, bǐngchén day, of the seventeenth year,
the Duke assembled with Qí Hóu and Jì Hóu,
and made a covenant at Huáng.
In the second month, bǐngwǔ day,
the Duke and Zhūlóu Yí Fù made a covenant at Cuì.
In the fifth month, bǐngwǔ day,
they, together with the army of Qí, fought at Xī.
On the dīngchǒu day of the sixth month,
Cài Hóu Fēng Rén died.
In autumn, eighth month,
Cài Jì returned from Chén to Cài.
On guǐsì day,
Cài Huán Hóu was buried.
Together with Sòng people and Wèi people attacked Zhūlóu.
2.17.8 In winter
on the first day of the tenth month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In the eighteenth year, in the spring, in the king’s first month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí at Luò.
The Duke’s consort Jiāng-shì thereupon went to Qí.
Why does the text not mention the Duke in connection with his consort?
The consort is considered an outsider.
What does it mean for the consort to be an outsider?
It is an internal term,
but in truth, the consort is external to the Duke.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day bǐngzǐ,
the Duke died in Qí.
On the next day, dīngyǒu,
the funeral procession of the Duke arrived from Qí.
In autumn, the seventh month.
In winter, in the twelfth month, on the day jǐchǒu,
our ruler, Duke Huán, was buried.
As the murderers have not yet been punished, why does the text record the burial?
Because the enemy was outside.
When the enemy is outside, why record the burial?
It is a euphemism, according to the noble man.
In the first year, in the spring, the king’s first month,
why does the text not say ‘the Duke ascended the throne’?
In the *Spring and Autumn Annals*, when a ruler is assassinated, the son is not noted as ‘ascending the throne’.
When the ruler is assassinated, why is the son not said to ascend the throne?
To conceal it.
What is concealed?
It conceals the son.
In the third month,
the consort absconded to Qí.
What is absconding?
Absconding is like fleeing.
When an internal member flees, it is called ‘absconding’.
The consort was already in Qí;
why does the text say she ‘absconded to Qí’?
It refers to concern for the mother.
The first month is for honoring the ruler;
concern for the mother comes after.
Why does the text not refer to the consort as Jiāng-shì?
It is a demotion.
Why is there a demotion?
Because she participated in the assassination of the Duke.
How did she participate?
The consort slandered the Duke to the Marquis of Qí.
The Duke said:
“Tóng is not my son;
he is the son of the Marquis of Qí.”
The Marquis of Qí was enraged;
he drank wine with the Duke.
As the Duke was leaving,
he ordered Lord Péngshēng to see him off.
As the Duke was getting into his carriage,
Péngshēng struck him with the shaft and killed him.
To remember the mother is praiseworthy;
so why is she demoted in the record concerning remembrance of the mother?
Because she did not do so for remembrance of the mother.
In summer,
Shān Bó escorted the Royal Lady.
Who is Shān Bó?
He is the minister among our grandees deputed by the Son of Heaven.
Why is it not recorded as an envoy?
Because he was summoned by the Son of Heaven and sent as such.
What does ‘escort’ mean?
It means he was made to take charge of her on our behalf.
Why did we have to take charge on her behalf?
When the Son of Heaven gives his daughter in marriage to a noble,
he must have a noble of the same surname take charge of her;
when a noble gives a daughter in marriage to a minister,
he must have a minister of the same surname take charge of her.
In autumn,
the residence of the Royal Lady was built outside.
Why is this recorded?
It is a reproach.
What is reproached?
To build it is proper;
to build it outside is not proper.
Why is building outside improper?
To build outside is against ritual propriety.
Why is the act of building it proper?
Because whosoever is to take care of the Royal Lady must have her residence rebuilt.
Why must her residence be rebuilt for her?
She may not reside in the ancestral residence,
a small residence would be suspicious,
and staying among the multitude of princes would be unworthy;
thus the proper way is to have a new building made for her.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day yǐhài,
the Marquis Lín of Chén died.
The king dispatched Róng Shū to grant a mandate to Duke Huán.
What is to grant?
To bestow.
What is the mandate?
To grant us regalia.
Why does it mention Duke Huán?
It is a posthumous mandate.
The Royal Lady went to Qí.
Why is it recorded?
Because we had charge of her.
The Qí army moved the people of Jì, Péng, Zī, and Wú.
What does ‘move’ mean?
To seize.
If it means to seize, why does the text say ‘move’ and not ‘seize’?
To avoid mentioning Duke Xiāng.
When outer states are seized, it is not recorded;
why is it recorded here?
Because it is significant.
Why is it significant?
Because from this, the destruction began.
In the second year, in the spring, in the king’s second month,
the burial of Duke Zhuāng of Chén.
In summer,
Lord Qìng Fù led troops to attack Yúqiū.
What is Yúqiū?
It is a city of Zhūlóu.
Why is it not linked to Zhūlóu?
Because it had become a state of its own.
Why did it become a separate state?
Because the ruler resided there.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the Royal Lady of Qí died.
Usually, an external consort is not recorded as having died;
why is her death recorded here?
Because it was entered in the records.
Why was it entered in the records?
Because we had charge of her.
In winter, the twelfth month,
Consort Jiāng-shì met with the Marquis of Qí at Gào.
On the day yǐyǒu,
Duke Féng of Sòng died.
In the third year, in the spring, in the king’s first month,
Niè met with the army of Qí and attacked Wèi.
Who is Niè?
He is one among our grandees not yet officially appointed.
In summer, the fourth month,
Duke Zhuāng of Sòng was buried.
In the fifth month,
King Huán was buried.
Since there was no prior mention of his death, why is the burial recorded?
It must have been a reburial.
In autumn,
Jì Jì entered Qí with Xī.
Who is Jì Jì?
The younger brother of the Marquis of Jì.
Why is he not named?
Because of his virtue.
What was virtuous in Jì Jì?
He admitted his guilt.
What does it mean to admit guilt?
The Lord of Lǔ said:
“Let me preserve my aunts and elder sisters after the five ancestral temples.”
In winter,
the Duke encamped at Láng.
Why is the encampment at Láng specifically recorded?
It reproaches the desire to save Jì but failing to do so afterwards.
In the fourth year, in the spring, in the king’s second month,
Consort Jiāng-shì entertained the Marquis of Qí at Zhùqiū.
In the third month,
Lady Jībó of Jì died.
In summer,
the Marquis of Qí, the Marquis of Chén, and the Earl of Zhèng met at Chuí.
The Jì Marquis greatly left his state.
What does it mean, "greatly left"?
It means to perish.
Who destroyed it?
Qí destroyed it.
Why does it not say "Qí destroyed it"?
It is because of the taboo for Xiāng Gōng.
The *Chūnqiū* practices taboos for the worthy.
How was Xiāng Gōng worthy?
He avenged a feud.
What feud?
A distant ancestor.
Āi Gōng presented offerings at Zhōu;
the Jì Marquis slandered him.
Given Xiāng Gōng’s actions in this case,
his devotion to serving his ancestors was complete.
What does it mean, “complete”?
Xiāng Gōng intended to avenge the feud against Jì,
so he divined, saying:
“The army will be divided and lost.”
“If I die for it, I do not consider it inauspicious.”
A distant ancestor: how many generations is that?
Nine generations.
Even after nine generations, can a feud still be avenged?
Even after a hundred generations, it can be.
Can it be so in a family?
He said:
“It cannot.”
Why is it allowed for a state?
The ruler of a state is a single body.
The shame of a former ruler
is as if it is the shame of the present ruler;
the shame of the present ruler
is as if it is the shame of the former ruler.
Why is the ruler of a state considered a single body?
Because the ruler takes the state as his very self.
The noble houses are hereditary,
so the ruler of the state is a single body.
Now, Jì committed no crime.
Is this not out of anger?
He replied:
“It is not.”
In ancient times, if there were an enlightened Son of Heaven,
then the Jì Marquis would certainly have been executed,
and there would be no Jì remaining. That the Jì Marquis was not executed, and Jì still exists to this day,
is as if there was no enlightened Son of Heaven.
In ancient times, the nobles certainly had occasions for assemblies and gatherings,
and there was a proper etiquette for audiences and missions.
In their formal titles and expressions, they always invoked their former rulers in mutual address.
In this matter, Qí and Jì have no pretext,
thus they cannot equally exist under Heaven.
Therefore, one who sought to remove the Jì Marquis
could not avoid removing Jì itself.
If there were an enlightened Son of Heaven, would Xiāng Gōng have been able to act thus?
He replied:
“He could not.”
If he could not, why then did Xiāng Gōng do so?
Above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, there was no regional lord;
those who harbored personal bonds or enmities would thus act.
In the sixth month, on yǐchǒu day,
the Qí ruler buried Jì Bó Jī.
When a consort from another state dies, her burial is not recorded;
why is it recorded here?
It is to conceal something.
What does it conceal?
Her state had perished,
so she was only buried in Qí.
This too was revenge for a feud;
why then was she buried?
Destroy what is fit to be destroyed,
and bury what is fit to be buried.
How is it fitting to bury her in this case?
Avenging a feud is not necessarily to kill,
but to drive out.
So, even when encountering the bier of the Jì Marquis,
one would still bury her.
In autumn, the seventh month.
In winter,
the ruler (Gōng) together with the Qí people hunted at Gào.
Why did the ruler hunt together with lesser men?
He was the Qí ruler.
If he was the Qí ruler, why is he merely referred to as "people"?
Because of the taboo and the enmity over the hunt.
Before and after this event there were matters,
so why is it singled out here?
It censures only this one enmity in the hunt.
Therefore, it chooses the most serious case to censure,
and there is nothing more serious than hunting with an enemy.
As for censuring only one case of enmity, why is it?
With an enemy, at no time can there be proper communication.
If they communicate, it is a grave matter for censure,
it cannot be censured enough,
thus only one is chosen for censure,
and all else is treated as of like kind.
In the fifth year, spring, the royal first month.
In summer,
Madam Jiāng went as emissary to Qí’s army.
In autumn,
Ní Lí came to court.
What is Ní?
It is Xiǎo Zhū Lóu.
If it is Xiǎo Zhū Lóu, why is it called Ní?
It was not yet allowed to be known by its official name.
What is Lí Lái?
A name.
What name?
It is a minor state.
In winter,
the ruler assembled with men of Qí, Sòng, Chén, and Cài to attack Wèi.
Why attack Wèi?
To install Shuò.
Why not say "install Wèi ruler Shuò"?
Because he rejected the king.
In the sixth year, spring, the royal third month,
the royal messenger Zǐ Tú came to save Wèi.
Who is the royal messenger?
A man of low rank.
Who is Zǐ Tú?
A noble.
If noble, why is he called merely "man"?
Because he was attached to the messengers.
Why attached to the messengers?
He was merely a royal envoy.
In summer, the sixth month,
the Wèi ruler Shuò entered Wèi.
Why is the Wèi ruler Shuò named so?
Because he was severed.
Why severed?
He violated an order.
What does "entered" signify?
It is a term of usurpation.
In autumn,
the ruler returned from attacking Wèi.
Why sometimes say "assembled",
sometimes "attacked"?
If intentions were achieved, it is called an assembly;
if not, it is called an attack.
The Wèi ruler Shuò entered Wèi,
so why was it called an attack?
It was not permitted to surpass the authority of the Son of Heaven.
Locusts.
In winter,
Qí people came to return Wèi’s treasure.
If it is Wèi's treasure,
why did the Qí people return it?
The Wèi people returned it.
If the Wèi people returned it,
why is it said the Qí people returned it?
It is an act of yielding to us.
What does it mean to yield to us?
The Qí ruler said:
“This was not the power of my small state, but the power of the Lǔ ruler.”
In the seventh year, spring,
Madam Jiāng met with the Qí ruler at Fáng.
In summer, on xīnmǎo day in the fourth month at night,
the constant stars were not visible.
At midnight,
the stars fell like rain.
What are constant stars?
They are the aligned stars.
If the aligned stars were not seen, how did one know it was the middle of the night?
Because the stars were reversed in their courses.
What does it mean "like rain"?
They were not actually rain.
If not rain, why call it "like rain"?
Those who do not rectify the *Chūnqiū* say:
"The stars fell like rain, not reaching a foot from the earth before returning."
The gentleman retouches it, saying:
"The stars fell like rain."
Why is this recorded?
To record the portent.
In autumn, there was a great flood.
There was no wheat sprouting.
If there were no sprouts, why first mention no wheat and then mention no sprouts?
A single disaster is not recorded;
they waited until there was no wheat and then recorded the absence of sprouts.
Why did they record it?
To note the calamity.
In winter,
Fū rén Jiāng Shì met with Qí Hóu at Gǔ.
In the eighth year, in the first lunar month of royal calendar,
the army encamped at Láng,
waiting for the people of Chén and Cài.
When encamping, it does not mention waiting,
why is waiting mentioned here?
It was because they had no choice.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
they offered sacrifices to the troops.
What is it to offer sacrifices to the troops?
When going out, it is called offering sacrifices to the troops;
when returning, it is called zhènlǚ;
the rite is the same;
all are practicing warfare.
Why speak of offering sacrifices to the troops?
It lasted a long time.
Why did it last a long time?
We waited until the day Jiǎwǔ,
and then offered sacrifices to the troops.
In summer,
our army together with the army of Qí laid siege to Chéng,
and Chéng surrendered to the army of Qí.
What is Chéng?
It means flourishing.
If flourishing, why call it Chéng?
To avoid recording the destruction of those of the same clan.
Why not state that they surrendered to our army?
To avoid it.
In autumn,
the army returned.
What is "returned"?
A gentle expression.
Why use a gentle term concerning the destruction of a clan-member?
To express regret.
It is said:
“The army is grieved!”
Why are they grieved?
It is not the fault of the army.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the day Guǐwèi,
Qí Wúzhī assassinated his lord Zhū’ér.
In the ninth year, in spring,
the people of Qí killed Wúzhī.
The Duke and the great officers of Qí formed an alliance at Jì.
Why did the Duke form an alliance with the great officers?
Qí was without a lord.
If so, why not name them?
Because it was avoided to form an alliance with great officers,
making it appear as the common multitude.
In summer,
the Duke campaigned against Qí,
installing Jiū.
What is “install”?
A formal term for bringing in.
Why speak of "campaigning"?
To campaign and then say "install"
is as if they could not install him.
What is Jiū?
It is Gōngzǐ Jiū.
Why not call him Gōngzǐ?
Before a ruler, ministers are named.
Qí Xiǎobái entered Qí.
Why use the clan name?
Because at the time he was head of the state.
Why say “entered”?
It is the language of usurpation.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day Dīngyǒu,
they buried Qí Xiāng Gōng.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
our army and the army of Qí fought at Qiánshí,
our army was defeated.
Normally, a defeat is not mentioned,
why here is defeat stated?
Because it was a punitive defeat.
Why a punitive defeat?
To seek revenge.
If this was revenge against a great state,
why send a lesser man?
The Duke.
If the Duke did so, why is he not named?
Because he did not participate in revenge.
Why did he not participate in revenge?
To seek revenge is the role of those below.
In the ninth month,
the people of Qí seized Zǐ Jiū
and killed him.
Why is “seized” used?
It is the internal expression,
meaning they threatened us and made us kill him.
Why refer to him as Zǐ Jiū?
Because of his noble status.
How was he noble?
He was proper to be a ruler.
In winter,
they deepened the Zhū River.
What is Zhū?
It is a river.
What is it to deepen?
To make it deeper.
Why make it deeper?
To fear Qí.
Why fear Qí?
Because of the killing of Zǐ Jiū.
In the tenth year, in the royal first lunar month,
the Duke defeated the army of Qí at Chángsháo.
In the second month,
the Duke invaded Sòng.
Why is it sometimes called “invade”,
and sometimes “campaign”?
Coarse actions are called “invade”,
refined ones are called “campaign”.
If there is battle, it is not called “campaign”;
if there is siege, it is not called “battle”;
if entering, it is not called “siege”;
if annihilating, it is not called “entering”;
the record preserves what is weightiest.
In the third month,
the people of Sòng relocated Sù.
What is it to relocate?
To cut off communication.
They returned the land thereby.
Zǐ Chénzǐ said:
“To cut off communication: perhaps thereby to force them into vassalage.”
In the sixth month of summer,
the armies of Qí and Sòng encamped at Láng.
The Duke defeated the army of Sòng at Chéngqiū.
Why mention encamping at Láng?
To indicate a campaign.
If it is a campaign, why speak of encamping?
Qí participated in the campaign but not in the battle,
thus “campaign” is stated.
We were able to defeat them,
therefore "encamped" is used.
In the ninth month of autumn,
Jīng defeated the army of Cài at Xīn.
He returned with Cài Hóu Xiànwǔ as captive.
What is Jīng?
It is the name of a region.
A region is less than a state;
a state is less than a clan;
a clan is less than a person;
a person is less than a name;
a name is less than a style name;
a style name is less than "Zǐ".
Why is Cài Hóu Xiànwǔ named?
To cut off.
Why cut him off?
Because he was captured.
Why not just state he was captured?
Because the capture of those from the central states by the yí and dí is not accepted.
In the tenth month of winter,
the army of Qí annihilated Tán.
Tánzǐ fled to Jǔ.
Why not say "left"?
The state was already destroyed;
there was nowhere to leave from.
In the eleventh year, spring, royal first month.
In the fifth month of summer, on the day Wùyín,
the Duke defeated the army of Sòng at Zī.
In autumn,
there was great flooding in Sòng.
Why is it recorded?
To note the disaster.
External disasters are not recorded,
so why is this one?
Because it reached us.
In winter,
the royal Jī married into Qí.
Why is it recorded?
Because it concerned us.
In the twelfth year, in spring, in the king’s third month,
Shū Jī of Jì married into Xī.
Why does it say “married into Xī”?
To conceal it.
Why conceal it thus?
Her state was gone,
she merely followed her uncle.
In summer, in the fourth month.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day jiǎwǔ,
Wàn of Sòng murdered his lord Jiē,
as did Dàifū Qiú Mù.
What does “as did” mean?
It means complicity.
There have been many regicides,
but aside from these, are there none complicit?
Kǒng Fù and Xún Xī were both complicit.
Aside from Kǒng Fù and Xún Xī, are there none complicit?
It is said: there are.
Then why is this one recorded?
Because of worthiness.
What makes Qiú Mù worthy?
Qiú Mù can be said to have not feared the strong or the intimidating.
How was it that he did not fear the strong and intimidating?
Wàn once fought against Lord Zhuāng,
and was captured by Lord Zhuāng.
After Lord Zhuāng returned,
he held him imprisoned in the palace,
and after several months
then released and let him return to be a great officer in Sòng.
He played a dice game with Lord Mǐn,
while women sat all around.
Wàn said:
“How great
is the virtue
and beauty of the Lord of Lǔ!
Of all the lords under Heaven who are suited to rule,
only the Lord of Lǔ!”
Lord Mǐn admired these women,
and envied his words.
He turned and said:
“This is a captive!
How as a captive,
could the Lord of Lǔ’s beauty reach such a degree?”
Wàn became angry,
struck Lord Mǐn,
and broke his neck.
Qiú Mù, hearing the lord had been murdered,
hurried there,
and met him at the gate.
With sword in hand, he shouted at him.
Wàn swung his arm at Qiú Mù,
shattering his skull,
and his teeth stuck in the door.
Qiú Mù can be said not to have feared the strong and intimidating.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Wàn of Sòng fled to Chén.
In the thirteenth year, in spring,
the Lord of Qí, people of Sòng, people of Chén, people of Cài, and people of Zhūlóu gathered at Běi Xìng.
In summer, in the sixth month,
the people of Qí destroyed Suì.
In autumn, in the seventh month.
In winter,
the duke met with the Lord of Qí,
and swore an alliance at Kē.
Why is the day not given?
Because it was easy.
How was it easy?
The covenant of Huán gave no date;
the assembly had no invitations,
because of trust.
Why did omitting the date begin here?
Lord Zhuāng was to meet with Huán,
Zǐ of Cáo stepped forward and said:
“How is your lordship disposed?”
Lord Zhuāng said:
“To live is less than to die.”
Zǐ of Cáo said:
“If so, then you will do as a lord, I as a subject.”
Lord Zhuāng said:
“Agreed.”
Thus they met with Huán.
Lord Zhuāng ascended the platform,
and Zǐ of Cáo followed with sword in hand.
Guǎn Zǐ stepped forward and said:
“What does your lord seek?”
Zǐ of Cáo said:
“The walls collapse upon our borders;
will our lord give no thought to this?”
Guǎn Zǐ said:
“Then what does your lord seek?”
Zǐ of Cáo said:
“I wish to request the fields at Wèn Yáng.”
Guǎn Zǐ turned and said:
“The lord has agreed.”
Lord Huán said:
“Agreed.”
Zǐ of Cáo requested an oath,
and Lord Huán came down to swear it.
After the oath,
Zǐ of Cáo struck with his sword and left.
A compelled covenant could be violated,
yet Lord Huán did not deceive.
Zǐ of Cáo could have been hated,
yet Lord Huán bore no grudge,
and the trust of Lord Huán became renowned through All Under Heaven,
beginning from the covenant at Kē.
In the fourteenth year, in spring,
the people of Qí, Chén, and Cáo attacked Sòng.
In summer,
Shàn Bó joined an expedition against Sòng.
Why does it say “joined in the expedition against Sòng”?
Because he came later.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Jīng entered Cài.
In winter,
Shàn Bó met with the Lord of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Lord of Wèi, and the Earl of Zhèng at Juàn.
In the fifteenth year, in spring,
the Lord of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Lord of Chén, the Lord of Wèi, and the Earl of Zhèng gathered at Juàn.
In summer,
the lady Jiāng Shì visited Qí.
In autumn,
the people of Sòng, Qí, and Zhūlóu attacked Ér.
The people of Zhèng raided Sòng.
In winter, in the tenth month.
In the sixteenth year, in spring, in the king’s first month.
In summer,
the people of Sòng, Qí, and Wèi attacked Zhèng.
In autumn,
Jīng attacked Zhèng.
In winter, in the twelfth month,
the duke met with the Lord of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Lord of Chén, the Lord of Wèi, the Earl of Zhèng, the Man of Xǔ, the Earl of Cáo, the Earl of Huá, the Master of Téng,
and swore a joint covenant at Yōu.
What is a “joint covenant”?
It is having the same desire.
The Lord Kè of Zhūlóu died.
In the seventeenth year, in spring,
the people of Qí seized Zhèng Zhān.
Who is Zhèng Zhān?
A lowly person of Zhèng.
This lowly person of Zhèng,
why mention the people of Qí seized him?
The record is very obsequious.
In summer,
the people of Qí carried out massacre in Suì.
What is “massacre”?
It means mass killing,
the killing of all the guards.
In autumn,
Zhèng Zhān fled from Qí and arrived.
Why is this recorded?
It is written because he was exceedingly sycophantic.
It is said:
“A sycophant has come,
a sycophant has come.”
In winter,
there were many elk.
Why is this recorded?
To note the unusual.
In the eighteenth year, in spring, in the third month of the king,
there was a solar eclipse.
In summer,
the Duke pursued the Róng west of the Jì River.
As there was not yet any campaign,
why say “pursued”?
It is to magnify that it was in the Central States that the pursuit occurred.
As there was not yet any campaign against the Central States,
why then mention a pursuit for the Central States?
It is to magnify that, before the enemy arrived, they prepared in advance to resist.
Why say “west of the Jì River”?
To magnify it.
In autumn,
there was a yù.
Why is this recorded?
To note the unusual.
In winter, the tenth month.
In the nineteenth year, in spring, in the first month of the king.
In summer, the fourth month.
In autumn,
Duke’s son Jié escorted a wife from Chén to marry in Juàn,
and thereafter made a covenant with the Marquis of Qí and the Duke of Sòng.
What is “yìng” (escort during marriage)?
When a lord marries a woman from one state,
two other states send escorts,
accompanied by a niece and a younger sister.
What is a niece?
She is the daughter of an elder brother.
What is a younger sister?
A woman’s younger sister.
A lord marries nine women with a single proposal;
a lord does not marry again.
The escorts are not usually recorded;
why then is it recorded here?
Because there was a subsequent event.
For high officials, there is no “subsequent event”;
here, why say “subsequently”?
For marriage rites,
a high official accepts the order but not the words,
and if upon leaving the borders there is something that will stabilize the altar of state and benefit the country,
he may act on his own accord.
Lady Jiāng went to Jǔ.
In winter,
people of Qí, Sòng, and Chén attacked our western border.
In the twentieth year, in spring, in the second month of the king,
Lady Jiāng went to Jǔ.
In summer,
Qí experienced a great disaster.
What is a great disaster?
A great famine.
What is a great famine?
Disease.
Why is this recorded?
To record the disaster.
External disasters are not recorded;
why then is it recorded here?
Because it reached us.
In autumn, the seventh month.
In winter,
the people of Qí attacked the Róng.
In the twenty-first year, in spring, in the first month of the king.
In summer, on the day xīnyǒu of the fifth month,
Duke Tú of Zhèng died.
In autumn, on the day wùxū of the seventh month,
Lady Jiāng passed away.
In winter, the twelfth month,
the late Duke Lì of Zhèng was buried.
In the twenty-second year, in spring, in the first month of the king,
there was a great collapse in Sì.
What is Sì?
A landslip.
What is a great collapse?
A calamity of collapse.
Why is the great collapse in Sì recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
Criticizing the start of resenting collapse.
On the day guǐchǒu,
our minor queen Wén Jiāng was buried.
Who is Wén Jiāng?
She was the mother of Duke Zhuāng.
The people of Chén killed their prince Yǔ Kòu.
In summer, the fifth month.
In autumn, on the day bǐngshēn of the seventh month,
a covenant was made at Fáng with Qí noble Gāo Xī.
Who is Qí noble Gāo Xī?
A grandee.
Why covenant with such a minor figure?
Because he is a ruler.
If he is a ruler, why not call him a ruler?
It is because his being in mourning and covenanting with a grandee is taboo.
In winter,
the Duke went to Qí to present betrothal gifts.
The presentation of betrothal gifts is not usually recorded;
why then is it recorded here?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
Personally presenting the betrothal gifts is not proper ritual.
In the twenty-third year, in spring,
the Duke returned from Qí.
For the covenant at Huán, there is no date;
as for this meeting, the full proceedings are not set forth;
it was trusted.
Why are the proceedings in this Huán state made explicit?
Because there was danger.
What danger?
The Duke was alone in Chéntuó.
Jì Shū came to make a proposal of marriage.
In summer,
the Duke went to Qí to observe the altar.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
For a lord to cross borders and observe the altar is not proper ritual.
The Duke returned from Qí.
Jīng sent envoys to make a marriage proposal.
Why is Jīng referred to as “people”?
It was the first time they were able to make a formal visit.
The Duke met the Marquis of Qí at Gǔ.
Shāo Shū presented himself before the Duke.
Why say “presented himself before the Duke”?
Because the Duke was outside the state.
In autumn,
the beams of the Huán Palace were painted red.
Why is this recorded?
To criticize.
What is criticized?
Painting the beams of the Huán Palace red is not proper ritual.
In winter, the eleventh month,
the Earl of Cáo, Shè Gū, died.
In the twelfth month, on the day jiǎyín,
the Duke made a covenant with the Marquis of Qí at Hù.
For the covenant at Huán, there is no date;
why then is it dated here?
Because there was danger.
What danger?
We were double-minded.
Zǐ of Lǔ said:
“That we were double-minded,
it was not their doing,
but ours.”
In the twenty-fourth year, in spring, the king’s third month,
they carved the pillars of Huán Palace.
Why is this recorded?
It is a reproof.
What is the reproof?
To carve the pillars of Huán Palace was not in accordance with ritual.
They buried Cáo Zhuāng Gōng.
In summer,
the Duke went to Qí to welcome his bride.
Why is this recorded?
Because the proper formality of personally welcoming the bride was observed, which accords with ritual.
In autumn,
the Duke returned from Qí.
On the wùchén day of the eighth month,
the consort Jiāng Shì entered.
Why is her entry specifically mentioned?
It is problematic.
Why is the day mentioned?
It is problematic.
In what way is it problematic?
The consort could not be made to enter without acquiescence,
for she had some agreement with the Duke,
and only then did she enter.
On the wùyín day,
the nobles and clan women met her,
presenting gifts of silk.
Who are the clan women?
The wives of the nobles.
What does “met” mean?
It means to meet.
What is meant by “presenting gifts”?
Presenting such gifts was not proper.
To see her and present gifts is not according to ritual.
Then what should have been presented?
Jujube and chestnuts,
or perhaps strips of dried meat.
There was a great flood.
In winter,
the Róng attacked Cáo.
Cáo Jī fled to Chén.
Who is Cáo Jī?
A noble of Cáo.
As Cáo had no more nobles,
why is this recorded?
Because he was worthy.
What was worthy about Cáo Jī?
When the Róng were about to attack Cáo,
Cáo Jī remonstrated, saying:
“The Róng are numerous but unrighteous;
My lord, I beg you not to resist them personally.”
The Earl of Cáo replied:
“That cannot be.”
He admonished three times but was not heeded,
so he departed,
thus the gentlemen considered that he understood the proper relation between ruler and minister.
Chì returned to Cáo Guō Gōng.
Who is Chì?
There was no Chì in Cáo;
it was Guō Gōng.
Who is Guō Gōng?
He was a lord who had lost his land.
In the twenty-fifth year, in spring,
the Marquis of Chén sent Nǚ Shū to make an engagement.
In summer, on the guǐchǒu day of the fifth month,
the Marquis of Wèi, Shuò, died.
On the xīnwèi day, the first of the sixth month,
there was a solar eclipse,
and offerings were made at the altar with sacrificial animals.
Why were animals sacrificed at the altar when there was a solar eclipse?
To appease the forces of yīn,
they circled the altar with vermillion silk.
Some say it was to threaten,
others say it was to avert darkness,
fearing that people might disturb it,
so they encircled it.
Lady Bó Jī married into Qǐ.
In autumn,
there was a great flood,
sacrificial animals were offered at the altar at the gate.
Why is it said “at the altar at the gate”?
At the altar, it followed ritual,
but at the gate, it was not proper.
In winter,
Duke’s son Yǒu went to Chén.
In the twenty-sixth year,
the Duke attacked the Róng.
In summer,
the Duke returned from campaigning against the Róng.
Cáo killed their noble.
Why is he not named?
Because they were many.
Why did many kill him?
Because he did not die for the ruler of Cáo.
If a ruler dies at his post, it is called extinction,
so why is it not called extinction?
It is out of respect for Cáo Jī.
This was probably in battle,
so why is it not recorded as a battle?
Also out of respect for Cáo Jī.
In autumn,
the Duke, together with the people of Sòng and Qí, attacked Xū.
In winter, on the guǐhài day, the first of the twelfth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the twenty-seventh year, in spring,
the Duke conferred with Qǐ Bó Jī at Táo.
In summer, in the sixth month,
the Duke conferred with the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Chén, and Earl of Zhèng,
and made a covenant of alliance at Yōu.
In autumn,
Duke’s son Yǒu went to Chén,
and they buried Yuán Zhòng.
Who is Yuán Zhòng?
A noble of Chén.
The burial of a noble is not usually recorded;
why is this one recorded?
Because it relates to Jìzǐ’s private matters.
How is it related to Jìzǐ’s private matters?
In order to avoid internal trouble.
A gentleman avoids internal trouble but not external dangers.
What is internal trouble?
Gōngzǐ Qìngfù, Gōngzǐ Yá, and Gōngzǐ Yǒu were all younger brothers of Zhuāng Gōng’s mother.
Gōngzǐ Qìngfù and Gōngzǐ Yá were in league with the consort to threaten the Duke;
Jìzǐ rose up to handle it,
so he could not participate in the government of the state.
If he just sat and watched, it was partiality toward kin.
Unable to endure seeing this,
therefore, he requested once again to go to Chén and thus attended the burial of Yuán Zhòng.
In winter,
Qǐ Bó Jī arrived.
Why does it say “arrived”?
When one simply comes, it is called “arrived”;
if one comes home for good, it is called “returned home.”
Jǔ Qìng came to escort Shū Jī.
Who is Jǔ Qìng?
A noble of Jǔ.
There were no nobles in Jǔ;
why is this recorded?
It is a reproof.
What is the reproof?
A noble crossed borders to fetch a lady,
which is not in accordance with ritual.
Qǐ Bó came to court.
The Duke met the Marquis of Qí at Chéngpú.
In the twenty-eighth year, in spring, in the king’s third month, on jiǎyín day,
Qí people attacked Wèi.
The people of Wèi fought the people of Qí;
the people of Wèi were defeated.
The campaign was not dated;
why, then, is there a date?
It is the day they arrived.
Battles are not described as campaigns;
why, then, does it say “campaign”?
It is the day they arrived.
In the *Chūnqiū*, those who campaign are considered guests,
and those who campaign are considered hosts;
therefore, Wèi was made the host.
Why was Wèi made the host?
Because Wèi had not yet committed a crime.
The defeated are named as “army”;
why, then, is Wèi not called “army”?
Because they had not yet obtained the title of “army”.
In summer, in the fourth month, on dīngwèi day,
Zhūlóu Zǐ Suǒ died.
In autumn,
Jīng attacked Zhèng.
The Duke allied with Qí people, Sòng people, and the people of Zhūlóu to rescue Zhèng.
In winter,
they built fortifications at Wēi.
There was no wheat or grain at all.
Since, in winter, it was already known that there was no wheat or grain,
why mention building Wēi first and only then say there was no wheat or grain?
It is because they wished to avoid directly recording that in a famine year, they built a town.
Zāng Sūn Chén requested to purchase grain from Qí.
What does “request to purchase grain” mean?
It is to request to buy grain.
Why is it not called an “embassy”?
Because it was regarded as being a private action of Zāng Sūn Chén.
Why make it a private action of Zāng Sūn Chén?
When a gentleman governs a state,
