he must have provisions for three years.
If there is one bad harvest,
he requests to buy grain—
this is a criticism.
In the twenty-ninth year, in spring,
the stables at Yán were renewed.
What does it mean to renew the stalls at Yán?
It means to repair the old ones.
Repairing the old is not normally recorded;
why is it recorded here?
It is a criticism.
A criticism of what?
That they made repairs in a year of disaster.
In summer,
the people of Zhèng invaded Xǔ.
In autumn,
there were locusts.
Why is this recorded?
To record an unusual event.
In winter, in the twelfth month,
Jì Shū Jī died.
A wall was built at Zhū and Fáng.
In the thirtieth year, in spring, in the king’s first month.
In summer,
the army camped at Chéng.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
the people of Qí seized Zhāng.
What is Zhāng?
It is a leftover town of Jǐ.
What does “seized it” mean?
It means they took it.
If they took it, why does it not say “took it”?
Out of consideration for Duke Huán.
Taking outer towns is not usually recorded;
why is this recorded?
Because it was the end of Jǐ.
In the eighth month, on guǐhài day,
Jì Shū Jī was buried.
The burial of outer noblewomen is not recorded;
why is this recorded?
It is to hide it.
Why is it hidden?
Because her state had perished,
she was only temporarily buried with her uncles.
In the ninth month, on gēngwǔ—the first day—
there was an eclipse of the sun.
At the altars, a sacrificial animal was used in the drums.
In winter,
the Duke and the Marquis of Qí met at Lǔ Jì.
The people of Qí attacked Shānróng.
This was the Marquis of Qí,
so why refer to “people”?
As a reproach.
Why the reproach?
Zǐ Sīmǎzǐ said,
“He must have forced the issue for himself.”
This was in fact a battle,
so why not mention the battle?
In the *Chūnqiū*, “battle” is used only for equals;
with Duke Huán fighting the Róng and Dí,
he only drove them away.
In the thirty-first year, in spring,
a terrace was built at Láng.
Why is this recorded?
It is a criticism.
A criticism of what?
It overlooked the place where the people wash and rinse.
In summer, in the fourth month,
the Earl of Xuē died.
A terrace was built at Xuē.
Why is this recorded?
It is a criticism.
A criticism of what?
That it was distant.
In the sixth month,
the Marquis of Qí came to present the spoils taken from the Róng.
Qí is a great power;
why come personally to present the Róng spoils?
To threaten us.
How did he threaten us?
By carrying the captured banners past us.
In autumn,
a terrace was built at Qín.
Why is this recorded?
It is a criticism.
A criticism of what?
That it faced another state.
In winter,
there was no rain.
Why is this recorded?
To record an unusual event.
In the thirty-second year, in spring,
a wall was built at Xiǎogǔ.
In summer,
the Duke of Sòng and the Marquis of Qí met at Liángqiū.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on guǐsì day,
Gōngzǐ Yá died.
Why is he not called “younger brother”?
Because he was killed.
If he was killed, why does it not say he was assassinated?
To conceal the killing for Jìzǐ’s sake.
Why conceal the killing for Jìzǐ’s sake?
Because Jìzǐ suppressed evil
not with the state’s courts,
but by following his own heart and thus concealed it.
How did Jìzǐ suppress evil?
Duke Zhuāng was ill,
about to die,
and summoned Jìzǐ because of his illness.
Jìzǐ arrived, and the duke entrusted him with the affairs of state,
saying:
“If I do not recover from this illness,
what will happen to the State of Lǔ?”
Jìzǐ replied:
“As long as Pān is present, why should you worry?”
The duke said:
“How can it be so?
Yá said to me:
‘Once in a generation in Lǔ,
and you already know this.
As long as Qìngfù lives.’”
Jìzǐ said:
“How would I dare?
Is this to bring chaos?
How would I dare?”
Soon after, Yá murdered Xièchéng.
Jìzǐ prepared medicine and gave it to him,
saying:
“If you obey my words and drink this,
you will certainly avoid disgrace before the world,
and will certainly have descendants in the State of Lǔ.
If you do not obey my words and do not drink this,
you will certainly be shamed before all under heaven,
and certainly will have no descendants in the State of Lǔ.”
So he obeyed his words and drank it;
after drinking, he went to Wúlěi’s house,
reached Wángdī and died.
Now Gōngzǐ Yá will also be so.
Why should his record be placed together with one who murders kin?
When a prince is about to kill his kin,
but does so only after being ordered, then execute him.
Is this then good?
The answer: Yes.
To record one who kills the heir apparent’s own younger brother directly as “prince”
is to strongly blame him.
Jìzǐ killed his mother’s elder son (his brother);
how can this be called good?
Execution that does not spare a brother
is the obligation of lord and minister.
If so, then why not simply execute him directly,
instead of poisoning him?
By punishing one’s brother through secret means and letting it appear as illness,
hiding and evading it,
so as to make it seem like dying of illness,
this is the way of affection for kin.
In the eighth month, on guǐhài day,
the duke passed away in the residence hall.
What is the residence hall?
It is the main sleeping chamber.
In winter, in the tenth month, on yǐwèi day,
Zǐ Pān died.
If a son dies, it is said, “the son died.”
Why in this case is it recorded as “Zǐ Pān died”?
If the ruler is alive, he is called “the heir apparent.”
If the ruler has died, he is called “Zǐ so-and-so.”
After burial, he is called “Zǐ.”
After a year has passed, he is called “duke.”
When Zǐ Pān died,
why was his burial not recorded?
He had not yet reigned more than a year as ruler.
If there is a son, a temple is established;
if there is a temple, burial is recorded.
If there is no son, there is no temple;
if there is no temple, burial is not recorded.
Gōngzǐ Qìngfù went to Qí.
The Dí attacked Xíng.
The first year, spring, in the king’s first month.
Why does it not say “ascended the throne”?
After succession by the killer of the ruler, it is not said “ascended the throne.”
Who succeeded?
He succeeded Zǐ Pān.
Who killed Zǐ Pān?
Qìngfù did.
He killed Gōngzǐ Yá;
soon after,
Jìzǐ did not escape.
Qìngfù killed the ruler;
why was he not executed?
Though there was intent, he was not apprehended.
He suppressed evil,
and then it was out of reach;
the blame was shifted in the legal case,
without investigating the facts and then executing him;
this is the way of affection for kin.
To whom was the case shifted?
The blame was shifted to the servant Dèng Hùyuè.
Why was the case shifted to the servant Dèng Hùyuè?
When Duke Zhuāng was alive,
Hùyuè had committed fornication in the palace;
Zǐ Pān had him arrested and flogged.
After Zhuāng Gōng died,
Qìngfù said to Hùyuè:
“Pān disgraced you,
everyone in the state knows it.
Why not assassinate him?”
He had Hùyuè assassinate Zǐ Pān,
and then executed Dèng Hùyuè and shifted the case to him.
When Jìzǐ arrived, he did not change this.
The people of Qí came to the rescue of Xíng.
In summer, in the sixth month, on xīnyǒu day, our ruler Duke Zhuāng was buried.
In autumn, in the eighth month,
the duke made a covenant with the Marquis of Qí at Luògū.
Jìzǐ returned home.
Why is he called Jìzǐ?
Because he was virtuous.
Why does it say “returned home”?
Because he was welcomed with joy.
In winter,
Zhòngsūn of Qí arrived.
Who is Zhòngsūn of Qí?
He is Gōngzǐ Qìngfù.
Gōngzǐ Qìngfù—why is he called Zhòngsūn of Qí?
Because he was associated with Qí.
Why associated with Qí?
To treat him as an outsider.
Why treat him as an outsider?
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* avoids naming those it venerates,
avoids naming those who are kin,
avoids naming those who are virtuous;
Zǐ Zǐ said:
“With the *Spring and Autumn Annals* as the *Spring and Autumn Annals*,
if there is no Zhòngsūn in Qí,
could it mean our Zhòngsūn?”
In the second year, spring, in the king’s first month,
the people of Qí moved Yáng.
In summer, in the fifth month, on yǐyǒu day,
there was an auspicious ancestral sacrifice to Duke Zhuāng.
Why is it said “auspicious”?
To say it is “auspicious”
is to say it was not yet truly auspicious.
Why was it not yet auspicious?
Because three years of mourning had not yet passed.
When three years have passed—
so why is it said three years have not passed?
The mourning of three years
is actually only twenty-five months.
Why is it said “to Duke Zhuāng”?
It was not yet proper to name the temple.
Why was it not yet proper to name the temple?
Because it was during the three years of mourning.
Why is “auspicious ancestral sacrifice to Duke Zhuāng” recorded?
To criticize.
Why criticize thus?
To criticize that in the beginning, mourning was not kept for three years.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on xīnchǒu day,
the duke died.
Why is the duke’s death not recorded with the place name?
To conceal it.
Why conceal it this way?
Because it was assassination.
Who assassinated him?
Qìngfù.
He killed Gōngzǐ Yá;
soon after,
Jìzǐ did not escape.
Qìngfù killed two rulers—why was he not executed?
Though the intent was there, he was not apprehended, suppressing evil.
By then it was out of reach;
they were slow to pursue the fugitive criminal;
this is the way of affection for kin.
In the ninth month,
the Lady Jiāng gave birth to a grandson in Zhūlóu.
Gōngzǐ Qìngfù fled to Jǔ.
In winter,
Gāo Zǐ of Qí came to form an alliance.
Who is Gāo Zǐ?
He is a great officer of Qí.
Why is it not said that he was an envoy?
Because we were without a ruler.
Then why was his personal name not used?
Because of joy for him.
Why joy?
He rectified our state.
How did he rectify our state?
After Zhuāng Gōng died,
Zǐ Bān committed regicide,
Mǐn Gōng was murdered,
and after these three rulers died,
for several years there was no ruler.
Suppose Qí had seized Lǔ,
they did not even raise troops;
all they did was speak words, nothing more.
Huán Gōng sent Gāo Zǐ with the soldiers of Nányáng
to establish Xī Gōng and build walls for Lǔ.
Some say that this was from Lù Mén to Zhēng Mén;
others say it was from Zhēng Mén to Lì Mén.
The people of Lǔ to this day consider it an admirable story,
saying:
“We still look forward to Gāo Zǐ.”
In the twelfth month,
the Dí entered Wèi.
Zhèng abandoned its army.
Why did Zhèng abandon its army?
Because they despised their general.
The Duke of Zhèng disliked Gāo Kè,
made him general,
drove him out and would not admit him,
thus abandoning the army.
First year, in spring, King’s first month,
Why does the Duke not state he ascended the throne?
For having succeeded a ruler who was murdered,
the heir does not state he ascends the throne.
Is he then not the heir?
Then why call him “heir”?
It is the consistent usage for all ministers and sons.
The army of Qí, army of Sòng, army of Cáo assembled north of Niè
to rescue Xíng.
In a rescue, “assembling” is not usually stated;
why is “assembling” mentioned here?
Because it was not in time for the event.
What does “not in time for the event” mean?
Xíng was already destroyed.
Who destroyed it?
It was the Dí who wiped it out.
Why is it not said that the Dí destroyed it?
To avoid mentioning it because of Huán Gōng.
Why avoid it for Huán Gōng?
Because above there was no Son of Heaven,
below, no regional lord;
under Heaven, there were states mutually destroying each other,
and Huán Gōng could not rescue them;
thus Huán Gōng felt ashamed.
Why mention “assembling” before “rescue”?
Because he was the ruler.
If ruler, then why use “army”?
Because he did not exclusively grant fiefs, as the feudal lords did.
Why not?
In fact, he did,
but the records do not show it.
Why do the records not show it?
Because it is against the duty of feudal lords to grant fiefs by themselves.
If feudal lords ought not grant fiefs personally,
then why say “in fact, he did”?
Because above there was no Son of Heaven,
below, no regional lord;
under Heaven, when states destroy each other,
if someone’s power is sufficient to help,
then helping is allowed.
In summer, the sixth month,
Xíng moved to Chén Yí.
What does “moved” mean?
It indicates their intention.
Who made them move?
It was not their own intention.
The army of Qí, Sòng, and Cáo fortified Xíng.
This was one matter;
then why does it again mention the armies of Qí, Sòng, and Cáo?
If it did not mention them again,
it could not be known it was a single matter.
In autumn, seventh month, on Wùchén day,
the Lady Jiāng died at Yí,
and the people of Qí sent her back.
What is Yí?
It is land of Qí.
If it is land of Qí, why say “the people of Qí sent her back”?
The lady died at Yí,
so the people of Qí sent her back.
If the lady died at Yí,
why did the people of Qí send her back?
Because Huán Gōng summoned and strangled her.
The people of Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
In the eighth month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Earl of Zhèng, the Earl of Cáo, and people of Zhūlóu at Zhēng.
In the ninth month,
the Duke defeated the army of Zhūlóu at Yīng.
In winter, tenth month, on Rénwǔ day,
Duke’s son Yǒu led troops and defeated the army of Jǔ at Lí,
and captured Jǔ Rú.
Who is Jǔ Rú?
A great officer of Jǔ.
If Jǔ had no great officers,
then why is this recorded?
Because it was Dà Jìzǐ who captured him.
Why is it significant that Dà Jìzǐ captured him?
Jìzǐ rectified internal troubles,
and properly repelled external difficulties.
How did he properly repel external difficulties?
The duke’s son Qìngfù murdered Mǐn Gōng,
fled to Jǔ,
the people of Jǔ expelled him,
he planned to go to Qí,
but the people of Qí would not admit him,
so he turned back and stopped above the Wènshuǐ;
he sent the duke’s son Xīsī to request entry.
Jìzǐ said:
“The duke’s son cannot enter;
if he enters, he will be killed.”
Xīsī could not bear to report this to Qìngfù,
and from the southern bank,
facing north, he wept.
Qìngfù heard it and said:
“Alas!
That is Xīsī’s voice.
All right then.”
He said:
“I cannot enter after all.”
So he hanged himself in the chariot and died.
The people of Jǔ heard, and said:
“We have seized the culprit of your state;
let us use him as ransom with Lǔ.”
The people of Lǔ did not yield,
so Jǔ raised troops and attacked Lǔ;
Jìzǐ faced them with a partial force and fought.
In the twelfth month, on Dīngsì day,
the mourning party of the Lady’s family arrived from Qí.
Why is the lady not called Jiāng?
It is a demotion.
Why the demotion?
Because of involvement in regicide.
Then why was she not demoted at the time of the regicide?
A demotion must be for the more serious matter;
nothing is more serious than her funeral cortège arriving.
In the second year, in the spring, during the royal first month,
a city was built at Chǔqiū.
Who built the city?
It was the city of Wèi.
Why is it not stated as "the city of Wèi"?
It was destroyed.
Who destroyed it?
The Dí destroyed it.
Why is it not stated that the Dí destroyed it?
It was to preserve the honor of Huán Gōng.
Why preserve the honor of Huán Gōng?
Above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, there was no Regional Lord;
among the rulers of all under Heaven, some perished through one another,
and Huán Gōng could not save them;
thus Huán Gōng was ashamed of this.
Then who rebuilt the city?
Huán Gōng rebuilt it.
Why is it not stated that Huán Gōng rebuilt it?
Because he did not have the exclusive right to enfeoff lands among the feudal lords.
Why not?
In reality he did, but in wording he did not.
Why is it not put so in wording?
By the principle of the feudal lords, one may not enfeoff lands exclusively;
by the principle of the feudal lords, one may not enfeoff lands exclusively;
then why say in reality he did so?
Above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, there was no Regional Lord;
among the feudal lords all under Heaven, when some perished through one another,
if there was strength enough to save,
then it was permissible to save them.
In the fifth month of summer, on xīnsì day,
our consort Āi Jiāng was buried.
Who was Āi Jiāng?
She was the wife of Zhuāng Gōng.
The army of Yú and the army of Jìn destroyed Xiàyáng.
Yú was a small state;
why is it listed above a great state?
Because Yú was the chief perpetrator.
Why was Yú the chief perpetrator?
Yú accepted bribes,
allowed the state-destroying army through its territory,
and thus brought about its own ruin.
How did it accept bribes?
Duke Xiàn gathered his ministers and asked them,
saying:
"Recently, I have lain awake at night, unable to sleep;
what does this mean?"
There was a minister who responded,
saying:
"Perhaps Your Grace's bed is uneasy?
Or perhaps one of the attendants is not at your side?"
Duke Xiàn did not answer.
Xún Xī then advanced, saying:
"Is it about Yú and Guō?"
Duke Xiàn bowed and invited him forward,
and together they withdrew to discuss, saying:
"I wish to attack Guō,
but Yú would come to its aid;
if I attack Yú, then Guō would aid them;
what should be done?
I hope you will consider this with me."
Xún Xī replied:
"If Your Grace accepts my plan,
then take Guō today,
and take Yú tomorrow,
what is there for Your Grace to worry about?"
Duke Xiàn said:
"But how can this be done?"
Xún Xī said:
"Send the chariots of Qūchǎn,
and the white jade from Chuíjí,
and you will surely obtain it.
As for the treasures, remove them from the inner storehouse,
and put them in the outer treasury;
as for the horses, remove them from the inner stables
and tether them in the outer stables;
what loss is there for Your Grace?"
Duke Xiàn said:
"Very well.
Even so,
Gōngzhī Qí remains there,
what should be done?"
Xún Xī said:
"Gōngzhī Qí knows, indeed he knows.
Even so,
Duke Yú is greedy and fond of treasures;
when he sees treasures,
he will surely not follow his advice;
let me go through with it."
So Xún Xī proceeded,
and when Duke Yú saw the treasures,
he assented.
Gōngzhī Qí did indeed remonstrate, saying:
"The Classic says,
'If the lips are gone, the teeth grow cold.'
The mutual aid between Yú and Guō
is not out of favor for each other;
so if Jìn takes Guō today,
tomorrow Yú will likewise perish.
Your Grace, please do not consent."
Duke Yú did not follow his advice,
lent the way and thus Guō was taken;
four years later,
Jìn in turn took Yú.
Duke Yú arrived clinging to his treasures and leading his horse.
Xún Xī saw him and said:
"How about my plan?"
Duke Xiàn said:
"Your plan has already been carried out;
as for the treasure, it is now mine;
even so,
my horses' teeth have grown longer too."
This was said in jest.
What was Xiàyáng?
It was a town of Guō.
Why is it not appended as belonging to Guō?
Because it became a state.
Why did it become a state?
Because the ruler lived there, that's all.
In the ninth month of autumn,
the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, people of Jiāng, and people of Huáng swore alliance at Guànzé.
Who were the people of Jiāng and Huáng?
They are called "distant states."
Distant states have already arrived;
so why mention only Qí and Sòng of the central states?
For great states, Qí and Sòng were mentioned;
for distant states, Jiāng and Huáng were mentioned;
by this, it is implied that none dared not arrive.
In the tenth month of winter,
there was no rain.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
Chǔ people invaded Zhèng.
In the third year, in the royal first month of spring,
there was no rain.
In the fourth month of summer,
there was no rain.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
People of Xú took Shū.
Why does it say "took it"?
Because it was easy.
In the sixth month,
it rained.
Why does it say "rain in the sixth month"?
Because rain came late and was not abundant.
In autumn,
the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, people of Jiāng, and people of Huáng met at Yánggǔ.
This was a grand assembly;
why is it only briefly mentioned?
Huán Gōng said:
"Do not block the valleys,
do not store up grain,
do not sell saplings,
do not take concubines as wives."
In winter,
Prince Yǒu went as an emissary to Qí to oversee the alliance.
What does it mean to "oversee the alliance"?
It means to go and participate in the alliance there.
Why does it sometimes say "come to the alliance"?
It means they come to hold the alliance with us.
Chǔ people attacked Zhèng.
In the fourth year, in the royal first month of spring,
the Duke met the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Chén, Marquis of Wèi, Earl of Zhèng, Viscount of Xǔ, and Earl of Cáo to invade Cài.
Cài collapsed.
What does "collapsed" mean?
It means the lower betrayed the upper.
For states it's called "collapse";
for towns, it's called "rebellion."
They then attacked Chǔ,
and encamped at Xíng.
Why does it say they encamped at Xíng?
Because they were waiting.
Whom were they waiting for?
For Qū Wán.
In summer,
the Xǔ noble, Xǔ Nán Xīn Chén, died.
Qǔ Wán of Chǔ came to make an alliance at Shī,
and they swore an oath at Zhàolíng.
Who is Qǔ Wán?
He is a great officer of Chǔ.
Why is his visit not named as a mission?
To honor Qǔ Wán.
Why honor Qǔ Wán?
Because he stood in place of Huán Gōng.
Why does it say “swore an oath at Shī” and “swore an oath at Zhàolíng”?
Because the troops were at Zhàolíng.
Since the troops were at Zhàolíng,
why then is the oath mentioned twice?
To show satisfaction in Chǔ’s submission.
What does it mean to show satisfaction at Chǔ’s submission?
If Chǔ has a king, it submits later;
if not, it rebels first.
They are Yí and Dí,
yet often trouble the Central States.
The southern and northern Yí interact.
The Central States continue only like a thread.
Huán Gōng rescued the Central States and expelled the Yí and Dí,
finally pacifying Jīng.
This is what a king must do.
Why does it say "came"?
To make Huán [Gōng] the leader.
There were affairs before,
and there were affairs after;
why then only here?
Because Huán Gōng is leader?
To order achievements.
The people of Qí seized Chén Yuán Tāotú.
What was Tāotú’s crime?
He blocked the way of the army.
How did he block the way of the army?
Tāotú said to Huán Gōng,
"You have already subdued the southern Yí.
Why not withdraw the troops, follow the seacoast eastward,
subdue the eastern Yí, and return home?"
Huán Gōng said,
"Agreed."
Accordingly, the army turned east along the coast,
falling into a great pit in Pèi Zé.
Looking back, they seized Tāotú.
Why is it that those who are seized are sometimes called “Marquis”
and sometimes simply “man”?
When one called “Marquis” is seized,
it is an act of hegemonic punishment.
When one called “man” is seized,
it is not an act of hegemonic punishment.
This seizure involved a crime;
why was it not considered hegemonic punishment?
In antiquity, when Zhōu Gōng campaigned east, the western states complained;
when he campaigned west, the eastern states complained.
Huán Gōng borrowed passage from Chén to attack Chǔ;
thus, the people of Chén did not wish the army’s return to be blamed on them—
the campaign was not just.
Not putting his army in order and then seizing Tāotú,
according to the ways of the ancients,
is not appropriate.
In autumn,
the Jiāng and Huáng people attacked Chén.
In the eighth month,
the lord returned from the campaign against Chǔ.
Chǔ had already submitted;
why was it attacked?
Because Chǔ broke the alliance.
Xǔ Miù Gōng was buried.
In winter, the twelfth month,
Gōngsūn Cí led an army to join the men of Qí, Sòng, Wèi, Zhèng, Xǔ, and Cáo in attacking Chén.
In the fifth year, spring,
the Marquis of Jìn killed his heir, Shēnshēng.
Why is it said plainly that the Marquis of Jìn killed him?
When a lord kills his heir or younger brother, to refer to him directly as "lord"
is a grave reproach.
The Ji of Qǐ came
to visit her son.
What does “came to visit her son” mean?
It is an inner matter,
she came together with her son.
In summer,
Gōngsūn Cí went to Móu.
The lord met the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Chén, Marquis of Wèi, Earl of Zhèng, Xǔ Nán, and Earl of Cáo to meet the royal heir at Shǒudài.
Why was it called a special meeting with the royal heir?
Because the heir was noble.
The heir is like an heir of heirs.
In autumn, the eighth month,
the lords swore an oath at Shǒudài.
Why are the lords not listed?
When the same event is mentioned twice,
the first is detailed, the next is general.
The Earl of Zhèng fled home and did not swear the oath.
What does it mean that he "fled home and did not swear the oath"?
He could not be allowed to take the oath.
If he could not be allowed to take the oath,
why say "fled home"?
Zǐ of Lǔ said,
"Because he should not have challenged many with a few."
The people of Chǔ destroyed Xián;
the heir of Xián fled to Huáng.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùshēn, beginning of the month,
there was an eclipse.
In winter,
the people of Jìn seized the Lord of Yú.
Yú was already destroyed,
why say "seized him"?
Because he was not included among the destroyed.
Why was he not included?
To be "destroyed" is the proper phrase for a fallen state.
"Destroyed" means it was by the combined efforts of all.
In the sixth year, spring, the first month of the king’s calendar.
In summer,
the lord joined with the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Chén, Marquis of Wèi, and Earl of Cáo to attack Zhèng,
and besieged Xīnchéng.
A city is not usually said to be besieged;
why is "besieged" stated here?
Because it was strong.
In autumn,
the people of Chǔ besieged Xǔ;
the lords then rescued Xǔ.
In winter,
the lord returned from the campaign against Zhèng.
In the seventh year, spring,
the people of Qí attacked Zhèng.
In summer,
the Lord of Xiǎo Zhūlóu came to pay homage.
Zhèng killed its great officer, Shēn Hóu.
Why is the state named in the killing?
When the state is named,
it means the ruler’s killing of a great officer.
In autumn, the seventh month,
the lord met the Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, heir of Chén, Kuǎn, and heir of Zhèng, Huá,
and swore an oath at Níngmǔ.
The Earl of Cáo, Bān, died.
Prince Yǒu went to Qí.
In winter,
Duke Zhāo of Cáo was buried.
In the eighth year, spring, the first month of the king’s calendar,
the lord met the royal agent, Marquis of Qí, Duke of Sòng, Marquis of Wèi, Xǔ Nán, Earl of Cáo, heir of Chén, Kuǎn, and heir of Zhèng, Huá,
and swore an oath at Tāo.
Who are the royal agents?
Minor functionaries.
Why are they listed before the lords?
Because of the command of the former kings.
The Earl of Zhèng begged to join in the alliance.
What does it mean to “beg to join the alliance”?
It means he remained in his place and asked to be included.
How did he “remain in his place and ask to be included”?
He made a measured plea.
In summer,
the Dí attacked Jìn.
In the seventh month of autumn,
a dÌ ceremony was performed at the Tàimiào;
used to present the Lady.
What does "used" mean?
"Used" means it ought not to be used.
What does "present" mean?
"Present" means it ought not to be presented.
To use the dÌ ceremony to present the Lady
is not in accordance with ritual.
Why is the Lady not referred to as Jiāng Shì?
It is a demotion.
Why is it a demotion?
It is to criticize taking a concubine as wife.
What does it mean, "taking a concubine as wife"?
It perhaps means being coerced by the envoys of Qí, whose women arrived first.
On Dīngwèi, the twelfth month of winter,
the Tiān Wáng died.
In the ninth year, in the third month of spring, on Dīngchǒu,
the Duke of Sòng, Yǔ Yuè, died.
Why is the burial not recorded?
Because it was taboo for Xiāng Gōng.
In summer,
the Duke convened with the Prime Minister Zhōu Gōng, Marquis of Qí, Viscount of Sòng, Marquis of Wèi, Earl of Zhèng, Baron of Xǔ, and Earl of Cáo at Kuíqiū.
Who is the Prime Minister Zhōu Gōng?
He is the official of state affairs for the Son of Heaven.
In the seventh month of autumn, on Yǐyǒu,
Lady Bó died.
Since she was not yet married, why does it record her death?
She had already been betrothed.
When a woman is betrothed,
she is given a style name and has her hair put up;
if she dies, she is mourned according to the rites for an adult.
On Wùchén, the ninth month,
the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuíqiū.
Why was the covenant of Huán not dated,
but this one is?
Because it was a time of calamity.
Why was it a time of calamity?
At the meeting of Guànzé,
Duke Huán of Qí was concerned for the Central States;
those who did not attend uninvited were the Jiāng and Huáng people.
At the meeting of Kuíqiū,
Duke Huán was boastful and proud;
nine states rebelled.
What does "boastful" mean?
It is like saying "arrogant and full of oneself."
What does "proud" mean?
It is like saying "No one is equal to me."
On Jiǎxū,
the Marquis of Jìn, Guǐzhū, died.
In winter,
Lǐ Kè of Jìn assassinated his lord's son, Xīqí.
This was a lord not yet in office a year;
why does it say "he assassinated his lord's son Xīqí"?
"Assassinated" is the term for a lord not yet a year on the throne.
In the tenth year, in the first month of spring,
the Duke went to Qí.
The Dí destroyed Wēn.
The son of Wēn fled to Wèi.
Lǐ Kè of Jìn assassinated his lord Zhuózi and his minister Xún Xī.
What does "and" mean here?
It means "together."
There have been many assassinations of lords;
apart from this, are there cases where it is not cumulative?
It is said:
"There were Kǒng Fù and Qiú Mù, both also cumulative."
Apart from Kǒng Fù and Qiú Mù,
is there any without cumulative blame?
It is said:
"There are."
If there are, why is it recorded here?
Because of their worthiness.
In what way was Xún Xī worthy?
Xún Xī can be said to have not gone back on his word.
How did he not go back on his word?
Xīqí and Zhuózi
were sons of Lí Jī.
Xún Xī was their tutor.
Lí Jī was of great beauty.
Duke Xiàn of Jìn greatly loved her,
and wished to establish her son as heir.
Thus, he killed the heir apparent Shēnshēng.
Shēnshēng
was tutored by Lǐ Kè.
Duke Xiàn was ill
and about to die;
he asked Xún Xī:
"How can a man be called faithful?"
Xún Xī replied:
"If the dead could return to life, and the living not be ashamed of their words,
then one can be called faithful."
Duke Xiàn died,
and Xīqí was set up.
Lǐ Kè said to Xún Xī:
"The ruler killed the rightful heir and set up the unrightful;
displaced the eldest and raised the youngest—what shall we do?
I beg to deliberate with you."
Xún Xī said:
"The ruler once questioned me,
and I replied:
'If the dead could return to life, and the living not be ashamed of their words,
then one can be called faithful.' "
Lǐ Kè knew he could not be joined in the plan,
so he withdrew and assassinated Xīqí.
Xún Xī established Zhuózi;
Lǐ Kè assassinated Zhuózi;
Xún Xī died for him.
Xún Xī can be said to have not gone back on his word.
In summer,
the Marquis of Qí and the Baron of Xǔ attacked the northern Róng.
Jìn killed its minister Lǐ Kè.
Lǐ Kè assassinated two lords;
so why is it not described as executing a traitor?
He was a minister of Duke Huì.
If so, who installed Duke Huì?
It was Lǐ Kè.
Lǐ Kè assassinated Xīqí and Zhuózi,
brought in Duke Huì in defiance;
Lǐ Kè established Duke Huì.
Then why did Duke Huì kill him?
Duke Huì said:
"You have killed the two youths,
now you intend to plot against me;
is not being your lord a calamity?"
So he killed him.
Then why does the record not mention Duke Huì's entry?
The records of Jìn do not describe the coming and going,
because they avoided mentioning Wén Gōng.
When Xiǎo Bái entered Qí,
why then was there no such avoidance for Duke Huán?
Because Duke Huán's reign was long
and his virtue was visible to the world,
so the avoidance was not due to the original offense.
Duke Wén’s reign was short,
and his virtue was not yet visible to the world,
so the avoidance was due to the original offense.
In the seventh month of autumn.
In winter,
there was a great hailstorm.
Why is it recorded?
To make note of extraordinary events.
In the eleventh year, in spring,
Jìn killed its minister Pī Zhèngfù.
In summer,
the Duke and Lady Jiāng Shì attended a meeting with the Marquis of Qí at Yánggǔ.
In the eighth month of autumn,
there was a great sacrifice for rain.
In winter,
the people of Chǔ attacked Huáng.
In the twelfth year, in the third month of spring, on Gēngwǔ,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In summer,
the people of Chǔ destroyed Huáng.
In the seventh month of autumn.
On Dīngchǒu, the twelfth month of winter,
the Marquis of Chén, Chǔ Jiù, died.
In the thirteenth year, in spring,
the Dí invaded Wèi.
In the fourth month of summer,
Chén Xuān Gōng was buried.
The Duke assembled with Qí Hóu, Sòng Gōng, Chén Hóu, Wèi Hóu, Zhèng Bó, Xǔ Nán, and Cáo Bó at Xián.
In the ninth month of autumn,
a great yú sacrifice was performed.
In winter,
Gōngzǐ Yǒu went to Qí.
In the fourteenth year, in spring,
the lords fortified Yuán Líng.
Who fortified it?
It was the city of Qǐ.
Why did they fortify Qǐ?
It was to destroy it.
Who destroyed it?
Perhaps it was because Xú and Jǔ coerced it.
Why is it not said that Xú and Jǔ coerced it?
Because it was to avoid mentioning Huán Gōng.
Why avoid mentioning Huán Gōng?
Above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, no regional chief;
when the feudal lords in the world destroyed each other,
Huán Gōng could not save them,
thus Huán Gōng was ashamed of it.
Then, who actually fortified it?
Huán Gōng fortified it.
Why is it not said that Huán Gōng fortified it?
Because it was not his place to grant fiefs independently of the feudal lords.
Why not?
Though he actually did so, the text does not record it as such.
Why does the text not record it?
It was not proper for a feudal lord, by right, to grant fiefs alone.
If, by the propriety of the feudal lords, they could not grant fiefs alone,
then why say that he actually did it?
Because above, there was no Son of Heaven;
below, no regional chief;
when the feudal lords in the world destroyed each other,
if he had the ability to save any,
then saving them was permissible.
In the sixth month of summer,
Jì Jī and the Lord of Zēng met at Fáng,
and had the Lord of Zēng come to court.
Why did the Lord of Zēng have to come to court at the bidding of Jì Jī?
It was a domestic arrangement.
It was not really to have him come to court,
but to come to make a request of her.
On Xīnmǎo day of the eighth month in autumn,
Shālù collapsed.
What is Shālù?
It is a settlement by the Yellow River.
Since it is a settlement,
what does "collapsed" mean?
It means the city was attacked.
Why is it recorded as "Shālù collapsed"?
It is to record something extraordinary.
Things extraordinary outside the state are not recorded,
so why is this recorded?
It is to record an anomaly for the whole world.
The Dí invaded Zhèng.
In winter,
Cài Hóu Xì passed away.
In the fifteenth year, in the first month of the royal calendar,
the Duke went to Qí.
The people of Chǔ attacked Xú.
In the third month,
the Duke assembled with Qí Hóu, Sòng Gōng, Chén Hóu, Wèi Hóu, Zhèng Bó, Xǔ Nán, and Cáo Bó to form a covenant at Mǔqiū,
and then encamped at Kuāng.
Gōngsūn Áo led troops along with the great officers of the feudal lords to rescue Xú.
In the fifth month of summer,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the seventh month of autumn,
the troops of Qí and Cáo attacked Lì.
In the eighth month,
there was the appearance of zhī.
In the ninth month,
the Duke returned from the assembly.
At the assembly of Huán Gōng he did not stay;
why did he stay this time?
Because it was for a long time.
Jì Jī returned to Zēng.
On the last day, jǐmǎo,
lightning struck the temple of Yí Bó.
What is meant by "the last day"?
It is darkness.
What does "struck" mean?
It means thunder and lightning struck the temple of Yí Bó.
Who was Yí Bó?
He was the descendant of Jì.
Since he was only a lesser descendant of Jì,
why is he called Yí Bó?
To elevate his status.
Why elevate him?
Heaven gave warning,
therefore his status was elevated.
Why is it recorded?
To record an anomaly.
In winter,
the people of Sòng attacked Cáo.
The people of Chǔ defeated Xú at Lóulín.
On the rénxū day of the eleventh month,
the Jìn Hóu and Qín Bó fought at Hán,
and captured the Jìn Hóu.
This was a side battle;
why is it not said that the army was defeated?
If the ruler was captured, it is not stated that the army was defeated.
In the sixteenth year, on the first day of the first month of the royal calendar, wùshēn,
stones fell at Sòngwǔ.
That month,
six wild geese flew backwards over the capital of Sòng.
Why mention first the falling, then the stones?
The falling stones were what people heard about;
they heard the sound thudding;
when they looked, they saw stones;
on closer examination, there were five.
What is meant by "that month"?
It means it just reached that month.
Why is the exact day not stated?
It was the last day of the month.
If so, why is "the last day" not recorded?
The Spring and Autumn Annals does not record the last day.
If the first day has an event, it is recorded;
even if the last day has an event, it is not recorded.
Why mention first "six" and then "geese"?
The six geese flying backwards is to record what was seen;
when seen, there were six;
on closer looking, they were wild geese;
when examined more slowly, they had flown backwards.
Why are the five stones and six wild geese recorded?
To record anomalies.
Anomalies from without are not recorded,
so why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly for the descendants of the king.
On rénshēn day of the third month,
Gōngzǐ Jì Yǒu died.
Why is he referred to as Jì Yǒu?
Because he was worthy.
On bǐngshēn day of the fourth month of summer,
Zēng Jì Jī died.
On jiǎzǐ day of the seventh month of autumn,
Gōngsūn Cí died.
In the twelfth month of winter,
the Duke assembled with Qí Hóu, Sòng Gōng, Chén Hóu, Wèi Hóu, Zhèng Bó, Xǔ Nán, Xíng Hóu, and Cáo Bó at Huái.
In the seventeenth year, in spring,
the people of Qí and Xú attacked Yīngshì.
In summer,
Xiàng was destroyed.
Who destroyed it?
Qí destroyed it.
Why is it not stated that Qí destroyed it?
It was to avoid mentioning Huán Gōng.
The Spring and Autumn Annals avoids naming the worthy,
but this was the destruction of a state,
so what worthiness was there?
The gentleman’s aversion to evil is strict at the beginning,
his approval of good enjoys the end.
Huán Gōng once had the achievement of restoring the extinct and preserving the perishing,
therefore, the gentlemen avoided naming him.
In autumn,
Madam Jiāng met with the Marquis of Qí at Biàn.
In the ninth month,
the Duke returned from the meeting.
In winter, in the twelfth month, on yǐhài day,
the Marquis of Qí, Xiǎobái, died.
In the eighteenth year, in spring, in the first month of the royal calendar,
the Duke of Sòng met with the Earl of Cáo, people of Wèi, people of Zhūlóu to attack Qí.
In summer,
troops went to rescue Qí.
On wǔyín day of the fifth month,
the Sòng army and the Qí army fought at Yǎn;
the Qí army was defeated.
When the text records a battle, it does not use the word “attack;”
why does it use “attack” here?
The Duke of Sòng joined the attack but did not join the battle,
therefore uses “attack.”
In the “Chūnqiū,” the “attacker” is the guest,
the “attacked” is the host.
Why is Qí not made the host?
Because of the campaign against Qí by Duke Xiāng.
Why connect it with Duke Xiāng’s campaign against Qí?
After Duke Huán died,
Shù Diāo and Yì Yá struggled for power,
the burial was not performed,
therefore they attacked Qí.
The Dí came to the aid of Qí.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on dīnghài day,
Duke Huán of Qí was buried.
In winter,
the people of Xíng and Dí attacked Wèi.
In the nineteenth year, in spring, in the third month of the royal calendar,
the people of Sòng captured Yīngqí, son of Téng.
In summer, in the sixth month,
the people of Sòng, Cáo, and Zhūlóu made a covenant at the south of Cáo.
The lord of Zēng joined the covenant at Zhūlóu.
Why is it said “joined the covenant”?
He joined later.
On jǐyǒu day,
the people of Zhūlóu seized the lord of Zēng,
and used him.
For what purpose?
Used him in the ancestral temple.
How was he used in the ancestral temple?
They struck his nose to offer blood at the altar.
In autumn,
the people of Sòng besieged Cáo.
The people of Wèi attacked Xíng.
In winter,
the Duke met with the people of Chén, Cài, Chǔ, and Zhèng, and made a covenant at Qí.
Liáng perished.
Since there was no record of attack,
why say Liáng perished?
It perished of itself.
How did it perish of itself?
Like a fish rotting away.
In the twentieth year, in spring,
the new south gate was built.
Why is this recorded?
It is a reproach.
Why the reproach?
Gates have ancient customs.
In summer,
the lord of Gào came to court.
Who is the lord of Gào?
He is a ruler who had lost his land.
Why is his name not recorded?
Because of the language of kinship.
On yǐsì day of the fifth month,
the west palace was destroyed by fire.
What is the west palace?
The minor bedchamber.
If a minor bedchamber, why is it called the west palace?
With a west palace, there must be an east palace.
The lord of Lǔ said:
“Since there is a west palace,
we know that feudal lords also have three palaces.”
Why record the disaster of the west palace?
To record the calamity.
The people of Zhèng entered Huá.
In autumn,
the people of Qí and Dí made a covenant at Xíng.
In winter,
the people of Chǔ attacked Suí.
In the twenty-first year, in spring,
the Dí invaded Wèi.
The people of Sòng, Qí, and Chǔ made a covenant at Lùshàng.
In summer,
there was a great drought.
Why is this recorded?
To record the calamity.
In autumn,
the Duke of Sòng, the Viscount of Chǔ, the Marquis of Chén, the Marquis of Cài, the Earl of Zhèng, the Baron of Xǔ, and the Earl of Cáo met at Huò,
and they seized the Duke of Sòng to attack Sòng.
Who seized him?
The Viscount of Chǔ seized him.
Why does it not say the Viscount of Chǔ seized him?
So as not to equate the grasp of China by the “barbarians” with that by the Huáxià people.
In winter,
the Duke attacked Zhūlóu.
The people of Chǔ sent Yí Shēn to come and present victory.
This is the Viscount of Chǔ,
so why call him only “people”?
It is derogatory.
Why derogatory?
Because he seized the Duke of Sòng.
Why is the seizing of the Duke of Sòng held as derogatory?
The Duke of Sòng and the Viscount of Chǔ had agreed to meet in chariots;
Gōngzǐ Mùyí admonished, saying:
“Chǔ is a land of the ‘Yi’,
strong but unrighteous,
may Your Lordship go in armor and with chariots.”
The Duke of Sòng said:
“No.
I have agreed to meet them in chariots,
I did this of myself,
if I change it myself,
then it would be unacceptable.”
In the end he went in chariots,
the people of Chǔ indeed ambushed with chariots,
and seized the Duke to attack Sòng.
The Duke said to Gōngzǐ Mùyí:
“You shall go back and guard the state,
the state is your state.
I have not followed your advice, and have come to this.”
Gōngzǐ Mùyí again said:
“Even if Your Lordship does not speak of the state,
the state is assuredly my state.”
Thereupon he returned, set up defenses, and guarded the state.
The people of Chǔ said to the people of Sòng:
“If you do not give me your state,
I shall kill your lord.”
The people of Sòng replied:
“Relying on the spirit of our altars and ancestors,
our state already has a lord.”
The people of Chǔ knew that even if they killed the Duke of Sòng,
they still could not obtain Sòng,
so they released him.
The Duke was thus released
and fled to Wèi.
Gōngzǐ Mùyí once more said:
“The state has been kept for Your Lordship;
why do you not return?”
Only then did they welcome Duke Xiāng home.
Where was the victory?
Victory was in Sòng.
Why does it not say “victory in Sòng”?
To avoid naming Duke Xiāng.
This is a circumlocution concerning the siege;
why is the siege not mentioned?
To avoid naming Gōngzǐ Mùyí.
In the twelfth month, on guǐchǒu day,
the Duke met with the feudal lords
and made a covenant at Bó.
Explanation of Sòng Gōng.
It had not previously been explained in words,
so why is it explained in words here?
Because it was Sòng Gōng himself who did it.
How was it Sòng Gōng who did it?
Because it was deliberated by Sòng Gōng himself.
In the twenty-second year, in the spring,
the Duke attacked Zhūlóu,
and took Xūqú.
In summer,
Sòng Gōng, Wèi Hóu, Xǔ Nán, and Téng Zǐ attacked Zhèng.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
they fought the Zhūlóu at Shēngxíng.
In winter, on the first day of the eleventh month, on the day Jǐsì,
Sòng Gōng fought the Chǔ army at Hóng,
the Sòng army was greatly defeated.
That some only fought on one side
— why does it mention the first day?
Chūnqiū’s language is elaborate yet not excessive, this is correctness.
Why correctness?
Sòng Gōng and the Chǔ army had agreed to battle at the south of Hóng.
The Chǔ army crossed Hóng and approached.
An official repeatedly said:
“Let us attack them before they have completed crossing.”
Sòng Gōng said:
“No.
I have heard
the gentleman does not block others.
Though I am the remnant of a ruined state,
I, the lone one, cannot bear to do it.”
After they had crossed,
but before they had completed forming ranks,
the official again said:
“Let us attack before they have completed their formation.”
Sòng Gōng said:
“No.
I have heard
the gentleman does not sound the drum if the ranks are not formed.”
Once their formation was set,
then Duke Xiāng gave the signal to drum,
and the Sòng army was utterly defeated.
Therefore the gentleman esteems highly the act of not drumming before ranks are set,
facing great affairs yet not forgetting great ritual.
There was a lord but no ministers,
so it is said that even in Wén Wáng’s battles,
there was nothing superior to this.
In the twenty-third year, in the spring,
Qí Hóu attacked Sòng,
and surrounded Mín.
It is not usual to say “enclosed” regarding cities—
so why does it say “enclosed” here?
Because of the gravity of the matter.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Sòng Gōng’s father Cí died.
Why is burial not recorded?
Yíng, because of avoidance of taboo.
In autumn,
the Chǔ army attacked Chén.
In winter, in the eleventh month,
Qǐzǐ died.
In the twenty-fourth year, in the first month of the king’s calendar.
In summer,
the Dí invaded Zhèng.
In autumn, in the seventh month.
In winter,
the Son of Heaven departed to reside in Zhèng.
The king has no outside;
so why does it say “departed”?
It was because he could not resist his own mother.
The Duke of Lǔ said:
“This king,
being unable to resist his mother,
is he not precisely as has just been described?”
Jìn Hóu Yíwú died.
In the twenty-fifth year, in the king’s first month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Wèi Hóu Huǐ destroyed and annihilated Xíng.
Why is Wèi Hóu Huǐ named?
It is severance.
Why severance?
Because Xíng shared the same clan-name.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Wèi Hóu Huǐ died.
Sòng Dàng Bójī came to receive a bride.
Who is Sòng Dàng Bójī?
She is the mother of the Dàng clan.
Why say “came to receive a bride”?
It is the language of brothers.
Why refer to “the bride”?
It is the language of a daughter-in-law with a mother-in-law.
Sòng killed one of its dàfū.
Why is the name not given?
For three generations Sòng had no dàfū,
because marriages were within the three degrees of kinship.
In autumn,
the Chǔ army besieged Chén,
and installed Dùn Zǐ in Dùn.
Why is “then” not used?
It was done twice.
Buried Wèi Wén Gōng.
In winter, in the twelfth month, on the day Guǐhài,
the Duke met with Wèi Zǐ and Jǔ Qìng, and swore an alliance at Táo.
In the twenty-sixth year, in the king’s first month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Duke met with Jǔ Zǐ and Wèi Níng Sù,
and swore an alliance at Xiàng.
The Qí army raided our western borders.
The Duke pursued the Qí army to Xī,
but did not catch them.
Why “to Xī but did not catch them”?
It is boastfulness.
In summer,
the Qí army attacked our northern borders.
The Wèi army attacked Qí.
Gōngzǐ Suì went to Chǔ to request military assistance.
What does “request” mean?
It is a humble expression.
Why use the same term for both foreign and internal requests?
To emphasize the importance of the army.
Why emphasize the army?
Because when an army goes out, if not proper, it does not return;
in battle, if not proper, it does not win.
In autumn,
the Chǔ army destroyed Wěi,
returning with Wěi Zǐ.
In winter,
the Chǔ army attacked Sòng,
and surrounded Mín.
Cities are not usually said to be enclosed;
why does it say “enclosed” here?
To criticize the manner in which the army was dispatched.
The Duke, with the Chǔ army, attacked Qí,
and took Gǔ.
The Duke returned from attacking Qí.
Since Gǔ was already taken,
why is “attacked” recorded?
Because the territory of Gǔ was not yet possessed.
Why was possession of Gǔ not yet secured?
It is said:
“When disaster arises,
it must begin from here.”
In the twenty-seventh year, in the spring,
Qǐzǐ came to court.
In summer, in the sixth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Qí Hóu Zhāo died.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Qi buried Xiào Gōng.
On the day Yǐsì,
Gōngzǐ Suì led an army into Qǐ.
In winter,
the people of Chǔ, the Marquis of Chén, the Marquis of Cài, the Earl of Zhèng, and the Man of Xǔ besieged Sòng.
These were the sons of Chǔ,
so why are they called “people”?
It is a term of demotion.
Why are they demoted?
Because they captured the Duke of Sòng and were therefore demoted,
thus throughout the end of the section on Duke Xī, they are demoted.
On the jiǎxū day of the twelfth month,
the Duke met the feudal lords and swore an alliance at Sòng.
In the twenty-eighth year, in spring,
the Marquis of Jìn attacked Cáo,
the Marquis of Jìn campaigned against Wèi.
Why is the Marquis of Jìn mentioned twice?
It is not that there were two separate people.
Then why is it not said, “Then”?
Because he had not yet attacked Cáo.
If he had not yet attacked Cáo, why does it say “attacked Cáo”?
To convey his intent.
His intent was to attack Cáo,
then why campaign against Wèi?
The Marquis of Jìn intended to attack Cáo,
requested passage through Wèi,
Wèi said it could not be granted,
so he was determined to attack it.
Gōngzǐ Mǎi garrisoned Wèi,
but did not complete the garrison,
he was condemned.
What does it mean to not complete the garrison?
Not completing the garrison
is an internal resignation,
he could not be sent on the mission.
If he could not be sent, why does it say “garrisoned Wèi”?
It follows the Duke’s intent.
What does “condemned” mean?
He was killed.
If he was killed, why call it “condemned”?
Internally, killing a major official is called “condemning.”
The people of Chǔ came to the aid of Wèi.
On the bǐngwǔ day of the third month,
the Marquis of Jìn entered Cáo,
captured the Earl of Cáo,
and handed him over to the people of Sòng.
What does “handed over” mean?
It means to give.
Why say “to the people of Sòng”?
To entrust him to their judgment.
What was the crime of the Earl of Cáo?
It was extremely wicked.
How wicked was it?
It cannot be expressed with a single crime.
In the summer, on the jǐsì day of the fourth month,
the Marquis of Jìn, the forces of Qí, the forces of Sòng, the forces of Qín, and the people of Chǔ battled at Chéngpú;
the army of Chǔ was utterly defeated.
This was a great battle,
why then use a lesser title?
Because Zǐyù attained ministerial rank.
If Zǐyù attained ministerial rank, why then are they called “people”?
It is a demotion.
Why are they demoted?
Because a minister is not equal to a lord.
Chǔ killed its senior minister Déchén.
The Marquis of Wèi fled to Chǔ.
On the guǐchǒu day of the fifth month,
the Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn, the Marquis of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Cài, the Earl of Zhèng, the Viscount of Wèi, and the Viscount of Jǔ,
and swore an alliance at Jiàntǔ.
The Marquis of Chén came to the meeting.
Why does it say “came to the meeting”?
He arrived later than the others.
The Duke had an audience at the court of the King.
Why does it not say, “the Duke went to the capital”?
Because the Son of Heaven was there.
Since the Son of Heaven was there,
why does it not say “the Son of Heaven was there”?
Because it does not record the audience as directed by the king.
In the sixth month,
the Marquis of Wèi Zhèng returned home from Chǔ to Wèi.
Wèi Yuánxuǎn fled to Jìn.
The Marquis of Chén Kuǎn died.
In autumn,
the Lady Bó Jī of Qǐ came.
Gōngzǐ Suì went to Qí.
In winter,

the Duke met with the Marquis of Jìn, the Marquis of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Cài, the Earl of Zhèng, the Viscount of Chén, the Viscount of Jǔ, the Viscount of Zhūlóu, and the people of Qín at Wēn.
The Heavenly King hunted at Héyáng.
Hunting was not recorded,
so why is it recorded here?
It does not record a second audience with the Son of Heaven.
The Man of Lǔ said:
“Wēn is near and Jiàntǔ is far.”
On the rénshēn day,
the Duke had an audience at the court of the King.
Why is the day recorded?
Because it is recorded in the inner records.
The people of Jìn captured the Marquis of Wèi,
and sent him back to the capital.
What does “sent back to the capital” mean?
What does “sent back to” mean?
“Sent back to the capital”—the crime is already established;
“sent back to”—the crime is not yet established.
If the crime is not yet established, how could they have organized the punitive expedition as hegemon?
“Sent back to the capital”
means being held at the side of the Son of Heaven;
whether the crime is established or not
can already be known.
“Sent back to”
is not at the side of the Son of Heaven;
whether the crime is established or not
cannot yet be known.
What was the crime of the Marquis of Wèi?
He killed Shūwǔ.
Why is it not recorded?
To avoid mentioning it for Shūwǔ’s sake.
The *Spring and Autumn Annals* avoids naming the faults of the worthy.
How was Shūwǔ worthy?
He gave up the state.
How did he give up the state?
Duke Wén drove out the Marquis of Wèi and installed Shūwǔ;
Shūwǔ declined the installation, and someone else took the position;
fearing then that the Marquis of Wèi could not return,
therefore he allowed himself to be installed,
and then worked for the Jiàntǔ assembly to restore the Marquis of Wèi.
The Marquis of Wèi returned,
and said:
“Shūwǔ usurped my state.”
Yuánxuǎn disputed, saying:
“Shūwǔ is without guilt.”
In the end, Shūwǔ was killed,
and Yuánxuǎn fled.
This was the Marquis of Jìn;
so why call him “people”?
It is a demotion.
Why demote him?
Because the disaster of Wèi was caused by Duke Wén.
How did Duke Wén cause it?
Duke Wén drove out the Marquis of Wèi and installed Shūwǔ,
causing suspicion between brothers,
leading to the killing of his brother by the ruler,
Duke Wén caused this.
Wèi Yuánxuǎn returned from Jìn to Wèi.
What does “from” mean?
It means “having some power behind it.”
This was to seize his lord,
why say “from”?
It was for the sake of contesting for Shūwǔ.
The feudal lords then besieged Xǔ.
The Earl of Cáo Xiāng returned to Cáo.
Then the feudal lords assembled to besiege Xǔ.
In the twenty-ninth year, in spring,
Jiè Gélú came.
Who is Jiè Gélú?
He is a lord of the Yí and Dí tribes.
Why is it not said that he came to court?
He was unable to appear at court.
The Duke returned from besieging Xǔ.
In the summer, in the sixth month,
the Duke met with the royal representative, the people of Jìn, Sòng, Qí, Chén, Cài, and Qín, and formed an alliance at Díquán.
In autumn,
there was a great hailstorm.
In winter,
Jiè Gélú came.
In the thirtieth year, spring, the king’s first month.
In summer,
the Dí invaded Qí.
In autumn,
Wèi killed its Dàfū Yuán Xuǎn and Prince Xiá.
The Marquess of Wèi had not yet arrived;
why say that the state killed them?
It was on the road that they were killed.
The Marquess of Wèi, Zhèng, returned to Wèi.
This being the killing of his Dàfū,
why does it say “returned”?
He returned to censure Yuán Xuǎn.
Why did he return to censure Yuán Xuǎn?
When Yuán Xuǎn served his lord,
when the lord went out, he came in;
when the lord came in, he went out;
he was thought not to be a true minister.
The people of Jìn and Qín besieged Zhèng.
The Jiè people invaded Xiāo.
In winter,
the Celestial King sent Zǎi Zhōugōng to come and make a friendly visit.
Prince Suì went to the capital,
then went to Jìn.
The Dàfū did not handle the matter at all;
why does it say Suì?
The Duke was unable to govern.
In the thirty-first year, spring,
they took the fields west of the Jǐ.
From whom did they take it?
They took it from Cáo.
Why not say they took it from Cáo?
It was taboo to mention taking land from those of the same surname.
There had not yet been an attack on Cáo;
why then does it say they took it from Cáo?
The Marquess of Jìn seized the Earl of Cáo,
and distributed the taken and occupied land to the feudal lords.
The Marquess of Jìn seized the Earl of Cáo,
and distributed the taken and occupied land to the feudal lords;
why then be concerned about saying they took land from those of the same surname?
It had been a long time.
Prince Suì went to Jìn.
In the fourth month of summer,
they performed four divinations for the suburb sacrifice,
yet did not comply,
so they released the sacrificial animals,
but still performed three “wàng” sacrifices.
Why is it sometimes said three divinations?
Sometimes four divinations?
Three divinations are according to ritual;
four divinations are not according to ritual.
How are three divinations according to ritual?
How are four divinations not according to ritual?
There are three ways to seek an auspicious omen.
For ancestral and seasonal sacrifices, no divination is performed;
why, then, perform divination for the suburb sacrifice?
To divine for the suburb sacrifice is not according to ritual.
Why is it not according to ritual?
The suburb sacrifice of Lǔ is not according to ritual.
Why is the suburb sacrifice of Lǔ not according to ritual?
The Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven;
the feudal lords sacrifice to Earth.
The Son of Heaven has the duty of offerings at the four outlooks,
and there is nothing he cannot address.
As for the feudal lords, if there are mountains and rivers not within the limits of their fiefs,
they do not sacrifice to them.
Why do some say “release the sacrificial animals”?
Some say “release the ox”?
To release the sacrificial animals is according to ritual; to release the ox is not.
Why is releasing the ox not ritual?
When the victim is injured, it is called “ox.”
What are the three “wàng” sacrifices?
They are outlook sacrifices.
Then to what do they sacrifice?
They sacrifice to Mount Tài, the Yellow River, and the Sea.
Why do they sacrifice to Mount Tài, the Yellow River, and the Sea?
Those mountains and rivers which can bring moisture within a hundred lǐ,
the Son of Heaven establishes their sacrifices.
If a spring issues upon touching stone,
and the land comes together within an inch,
and within a day covers the whole world with rain,
only Mount Tài is like this.
The Yellow River and the Sea bring moisture for a thousand lǐ.
What does “still” mean?
If communication is possible, it may be stopped.
Why is it recorded?
To criticize making outlook sacrifices in place of the suburb sacrifice.
The seventh month of autumn.
In winter,
the Lady Consort of Qǐ came to seek a wife.
Why does it say she came to seek a wife?
It was the language of brothers.
Why is the term “wife” used?
Because it was in the name of the lady of the house.
The Dí besieged Wèi.
In the twelfth month,
Wèi moved to Dìqiū.
In the thirty-second year, spring, the king’s first month.
Summer, fourth month, jǐchǒu day,
the Earl of Zhèng, Jiē, died.
The people of Wèi invaded the Dí.
In autumn,
the people of Wèi and the Dí formed an alliance.
Winter, twelfth month, jǐmǎo day,
the Marquess of Jìn, Zhòng-Ěr, died.
In the thirty-third year, spring, second month of the king,
the people of Qín entered Huá.
The Marquess of Qí sent Guó Guīfù to make a friendly visit.
In summer, fourth month, xīnsì day,
the people of Jìn together with Jiāng Róng defeated Qín at Xiáo.
Why is it referred to as Qín?
Because it belonged to the Yí and Dí.
Why say it belonged to the Yí and Dí?
The Earl of Qín was going to attack Zhèng;
Bǎilǐzǐ and Jiǎnshūzǐ remonstrated, saying:
“Attacking others from a distance of a thousand lǐ,
there has never been one who did not perish.”
The Earl of Qín grew angry and said:
“At your age,
the trees atop the granary would have long grown thick;
what do you know?”
The army set out;
Bǎilǐzǐ and Jiǎnshūzǐ saw their sons off and warned them, saying:
“If you die, it will surely be in the crags of Xiáo;
this is where King Wén sheltered from wind and rain,
I shall lay your body to rest there.”
Their sons bowed to the army and set out.
Bǎilǐzǐ and Jiǎnshūzǐ followed and wept for their sons.
The Earl of Qín was angry and said:
“Why are you weeping for my army?”
They replied:
“We would not dare to weep for your army,
we weep for our sons.”
Xián Gāo, a merchant of Zhèng,
met them at Xiáo
and, feigning the command of the Earl of Zhèng, supplied the army with food;
some say he returned,
some say he went.
Nevertheless, the people of Jìn, together with Jiāng Róng, encircled them at Xiáo and attacked them,
so that not a single horse or chariot returned.
Why does it mention Jiāng Róng?
Jiāng Róng was insignificant;
mentioning them is also to stress smallness.
Why speak of the insignificance of Jiāng Róng?
It was Xiān Zhěn;
some say Duke Xiāng personally engaged them.
If Duke Xiāng personally engaged them, why then say “the people of Jìn”?
To diminish.
Why diminish?
Because the lord was at the mourning hall and the army engaged in danger,
he could not be buried.
Feigned battle is not recorded with the day;
why then record the day?
Because it was the end.
Guǐsì day,
they buried Duke Wén of Jìn.
The Dí invaded Qí.
The Duke attacked Zhūlóu
and took Cóng.
In autumn,
Gōngzǐ Suì led an army to attack Zhūlóu.
The Jìn people defeated the Dí at Jī.
In the tenth month of winter,
the Lord went to Qí.
In the twelfth month,
the Lord returned from Qí.
On yǐsì day,
the Lord died at Xiǎoqǐn.
The falling frost did not kill the grass,
and the plum and plum trees bore fruit.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
In what is it anomalous?
It is untimely.
The Jìn people, Chén people, and Zhèng people attacked Xǔ.
In the first year, in the first month of King’s calendar in spring,
the Lord ascended the throne.
On the guǐhài day in the second month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
The Son of Heaven sent Shūfú to attend the funeral.
What does it mean, “to attend the funeral”?
To attend the funeral is according to ritual.
On the dīngsì day of the fourth month in summer,
our Lord Xī Gōng was buried.
The Son of Heaven sent Máo Bó to come and bestow a mandate on the Lord.
What does “bestow” mean?
It means to grant.
What does “mandate” mean?
To confer attire upon us.
The Marquis of Jìn attacked Wèi.
Shū Sūn Déchén went to the capital.
The Wèi people attacked Jìn.
In autumn,
Gōngsūn Áo met with the Marquis of Jìn at Qī.
On the dīngwèi day of the tenth month in winter,
the heir apparent of Chǔ, Shāngchén, murdered his Lord Kūn.
Gōngsūn Áo went to Qí.
In the second year, on the jiǎzǐ day of the second month in the King's spring,
the Marquis of Jìn and the army of Qín fought at Péngyá,
and the Qín army was defeated.
On the dīngchǒu day,
they established a spirit tablet for Lord Xī.
What does “to establish a spirit tablet for Lord Xī” mean?
It means establishing a tablet for Lord Xī.
For what is a spirit tablet used?
For the Yú shrine, mulberry wood is used;
for the Liàn shrine, chestnut is used.
Why use chestnut?
To store the spirit tablet.
Why is the establishment of Lord Xī's spirit tablet recorded?
It is a criticism.
Why is it a criticism?
Because it was untimely.
How was it untimely?
They wished to mourn for long, but afterwards were unable.
On the yǐsì day of the third month,
they swore an alliance with Chǔfù of Jìn.
This is Chǔfù of Jìnyáng,
so why is the clan name omitted?
Because the given name was used in making alliance with the Dàfū.
In the sixth month of summer,
Gōngsūn Áo met with the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, the Earl of Zhèng, and the Jìn official Hú to swear an alliance at Chuíliǎn.
From the twelfth month there was no rain
until the seventh month in autumn.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
A great drought is recorded as a disaster,
this also was a drought,
so why is it recorded as an anomaly?
When a great drought is short in duration, it is called a disaster,
therefore it is recorded as a disaster.
This drought lasted a long time without disaster,
so it is recorded as an anomaly.
On the dīngmǎo day of the eighth month,
a great ceremony was held in the great ancestral temple,
elevating Lord Xī.
What is the great ceremony?
It is the Grand Xiá.
What is the Grand Xiá?
It is a joint sacrifice.
How is the joint sacrifice performed?
The tablets from destroyed temples are arranged before the Great Ancestor,
the tablets from undestroyed temples are all elevated,
they partake of offerings together with the Great Ancestor,
and once every five years there is again a Grand Sacrifice.
What does “elevate” mean?
It means to ascend.
Why mention specifically the elevation of Lord Xī?
It is a criticism.
Why a criticism?
Because the sequence of sacrifices was reversed.
How were the sacrifices reversed?
Ancestor was honored before the parent.
In winter,
the people of Jìn, Sòng, Chén, and Zhèng attacked Qín.
Gōngzǐ Suì went to Qí to give betrothal gifts.
Betrothal gifts are not usually recorded,
so why is this recorded?
It is a criticism.
Why a criticism?
It is a criticism of marrying during mourning.
If the marriage occurred after the three-year period,
then why is marrying during mourning criticized?
Because within three years no weddings are planned.
To make sacrifice at the altar of Zhuāng Gōng is a criticism.
Then why not criticize at the sacrifice?
The three years’ mourning is deeply felt,
it is not a hollow attachment.
Since the human heart is thought to possess it,
if it is assumed the human heart possesses it,
then why criticize marrying and nothing else?
Marriage is a great felicity,
not ordinary felicity.
Its happiness concerns oneself,
so if one assumes one has a human heart,
then it should be changed in this matter.
In the third year, first month of King’s calendar in spring,
Shū Sūn Déchén met with the people of Jìn, Sòng, Chén, Wèi, and Zhèng to attack Shěn,
and Shěn was defeated.
In the fifth month of summer,
Wángzǐ Hǔ died.
Who was Wángzǐ Hǔ?
He was a Dàfū of the Son of Heaven.
If he were an external Dàfū, his death would not be recorded;
so why is his death recorded?
Because he was newly sent to us.
The people of Qín attacked Jìn.
In autumn,
the people of Chǔ laid siege to Jiāng.
There was a rain of locusts in Sòng.
What does a rain of locusts mean?
They died and fell.
Why is this recorded?
To record an anomaly.
External anomalies are not recorded,
so why is this recorded?
Because it was an anomaly written for the descendants of the King.
In winter,
the Lord went to Jìn.
On the jǐsì day of the twelfth month,
the Lord and the Marquis of Jìn swore an alliance.
Chǔfù of Jìnyáng led an army to attack Chǔ and rescue Jiāng.
This is an attack on Chǔ,
so why say “to rescue Jiāng”?
It is to justify the action.
How is it a justification?
Attacking Chǔ on the pretext of rescuing Jiāng.
In the fourth year, in spring,
the Lord returned from Jìn.
In summer,
the rebellious wife Jiāng went to Qí.
What is meant by “the rebellious wife Jiāng went to Qí”?
It means she was abandoned.
Master Gāo said:
“Marrying into the house of a dàfū means being abandoned.”
The Dí invaded Qí.
In autumn,
the people of Chǔ destroyed Jiāng.
The Lord of Jìn attacked Qín.
The Lord of Wèi sent Níng Yú as an envoy.
In winter, the eleventh month, on rényín day,
the Lady of the Fēng clan passed away.
In the fifth year, in the first month of spring, the first month of the King,
the King sent Róng Shū to return the funeral gifts,
as well as a grant.
What is meant by “funeral gifts”?
The mouthfuls of food.
What does the phrase “to return the funeral gifts and grant” mean?
It combined them.
To combine them is not according to the rites.
On xīnhài day in the third month,
our young lady Chéng Fēng was buried.
Who was Chéng Fēng?
She was the mother of Duke Xī.
The King sent Shào Bó to join in the burial.
In summer,
Gōngsūn Áo went to Jìn.
The people of Qín entered Ruò.
In autumn,
the people of Chǔ destroyed Liù.
In winter, on jiǎshēn day in the tenth month,
the Lord Yè of Xǔ died.
In the sixth year, in spring,
they buried Duke Xī of Xǔ.
In summer,
Jìsūn Xíngfù went to Chén.
In autumn,
Jìsūn Xíngfù went to Jìn.
On yǐhài day in the eighth month,
the Lord Huān of Jìn died.
In winter, in the tenth month,
Prince Suì went to Jìn.
They buried Duke Xiāng of Jìn.
Jìn killed his dàfū Yáng Chùfù.
Jìn’s Hú Shègū fled to the Dí.
When Jìn killed his dàfū Yáng Chùfù,
why then did Hú Shègū flee?
Hè Shègū was the killer.
If Shègū was the killer, why does the record say the state killed him?
The lord was concealing his words.
How did he conceal his words?
The lord wished to make Shègū a general.
Yáng Chùfù remonstrated, saying,
“Shègū is not liked by the people.
He cannot be made general.”
So he removed him from the generalship.
Yáng Chùfù left,
and Shègū entered.
The lord said to Shègū,
“Yáng Chùfù said,
‘Shègū is not liked by the people.
He cannot be made general.’”
Shègū became angry,
and went out to stab Yáng Chùfù in the court and fled.
In the intercalary month,
no notification of the month was made,
yet he still attended court at the ancestral temple.
What is meant by not notifying the month?
It means not notifying the new moon.
Why was the new moon not notified?
Heaven did not count this month.
Since it was an intercalary month,
why is it said that heaven did not count this month?
This month is not a regular month.
What does “yet” mean?
It means because it is permissible to stop regular practice.
In the seventh year, in spring,
the duke attacked Zhūlóu.
On jiǎxū day in the third month,
they seized Xūqú.
When seizing a city, the date is not usually recorded;
why is the date recorded here?
It is to distance oneself by the phrasing,
as if they were someone else.
They then fortified Wú.
In the fourth month of summer,
the Duke Wángchén of Sòng died.
The people of Sòng killed their dàfū.
Why is the name not given?
For three generations Sòng had no dàfū,
for three generations they married within the clan.
On wùzǐ day,
the people of Jìn and the people of Qín fought at Línghú.
Xiān Mèi of Jìn fled with his troops to Qín.
This was a partial battle;
why does the record not say the army was defeated?
Because they were equally matched.
This refers to Xiān Mèi of Jìn;
why refer to him as just “man”?
To downgrade him.
Why downgrade him?
Because he was outside.
How is he outside?
He left with his army.
Why does it not say “departed”?
Because he was already outside.
The Dí invaded our western borders.
In the eighth month of autumn,
the duke met with the lords and the dàfū of Jìn,
and made a covenant at Hù.
Why are the lords not listed?
Why is the dàfū not named?
The duke lost the order of precedence.
What does it mean that the duke lost precedence?
The lords should not be made to covenant with the duke,
but he let the dàfū of Jìn covenant with him.
In winter,
Xú attacked Jǔ.
Gōngsūn Áo went to Jǔ to oversee the covenant.
In the eighth year, in spring, the first month of the King.
In the fourth month of summer.
On wùshēn day in the eighth month of autumn,
the Son of Heaven passed away.
On rénwǔ day of the tenth month in winter,
Prince Suì met Zhào Dùn of Jìn,
and made a covenant at Héngyōng.
On yǐyǒu day,
Prince Suì met the Yīluò Róng and made a covenant at Bào.
Gōngsūn Áo went to the capital,
but did not reach Fù.
On bǐngxū day,
he fled to Jǔ.
What is meant by “did not reach Fù”?
“Did not reach Fù”
is a distancing phrase.
He could not be made to go.
If he could not be made to go,
why is it recorded that he went to the capital?
That was the duke’s wish.
Why does it not say “sent out”?
Because he was already outside.
Qiū.
The people of Sòng killed their dàfū Sīmǎ.
Sòng Sīchéng came as a fugitive.
What is a Sīmǎ?
What is a Sīchéng?
Both are officials selected by office.
Why are both officials selected by office?
For three generations Sòng had no dàfū,
for within three generations they married within the clan.
In the ninth year, spring,
Máo Bó came to request gold.
Who is Máo Bó?
A dàfū of the Son of Heaven.
Why is he not called an envoy?
It was during mourning, and he had not yet become sovereign.
More than a year had passed,
why is it said he was not yet sovereign?
He had ascended the throne, but not yet taken the title “king.”
If not yet titled king, how do we know he ascended the throne?
As among zhūhóu, they take the throne after the mourning year;
thus we know that the Son of Heaven also takes the throne after the mourning year.
And as the Son of Heaven is called king only in the third year,
so also the zhūhóu are called “zǐ” within their fief in the third year.
After a year they are called “gōng,”
then why in their fief are they called “zǐ” in the third year?
In light of the hearts of the people and ministers,
they cannot go a single day without a ruler;
but in light of the principle of end and beginning,
there cannot be two rulers in one year;
so there cannot be a year without a ruler.
In light of the heart of a filial son,
three years is unbearable to bear.
Why is it recorded that Máo Bó came to request gold?
To censure.
What is censured?
A king has nothing to request,
to request gold is contrary to ritual.
Then is he a king?
It is said: No.
If he is not a king, then why call him a king?
A king has nothing to request,
it is said: this is a zǐ.
He continues the model of King Wén,
and upholds the law and regulations of King Wén;
the laws of King Wén had no requests,
yet he requested,
therefore it is censured.
The Lady Jiāng went to Qí.
In the second month,
Shū Sūn Déchén went to the capital.
On Xīnchǒu day,
Duke Xiāng Wáng was buried.
The burial of a king is not recorded,
why is it recorded here?
It was not recorded at the proper time.
When recorded after the time,
if I have involvement, then it is recorded.
The Jìn people killed their dàfū Xiān Dū.
In the third month,
the Lady Jiāng returned from Qí.
The Jìn people killed their dàfū Shì Hú and Jī Zhèng Fù.
Chǔ attacked Zhèng.
Prince Suì assembled the Jìn people, Sòng people, Wèi people, and Xǔ people to rescue Zhèng.
Summer,
the Dí invaded Qí.
In autumn, the eighth month,
Cáo Bó Xiāng died.
In the ninth month, on Guǐyǒu day,
there was an earthquake.
What is an earthquake?
The earth moved.
Why is it recorded?
To record strange events.
Winter,
the Chǔ son sent Jiāo on a diplomatic mission.
Who is Jiāo?
A Chǔ dàfū.
Chǔ had no dàfū,
why is it recorded here?
It is the beginning of having dàfū.
If it is the beginning of having dàfū,
then why not record the surname?
There are many such cases among the Xǔ and the Yí and Dì.
The Qín sent back the funerary gifts of Duke Xī Gōng and Chéng Fēng.
Why are Duke Xī Gōng and Chéng Fēng mentioned?
Both were included.
Including both is contrary to ritual.
Why is it not recorded as “and Chéng Fēng”?
Because Chéng Fēng was honored.
Duke Gòng Gōng of Cáo was buried.
In the tenth year, spring, third month of the King, on Xīnmǎo day,
Zāng Sūn Chén died.
Summer,
Qín attacked Jìn.
Chǔ killed its dàfū Yí Shēn.
From the first month it did not rain
until the seventh month of autumn.
When Sūzǐ made a covenant at Nǚlì.
Winter,
the Dí invaded Sòng.
The Chǔ son and the Hóu of Cài encamped at Qūhé.
In the eleventh year, spring,
the Chǔ son attacked Juàn.
Summer,
Shū Péngshēng assembled with Jìn Xì Quē at Chéngkuāng.
Autumn,
Cáo Bó came to court.
Prince Suì went to Sòng.
The Dí invaded Qí.
In winter, the tenth month, on Jiǎwǔ day,
Shū Sūn Déchén defeated the Dí at Xián.
What are the Dí?
They are the Cháng Dí.
There were three brothers,
one went to Qí,
one went to Lǔ,
one went to Jìn.
As for the one who went to Qí,
Prince Chéng Fù killed him.
As for the one who went to Lǔ,
Shū Sūn Déchén killed him.
For the one who went to Jìn, it is not yet known.
Why is the word “defeat” used?
To magnify it.
Why is the date given?
To magnify it.
Why is the place given?
To magnify it.
Why is it recorded?
To record a strange event.
In the twelfth year, spring, first month of the King,
Shèng Bó came as a fugitive.
Who is Shèng Bó?
A ruler who lost his territory.
Why is his personal name not recorded?
It is the language of brothers.
The Qǐ Bó came to court.
In the second month, on Gēngzǐ day,
Zǐ Shū Jī died.
She was not yet married—why is “died” used?
She had already been betrothed.
When a woman is betrothed,
her courtesy name is bestowed and her hair is bound;
if she dies, she is given adult mourning rites.
Why is the title “Zǐ” used?
Because of her rank.
How is she ranked?
She was a uterine sister.
Summer,
the Chǔ people besieged Cháo.
Autumn,
the Téng zǐ came to court.
The Duke of Qín sent Suì to conduct a friendly visit.
Who is Suì?
He is a grandee of Qín.
Qín had no grandees;
why is this recorded?
It is because of the worthiness of Duke Miù.
In what was Duke Miù worthy?
He was considered able to adapt.
What does it mean that he was able to adapt?
He was ever courteous and skilled in concise speech.
He made gentlemen easily grow negligent,
let alone when I possess much of this quality;
only a solitary person who resolutely perseveres,
with no other skill.
His heart is at peace,
he is able to be accommodating,
and this is difficult.
On the wùwǔ day of the twelfth month in winter,
the Jìn people and the Qín people battled at Héqū.
This was a partial engagement;
why does it not say that the armies suffered a rout?
Because they were evenly matched.
Why is the terrain described as watery?
The area around Héqū is sparse;
within a thousand lǐ the Yellow River only bends once.
Jìsūn Xíngfù led the troops to fortify Zhū and conduct transportation.
In the thirteenth year, during the first month of spring in the royal calendar.
On the rénwǔ day in the fifth month of summer,
the Marquis Shuò of Chén passed away.
The lord of Zhūlóu, Qū Chú, passed away.
From the first month, there was no rain until the seventh month of autumn.
The ancestral shrine's building collapsed.
What is the ancestral shrine?
It is the ancestral temple of the Duke of Lǔ.
Zhōu Gōng called it the Grand Temple,
the Duke of Lǔ called it the Ancestral Hall,
other lords called it the palace.
This is the ancestral temple of the Duke of Lǔ.
Why is it called the Ancestral Hall?
Ancestral Hall is just Ancestal Hall—
it means it endures, generation after generation, and is not destroyed.
Why did Zhōu Gōng call it the Grand Temple in Lǔ?
He enfeoffed the Duke of Lǔ in the position of Zhōu Gōng.
Zhōu Gōng paid homage in front;
the Duke of Lǔ paid homage in the rear.
It is said:
“While alive, he nourished Zhōu Gōng;
when dead, he served as attendant to Zhōu Gōng.”
If so, was Zhōu Gōng in Lǔ?
It is said: “He was not in Lǔ.
He enfeoffed the Duke of Lǔ as Zhōu Gōng.”
Then why did Zhōu Gōng not go to Lǔ?
Because he wished the world to be unified towards Zhōu.
With what offerings did Lǔ make sacrifices to Zhōu Gōng?
Zhōu Gōng used a white bull;
the Duke of Lǔ used a red ox.
The other lords did not shave (the victims).
Why were sacrifices to Zhōu Gōng in Lǔ considered grand?
Zhōu Gōng was grand;
the Duke of Lǔ illuminated;
the other lords only supplied stores.
Why is the collapse of the ancestral shrine recorded?
To censure.
Censure for what?
For long neglect.
In winter,
the duke went to Jìn.
The Marquis of Wèi convened a meeting at Tà.
The Dí invaded Wèi.
On the jǐchǒu day of the twelfth month,
the duke and the Marquis of Jìn made a covenant.
Returned from Jìn.
The Duke of Zhèng convened the duke at Fěi.
What does “returned” mean?
It is a term of approval.
Why is it considered good?
Going aligns with the faction (party);
the Marquis of Wèi convened the duke at Tà,
thereby he was able to covenant with the Marquis of Jìn.
Returning aligns with the faction;
the Duke of Zhèng convened the duke at Fěi,
thus it is considered good.
In the fourteenth year, spring, in the king's first month,
the duke returned from Jìn.
The people of Zhūlóu attacked our southern borders.
Uncle Péngshēng led an army to attack Zhūlóu.
On the yǐhài day of the fifth month in summer,
the Marquis Pān of Qí passed away.
In the sixth month,
the duke met with the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Chén, the Marquis of Wèi, the Duke of Zhèng, the Man of Xǔ, the Earl of Cáo, and Zhào Dùn of Jìn.
On the guǐyǒu day,
they formed an alliance at Xīnchéng.
In the seventh month of autumn,
a comet entered the constellation Běidǒu (the Northern Dipper).
What is a comet?
It is a huìxīng (broom star).
What does it mean that it entered Běidǒu?
Běidǒu has a center.
Why is this recorded?
