It is to chronicle an anomaly.
The duke returned from the meeting.
The people of Jìn attempted to install Jiēzī in Zhūlóu,
but were unable to accomplish it.
What does “install” mean?
It means “to put forward a candidate.”
What does “were unable to install” mean?
It means it was a major failure.
How was their failure great?
Xì Quē of Jìn led an army of eight hundred war chariots to install Jiēzī in Zhūlóu;
their force was strong, seemingly with surplus strength, and installed him.
The people of Zhūlóu said:
“Jiēzī is backed by Jìn;
Guóqiě is backed by Qí.
If you count by their designation,
then Jiēzī is fourth,
Guóqiě is sixth.
If you wield the prestige of a great state to press the matter,
still, one cannot yet know whether Qí or Jìn will possess it.
If noble, then all are noble;
even so,
Guóqiě is elder.”
Xì Quē said:
“It is not that my strength cannot install him;
it is that righteousness truly does not permit it.”
He withdrew his army and abandoned the effort.
Therefore gentlemen say their failure to install was great.
This Xì Quē of Jìn—
why is he referred to without title?
It is to denigrate him.
Why denigrate?
Because he did not act in concert with the grandee when deposing and installing the lord.
Why not act in concert?
He did so in fact, but the record does not say so.
Why does the record not say so?
Because a grandee cannot by right solely depose and install the ruler.
On the jiǎshēn day of the ninth month,
Gōngsūn Áo died in Qí.
Gōngzǐ Shāngrén of Qí murdered his lord Shè.
This was a ruler of less than a year’s reign.
What is the meaning of “murdered his lord Shè”?
He installed him himself,
then killed him himself:
making the dead honored and the living base.
Zi'āi of Sòng fled and came here.
Who is Zi'āi of Sòng?
He is simply unknown.
In winter,
Shān Bó went to Qí,
the people of Qí seized Shān Bó,
and the people of Qí seized Zǐ Shūjī.
Why is it that sometimes when someone is seized, they are called by the title “envoy,” and sometimes not?
When titled as envoy and seized,
it is because they were seized in the course of their mission.
When not titled as envoy,
it is because he was seized for his own fault.
What was Shān Bó’s crime?
Licentious conduct.
How was it licentious?
He was licentious with Zǐ Shūjī.
Why then does it not record “the people of Qí seized Shān Bó and Zǐ Shūjī”?
It is an internal expression,
to make it appear as if they were guilty of different offences.
In the fifteenth year, in the spring,
Jì Sūn Xíngfù went to Jìn.
In the third month,
the Sīmǎ Huá Sūn of Sòng came to swear an alliance.
In summer,
the Earl of Cáo came to pay court.
The people of Qí returned the funeral of Gōngsūn Áo.
Why is it not said “came”?
It is an internal statement.
They threatened us and then returned it,
thus acting as if coming.
On Xīnchǒu, the first day of the sixth month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
Sacrificial animals were beaten at the altar of the soil.
The Earl of Shān returned from Qí.
Xì Quē of Jìn led an army to attack Cài.
On Wùshēn,
they entered Cài.
It says “entered” and does not say “attacked”;
why does it here say “attacked”?
It refers to the day of arrival.
What day is it?
It is the day of arrival.
In autumn,
the people of Qí invaded our western borders.
Jì Sūn Xíngfù went to Jìn.
In winter, in the eleventh month,
the feudal lords swore an alliance at Hù.
In the twelfth month,
the people of Qí came bringing Zǐ Shū Jī back.
Why does it say “came”?
It was out of pity.
This person has committed a crime;
why have pity?
Parents toward their children,
even if they have committed crimes,
still behave as if unwilling for them to bear their crimes.
The Marquis of Qí invaded our western borders,
and then attacked Cáo,
entering its outer wall.
What is the outer wall?
It is the expanded city wall.
Is entering the outer wall recorded?
It is said, it is not recorded.
Since entering the outer wall is not recorded,
why is it recorded here?
It was an action against us.
What is an action against us?
It is an internal statement.
In truth, it was our people who moved in response.
In the sixteenth year, in the spring,
Jì Sūn Xíngfù met with the Marquis of Qí at Yánggǔ;
the Marquis of Qí did not reach an alliance.
Why does it say “did not reach an alliance”?
He did not meet to make an alliance.
In summer, in the fifth month,
the Duke did not observe the new moon four times.
Why did the Duke four times not observe the new moon?
The Duke was ill.
Why mention the Duke did not observe the new moon due to illness?
From this on, whenever the Duke was not ill, he observed the new moon.
Then why does it not state the Duke was not ill but did not observe the new moon?
It is acceptable to state illness,
but not to state there was no illness.
On Wùchén in the sixth month,
Prince Suì and the Marquis of Qí swore an alliance at Xīqiū.
In autumn, on Xīnwèi in the eighth month,
the Lady Jiāng died.
The Spring Terrace was demolished.
What is the Spring Terrace?
It is the Lang Terrace.
If it is the Lang Terrace, why call it the Spring Terrace?
Before completion, it is called the Lang Terrace;
after completion, it is called the Spring Terrace.
Why is the demolition of the Spring Terrace recorded?
It is reproach.
Why reproach?
For building it, reproach;
for demolishing it, reproach.
Our former rulers built it;
we demolished it ourselves;
it would have been better not to dwell in it at all.
The people of Chǔ, Qín, and Bā destroyed Yōng.
In winter, in the eleventh month,
the people of Sòng assassinated their ruler Chǔ Jiū.
When a ruler is assassinated, why is the assassin sometimes named,
and sometimes unnamed?
If a grandee assassinates the ruler, the name is stated;
if one of low rank, all the people are named;
if grandees kill one another, they are simply called “people”;
if those of low rank, all are called “bandits”.
In the seventeenth year, in the spring,
the people of Jìn, Wèi, Chén, and Zhèng attacked Sòng.
In summer, on Guǐhài, the fourth month,
our Young Lady Shèng Jiāng was buried.
Who is Shèng Jiāng?
She is the mother of Duke Wén.
The Marquis of Qí attacked our western borders.
On Guǐwèi in the sixth month,
the Duke and the Marquis of Qí swore an alliance at Gǔ.
The feudal lords gathered at Hù.
In autumn,
the Duke returned from Gǔ.
In winter,
Prince Suì went to Qí.
In the eighteenth year, in the royal second month, on Dīngchǒu,
the Duke died beneath the Terrace.
The Earl of Qín, Yīng, died.
In summer, on Wùxū, the fifth month,
the people of Qí assassinated their ruler Shāng Rén.
On Guǐyǒu in the sixth month,
our ruler Duke Wén was buried.
In autumn,
Prince Suì and Shū Sūn Déchén went to Qí.
In winter, in the tenth month,
the “Son” died.
Who is said to be the “Son” who died?
It refers to Zǐ Chì.
Why is the date not recorded?
It is concealed.
Why is it concealed?
He was murdered.
If he was murdered, why is the date not recorded?
It is unbearable to mention.
Lady Jiāng returned to Qí.
Jì Sūn Xíngfù went to Qí.
Jǔ assassinated its ruler Shùqí.
Why name the state in cases of assassination?
To name the state in an assassination
is the phrase used when many assassinate their ruler.
In the first year, in the royal first month of spring,
the Duke came to the throne.
After following on from a murdered ruler, it does not say “came to the throne”;
why does it now say “came to the throne”?
It is as according to intention.
Prince Suì went to Qí to receive the bride.
In the third month,
then Lady Fù Jiāng returned from Qí.
Why is Suì not referred to as "prince"?
If one appears twice in a single matter,
then the final mention is by name.
Why is the lady not called "Jiāng-shì"?
It is a reduction.
Why reduce her title?
It is to criticize the taking of a wife during mourning.
He who marries during mourning is a duke,
so why is the lady’s title reduced?
Within, there is no way to reduce the duke.

It is the language of a daughter-in-law, with a mother-in-law.

In antiquity, when a grandee left,

If the ruler banishes him, it is not proper;

In ancient times, when a minister was in deep mourning,

Zhào Dùn murdered his lord;

The one who personally slew the ruler was Zhào Chuān;
the one who personally slew the ruler was Zhào Chuān;

Because he did not punish the traitor.

The historiographer of Jìn recorded the traitor, saying:

The historiographer replied:

someone killed your ruler,

If this is not murdering the ruler, what is it?”
How did Zhào Dùn return to the state?
Duke Líng was without principle;
he made all the high officials attend the inner court,
then he sat atop the tower,
pulling arrows to shoot at them,
himself darting aside to avoid the missiles,
taking pleasure in it alone.
After Zhào Dùn had finished attending court and exited,
he stood in the court with the other high officials,
and there was a man carrying a dustpan
coming out from the women’s quarters.
Zhào Dùn said:
“What is he doing?
Why is that dustpan coming out from the women’s quarters?”
They called out to him but he did not answer.
He said:
“You are a high official;
if you wish to see for yourself, go and look.”
Zhào Dùn went to look,
and there was a glaringly dead man.
Zhào Dùn said:
“What is this?”
He replied:
“A cook.
The bear’s paw was undercooked,
the duke became angry,
used a ladle to strike and kill him,
dismembered him,
and now wants me to throw him out.”
Zhào Dùn said:
“Alas!”
He hurried in.
Duke Líng, seeing that Zhào Dùn had complained, bowed twice.
Zhào Dùn slowly faced north, bowed twice, and knocked his head on the ground,
then hurried out.
Duke Líng felt ashamed in his heart,
and wanted to kill him.
Thereupon he sent a certain warrior to go kill him.
The warrior entered his main gate,
but there was no one guarding the gate;
he entered the inner quarters,
but there was no one in the inner quarters;
he went up into the hall,
but there was no one there.
Looking down and peering through the door,
he saw Zhào Dùn eating fish and soup.
The warrior said:
“Alas!
You truly are a benevolent man!
I entered your main gate,
and there was no one;
I entered your inner quarters,
and there was no one;
I went up to your hall,
and there was no one;
this is your easygoing nature.
You are a chief minister of Jìn but eat fish and soup;
this is your frugality.
The ruler ordered me to kill you,
but I cannot bring myself to do so.
Even so,
I cannot face my lord again.”
And so he cut his throat and died.
When Duke Líng heard of it,
he was enraged.
His desire to kill Zhào Dùn grew all the more intense,
but there was no one among the people willing to go.
Thereupon he set an ambush in the palace,
summoned Zhào Dùn to dine with him.
Zhào Dùn’s charioteer, Qí Mí Míng,
the strongest man in the state,
alertly followed Zhào Dùn inside,

When Zhào Dùn had finished eating,

“I have heard your sword is said to be a sharp sword;
show it to me,
I wish to see it.”
Zhào Dùn arose,
about to draw his sword,
Qí Mí Míng called out from below:
“When Dùn finishes dining, he departs;
why do you draw your sword in the presence of the ruler?”
Zhào Dùn understood,
hesitated on the steps and ran.
Duke Líng had a Zhou hound,
called an áo;
he called the hound and set it on him;
the hound too leapt up the stairs and pursued him.
Qí Mí Míng intercepted and kicked it,

Zhào Dùn looked back and said:

Nevertheless, in the palace the armed soldiers rose up beating drums,

Zhào Dùn looked back and said:

He replied:

Zhào Dùn said:

He replied:

Since you are already mounted,

Zhào Dùn galloped out,

Zhào Chuān, taking advantage of the people’s displeasure,

stood with him in the court,

locusts.

King Zhuāng said:

they were not pardoned if it was not proper;
by acting with what is not proper, I would mislead the people,

Afterwards, the army of Jìn which came to the rescue of Zhèng arrived,

the grandees acted in his stead.
Why was the meeting still held?
Because there was no shame in it.
Why was there no shame?
Because the duke was young.
The duke met with Yǐn Zǐ, the Marquis of Jìn, Guó Zuǒ of Qí, and people of Zhūlóu to attack Zhèng.
The Earl of Cáo returned from the capital.
When one is seized and returned, the name is given;
why is the Earl of Cáo not named?
And why does it not say, "returned again to Cáo"?
Because it was easy.
How was it easy?
Because at the time Gōngzǐ Xǐ was within.
If Gōngzǐ Xǐ was within at the time, why was it easy?
Because Gōngzǐ Xǐ was a benevolent man.
He governed the state peacefully within,
handled affairs in the capital, and allowed him to escape.
Why does it say, "from the capital"?
It means it was extremely easy,
apart from this, there was no difficulty.
In the ninth month,
the Jìn people seized Jìsūn Xíngfù,
and released him at Zhāoqiū.
Previously, when someone was seized, there had not been the saying “released,”
so why was “released” said in this case?
It was done out of benevolence.
It is said, “He was resting at Zhāoqiū.”
Until now, “out of benevolence” had not been said of one released;
so why is it said here?
It was a substitute for imprisoning the ruler.
How was it substituting for imprisoning the ruler?
Previously, the people of Jìn came to request military assistance, but it was not granted;
the ruler met with the Marquis of Jìn,
and the Jìn were about to seize the ruler.
Jìsūn Xíngfù said,
“This is my crime.”
Thereupon they seized Jìsūn Xíngfù.
Later, Chéng Gōng was about to meet with Jìn Lì Gōng,
but the meeting was not at the appointed time,
and they were about to seize the ruler.
Jìsūn Xíngfù said,
“I have committed an offense;
they seize his ruler.
You have committed an offense;
they seize your father.
This is a grave misjudgment in listening to reports.
Now it is my own offense;
instead of punishing me,
you would seize my ruler.
I fear that this misjudgment brings shame to the ancestral temple.”
So they seized Jìsūn Xíngfù.
In the tenth month of winter, on yǐhài day,

In the twelfth month, on yǐchǒu day,

The ruler returned from the meeting.
On yǐyǒu day,
Gōngzǐ Yǎn was assassinated.
In the seventeenth year, in spring,
Wèi Běigōng Jié led an army to invade Zhèng.

the ruler met with Yǐn Zǐ, Shàn Zǐ, the Marquis of Jìn, the Marquis of Qí, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Cáo, and the people of Zhūlóu to attack Zhèng.
In the sixth month, on yǐyǒu day,

Qí Gāo Wújiù fled to Jǔ.
In the ninth month, on xīchǒu day,
the suburban sacrifice was performed.
Why was it performed?
It should not have been performed,
the ninth month was not the proper time for the suburban sacrifice.
Then why was the sacrifice performed?
The proper time is the first xīn day of the first month;
some say the sacrifice should be performed only after there is a reason.
The Marquis of Jìn sent Xún Yīng to request military aid.
In winter,
the ruler met with Shàn Zǐ, the Marquis of Jìn, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Cáo, the people of Qí, and the people of Zhūlóu to attack Zhèng.

On rénshēn day,
Gōngsūn Yīngqí died at Lízhěn.
It was not this month or day;
why was his death recorded with this date?
One waits for the ruler's command to allow the death of a Dàfū to be recorded.
Why is the command needed?
Earlier, Yīngqí fled to Jìn,
the ruler met the Marquis of Jìn,

Yīngqí pleaded for the ruler,
and the ruler allowed him to return and serve again as Dàfū.
He returned and died at Lízhěn.
Without the ruler's command, it was not permitted to record the death of a Dàfū.
When the ruler returned,
he said,
“I had already promised he would return as Dàfū.”
Only then was his death recorded.

Jìn killed its Dàfū: Xì Qí, Xì Zhōu, and Xì Zhì.

Jìn assassinated its ruler Zhōupú.

In the eighth month, the Viscount of Zhūlóu came for an audience.
A deer park was built.

To censure.

There was already a park,

On jǐchǒu day,

The Marquis of Jìn sent Shì Péng to request military aid.

Zhòngsūn Miè met with the Marquis of Jìn, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Viscount of Zhūlóu, and Qí Cuī Zhù to swear an alliance at Xūzhēng.
On dīngwèi day,
our late ruler Chéng Gōng was buried.
The first year, spring, in the king’s first month,
the ruler ascended the throne.
Zhòngsūn Miè met Jìn Luán Yǎn, Sòng Huá Yuán, Wèi Níng Zhí, and people of Cáo, Jǔ, Zhūlóu, Téng, and Xuē to besiege Sòng’s Péngchéng.
Why did Sòng Huá Yuán, as Sòng, help the other lords besiege Péngchéng?
It was to punish Sòng.
How was it a punishment?
Yúshí fled to Chǔ;
Chǔ, on his account, attacked Sòng
and captured Péngchéng to enfeoff Yúshí.
What was Yúshí’s offense?
Causing this occupation was his offense.
Chǔ had already captured it;
why was it returned to Sòng?
Because it cannot be exclusively enfeoffed by one lord, not shared with the other lords.
In summer,

In the ninth month, on xīnyǒu day,
the Son of Heaven died.

The Marquis of Jìn sent Xún Yīng to present gifts.

King Jiǎn was buried.
The Zhèng army attacked Sòng.
In the fifth month of summer, on Gēngyín day,

In the sixth month, on Gēngchén day,

The Jìn army, the Sòng army, and Wèi Nìngzhí invaded Zhèng.
In autumn, seventh month,
Zhòngsūn Miè met with Jìn Xún Yīng, Sòng Huá Yuán, Wèi Sūn Línfù, the people of Cáo, and the people of Zhūlóu at Qī.
On Jǐchǒu day,
we buried our Lesser Lady Qí Jiāng.
Who was Qí Jiāng?
As for Qí Jiāng and Miù Jiāng, is it still unknown whether she was Lady Xuān or
Lady Chéng?
Shūsūn Bào went to Sòng.

Zhòngsūn Miè met with Jìn Xún Yīng, Qí Cuī Zhù, Sòng Huá Yuán, Wèi Sūn Línfù, the people of Cáo, the people of Zhūlóu, the people of Téng, the people of Xuē, and the people of Xiǎo Zhūlóu at Qī,
and then fortified Hǔláo.
What is Hǔláo?
It is a city of Zhèng.
Why does the text say "fortified" it?
It means "seizing" it.
If it means seizing, then why not say "seize"?
Because in the Central States it is taboo.
Why is it taboo in the Central States?
Taboo against mentioning attacking the bereaved.
Why is it not connected to Zhèng?
Because of the taboo in the Central States.
The nobles did not "carry through" the affair,
so why does the text use "then"?
It attributes the blame to the nobles.
Chǔ killed its noble Gōngzǐ Shēn.
9.3 "The Third Year of Duke Xiāng"
In the third year, spring,

Jǔ was about to destroy it,

To obtain a successor after Jǔ.

he died at Cāo.
What is Cāo?

When feudal lords die within their own fiefs but not on campaign,
why is it recorded as being on campaign?
It is to conceal the truth.
Why conceal it?
Because it was murder.
Who murdered him?
His own minister murdered him.
Why is it not recorded as his minister murdering him?
It was an act of taboo in the Central States.
Why this taboo in the Central States?
The Earl of Zhèng was about to assemble the feudal lords at Wéi,
when his minister remonstrated, saying,
“The Central States are not worthy to take refuge in;
then it would be better to rely on Chǔ.”
The Earl of Zhèng replied,
“That cannot be.”
His minister said,
“If you take the Central States for righteousness,
then they will attack us while we are in mourning;
if you take the Central States for strength,
then Chǔ is the wiser choice.”
Thereupon, he murdered him.
As for the name Kūnyuán, why is it used?
He was wounded and fled,
but died before reaching his lodging.
Since he did not meet the feudal lords,

It conveys his intent.

Why is it sometimes called ‘calamity’?

When not called ‘fire’ for domestic incidents,

To record calamity.

Because the royal descendants record calamity.

the Lord of Qí attacked our northern border,

the Lord of Jìn Zhōu died.

the gōng met with the Lord of Jìn, Lord of Sòng, Lord of Wèi, Earl of Zhèng, Earl of Cáo, Lord of Jǔ, Lord of Zhūlóu, Earl of Xuē, Earl of Qǐ, and Lord of Xiǎo Zhūlóu at Júlíang.

the Lord of Qí attacked our northern border,
and besieged Chéng.
A great sacrificial rain ceremony was held.
In winter,
Shū Sūnbào went to Jìn.
In the seventeenth year, in the royal second month, on gēngwǔ day,
the Lord of Zhūlóu Jiàn died.
People of Sòng attacked Chén.
In summer,
Wèi Shí Mǎi led troops to attack Cáo.
In autumn,
the Lord of Qí attacked our northern border,
and besieged Táo.
Qí Gāo Hòu led troops to attack our northern border,
and besieged Fáng.
In the ninth month,
a great sacrificial rain ceremony was held.
Sòng Huá Chén fled to Chén.
In winter,
the people of Zhūlóu attacked our southern border.
In the eighteenth year, in spring,
the Bái Dí came.
Who are the Bái Dí?
They are rulers among the Yí and Dí.
Why is it not called “audience at court”?
Because they could not make court visits.
In summer,
the people of Jìn seized the Wèi messenger Shí Mǎi.
In autumn,
the Qí army attacked our northern border.
In winter, in the tenth month,

the gōng met with the Lord of Jìn, Lord of Sòng, Lord of Wèi, Earl of Zhèng, Earl of Cáo, Lord of Jǔ, Lord of Zhūlóu, Lord of Téng, Earl of Xuē, Earl of Qǐ, and Lord of Xiǎo Zhūlóu to surround Qí together.
The Earl of Cáo Fùchú died in the army.
Chǔ Prince Wǔ led troops to attack Zhèng.
In the spring of the nineteenth year, the royal first month,
the feudal lords formed an alliance at Zhù’ē.
The people of Jìn seized the lord of Zhūlóu.
The duke returned from the campaign against Qí.
This was a joint siege of Qí,
but what caused the campaign?
The siege of Qí had not yet occurred.
If Qí had not yet been besieged, why does it mention besieging Qí?
It was to check Qí.
Why check Qí?
Because they frequently attacked.
Some say it was because of their arrogance and insolence,
for their heir took a place above the other feudal lords.
They took the fields of Zhūlóu from the Huò River.
Why does it say from the Huò River?
Because the Huò was the border.
Why say that the Huò was the border?
Huò means to shift.
Jì Sūnsù went to Jìn.
Cáo Chénggōng was buried.
In summer,
Wèi Sūn Línfù led troops to attack Qí.
In autumn, seventh month, on Xīnmǎo day,
the marquis of Qí, Yuàn, died.
Jìn Shì Gài led troops to attack Qí,
reaching Gǔ,
and hearing of the death of the marquis of Qí,
then returned.
What is meant by returned?
It signifies good form in wording.
Why call it good?
It gave importance to not attacking the bereaved.
He had received orders from the ruler to attack Qí—
so why stress not attacking the bereaved?
The grandee leaves by the ruler’s command,
but advances or withdraws at his own discretion.
On the day Bǐngchén in the eighth month,
Zhòngsūn Miè died.
Qí killed its grandee Gāo Hòu.
Zhèng killed its grandee Gōngzǐ Xǐ.
In winter,
Qí Línggōng was buried.
The western outer city wall was built.
Shūsūn Bào met with Jìn Shì Gài at Kē.
Wǔchéng city was built.
In the twentieth year, the royal first month on the day Xīnhài,
Zhòngsūn Sù met with the people of Jǔ,
and formed an alliance at Xiàng.
In the sixth month of summer, on the day Gēngshēn,

the duke met with the marquis of Jìn, the marquis of Qí, the duke of Sòng, the marquis of Wèi, the earl of Zhèng, the earl of Cáo, the viscount of Jǔ, the viscount of Zhūlóu, the viscount of Téng, the earl of Xuē, the earl of Qǐ, and the lesser viscount of Zhūlóu,
and they formed an alliance at Chányuān.
In autumn,
the duke returned from the meeting.
Zhòngsūn Sù led troops to attack Zhūlóu.
Cài killed its grandee Gōngzǐ Xiè.
Cài Gōngzǐ Lǚ fled to Chǔ.
Chén Hóu’s younger brother Guāng fled to Chǔ.
Shūlǎo went to Qí.
In winter, on the day Bǐngchén, the first day of the tenth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Jì Sūnsù went to Sòng.
In the twenty-first year, the royal first month,
the duke went to Jìn.
Zhūlóu Shùqí came in flight to Lǔ, bringing with him Qī and Lüqīu.
Who was Zhūlóu Shùqí?
A grandee of Zhūlóu.
Zhūlóu had no grandee;
why was this recorded?
Because of the importance of the territory.
In summer,
the duke returned from Jìn.
In autumn,
Jìn Luán Yíng fled to Chǔ.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngxū, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In winter, on the day Gēngchén, the first day of the tenth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
The earl of Cáo came for court audience.
The duke met with the marquis of Jìn, marquis of Qí, duke of Sòng, marquis of Wèi, earl of Zhèng, earl of Cáo, viscount of Jǔ, viscount of Zhūlóu at Shāngrèn.
On the day Gēngzǐ in the eleventh month,
Kǒngzǐ was born.
In the twenty-second year, the royal first month,
the duke returned from the meeting.
In the fourth month of summer.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Shūlǎo died.
In winter,

the duke met with the marquis of Jìn, marquis of Qí, duke of Sòng, marquis of Wèi, earl of Zhèng, earl of Cáo, viscount of Jǔ, viscount of Zhūlóu, viscount of Téng, earl of Xuē, earl of Qǐ, and lesser viscount of Zhūlóu at Shāsuí.
The duke returned from the meeting.
Chǔ killed its grandee Gōngzǐ Zhuīshū.
In the twenty-third year, royal second month, on the day Guǐyǒu, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Third month, Jǐsì day,
Qǐ Bó Gài died.
In summer,
Zhūlóu Bǐwǒ came in flight to Lǔ.
Who was Zhūlóu Bǐwǒ?
A grandee of Zhūlóu.
Zhūlóu had no grandee;
why was this recorded?
Because it was near in time.
Qǐ Xiào Gōng was buried.
Chén killed its grandees Qìng Hǔ and Qìng Yín.
Chén Hóu’s younger brother Guāng returned to Chén from Chǔ.
Jìn Luán Yíng re-entered Jìn,
entering Qǔwò.
What is Qǔwò?
A settlement of Jìn.
Why does it say entered Jìn,
then entered Qǔwò?
Luán Yíng was about to enter Jìn,
the people of Jìn did not accept him,
so he entered through Qǔwò.
In autumn,
the marquis of Qí attacked Wèi,
then attacked Jìn.
In the eighth month,
Shūsūn Bào led troops to aid Jìn,
encamping at Yōngyú.
Why does it first mention aiding, then mention encamping?
To convey the duke's command first.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Zhòngsūn Sù died.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Yǐhài,
Zāng Sūn Hé fled to Zhūlóu.
The people of Jìn killed Luán Yíng.
Why does it not say they killed their grandee?
He was not their grandee.
The marquis of Qí attacked Jǔ by surprise.
In the twenty-fourth year, in spring,
Shūsūn Bào went to Jìn.
Zhòngsūn Jié led his army to invade Qí.
In summer,
the Lord of Chǔ attacked Wú.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Jiǎzǐ, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse;
it was total.
Cuī Zhù of Qí led his army to attack Jǔ.
There was a great flood.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐsì, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.

The Duke met with the Lord of Jìn, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Zhèng, the Earl of Cáo, the Lord of Jǔ, the Lord of Zhūlóu, the Lord of Téng, the Earl of Xuē, the Earl of Qǐ, and the Lord of Xiǎo Zhūlóu at Chén Yí.
In winter,
the Lord of Chǔ, the Marquis of Cài, the Marquis of Chén, and the Viscount of Xǔ attacked Zhèng.
The Duke returned from the meeting.
Chén Zhēn Yíjiù fled to Chǔ.
Shūsūn Bào went to the capital.
There was a great famine.
In the twenty-fifth year, in spring,
Cuī Zhù of Qí led his army to attack our northern border.
In summer, in the fifth month, on the day Yǐhài,
Cuī Zhù of Qí murdered his lord Guāng.

The Duke met with the Lord of Jìn, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Wèi, the Earl of Zhèng, the Earl of Cáo, the Lord of Jǔ, the Lord of Zhūlóu, the Lord of Téng, the Earl of Xuē, the Earl of Qǐ, and the Lord of Xiǎo Zhūlóu at Chén Yí.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Zhèng Gōngsūn Shězhī led his army into Chén.
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the day Jǐsì,
the feudal lords formed a covenant at Zhòngqiū.
The Duke returned from the meeting.
The Marquis of Wèi entered Chén Yí.
What is Chén Yí?
It is a town of Wèi.
Why is it not said that he entered Wèi?
Because Lord Xuān was murdered.
Qū Jiàn of Chǔ led his army to destroy Shūjiū.
In winter,
Zhèng Gōngsūn Chài led his army to attack Chén.
In the twelfth month,
the Lord of Wú, Yè, attacked Chǔ,
and died at the city gate at Cháo.
He died at the city gate at Cháo—which means what?
He entered the gate at Cháo and died.
To enter the gate at Cháo and die—what does this mean?
It means he died at the gate of Cháo.
How did the Lord of Wú come by such a name?
He was wounded and returned,
but before reaching his quarters, he died.
In the twenty-sixth year, in the second month of the royal calendar, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Nìng Xǐ of Wèi murdered his lord Piāo.
Sūn Línfù of Wèi entered Qī to rebel.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Marquis of Wèi, Kàn, returned to Wèi.
This was because Lord Xuān was murdered.
Why is it said “returned”?
Because Piāo was detested.
Why was Piāo detested?
There was no one who approved Piāo’s accession.
Then why is it not said “established Piāo”?
It is not said “established Piāo”
because the Marquis of Wèi was hated.
In summer,
the Lord of Jìn sent Xún Wú as an envoy.
The Duke met with the men of Jìn, Liáng Xiāo of Zhèng, the men of Sòng, and the men of Cáo at Chányuān.
In autumn,
the Duke of Sòng killed his heir apparent, Cuó.
The men of Jìn seized Wèi Nìng Xǐ.
This was the seizure of someone guilty;
why could they not execute him as the hegemon?
Because they did not seize him for his crime.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
the Viscount of Xǔ, Nìng, died in Chǔ.
In winter,
the Lord of Chǔ, the Marquis of Cài, and the Marquis of Chén attacked Zhèng.
They buried Xǔ Línggōng.
In the twenty-seventh year, in spring,
the Lord of Qí sent Qìng Fēng to act as envoy.
In summer,
Shūsūn Bào met Zhào Wǔ of Jìn, Qū Jiàn of Chǔ, Gōngsūn Guīshēng of Cài, Shí È of Wèi, Kǒng Yuàn of Chén, Liáng Xiāo of Zhèng, men of Xǔ, and men of Cáo at Sòng.
Wèi killed its grandee Nìng Xǐ,
and the Duke of Wèi's younger brother, Tuán, fled to Jìn.
Since Wèi killed its grandee Nìng Xǐ,
why did the Duke of Wèi's younger brother Tuán flee to Jìn?
He fled because of the killing of Nìng Xǐ.
Why did he flee because of the killing of Nìng Xǐ?
Wèi Nìng Zhí and Sūn Línfù drove out the Marquis of Wèi and installed Gōngsūn Piāo,
Nìng Zhí fell ill and was about to die,
and said to Xǐ:
“It was not my intention to depose the Marquis;
it was the Sūn family’s doing.
If I die,
can you surely restore the Duke?”
Xǐ said:
“Yes.”
Nìng Zhí died,
and Xǐ became a grandee.
He sent someone to say to Duke Xiàn:
“It was not the Nìng family that deposed the Duke;
it was the Sūn family who did it.
I wish to restore you. What do you think?”
Duke Xiàn said:
“If you truly wish to restore me,
I request we swear an oath.”
Xǐ said:
“There is no need for oaths;
please have Prince Tuán agree to it.”
Duke Xiàn said to Prince Tuán:
“The Nìng family wishes to restore me,
I wish to make an oath with them.
He says:
‘There is no need for oaths;
please have Prince Tuán agree to it.’
You must surely make this agreement for me.”
Prince Tuán replied:
“To be bound and chained, to bear the axe and go wherever the lord commands—this is the business of ministers and inferiors.
But as for making agreements to establish faith, that is not something inferiors dare to do.”
Duke Xiàn angrily said:
“It was not the Nìng or Sūn families who deposed me;
it was all of you together.”
Prince Tuán had no choice but to agree;
having agreed,
he returned,
arrived,
and killed Nìng Xǐ.
Prince Tuán took his wife and children and left;
about to cross the Yellow River,
he made an oath with his wife and children:
“If we ever tread Wèi’s soil or eat Wèi’s grain, let us meet our death before the wild pheasants.”
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
Bào and the grandees of the various lords swore an oath at Sòng.
Why is Bào mentioned again?
He was almost considered a feudal lord.
Why was he almost a feudal lord?
Because Shí È of Wèi was present;
it was thus said that “the band of wicked men was there.”
In winter, in the twelfth month, on the day Yǐhài, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the twenty-eighth year, in spring,
there was no ice.
In summer,
Shí È of Wèi fled to Jìn.
The Lord of Zhūlóu came to court.
In the eighth month of autumn,
the Grand Rain Sacrifice was held.
Zhòngsūn Jié went to Jìn.
In winter,
Qí Qìngfēng came fleeing.
In the eleventh month,
the Duke went to Chǔ.
On the jiǎyín day of the twelfth month,
the Son of Heaven passed away.
On the jǐwèi day,
the Lord Zhāo of Chǔ died.
In the twenty-ninth year, in spring, in the royal first month,
the Duke was in Chǔ.
Why does the text say the Duke was in Chǔ?
Because in the first month, he was preserving the ruler.
In the fifth month of summer,
the Duke returned from Chǔ.
On the gēngwǔ day,
the Lord Kǎn of Wèi died.
Yǎn murdered Yújì, the Prince of Wú.
Who is Yǎn?
One of the retainers,
a criminal.
If he is a criminal, why call him Yǎn?
He is not truly a criminal.
A gentleman does not associate with criminals;
to associate with criminals is to treat death lightly.

Zhòngsūn Jié, together with Jìn Xún Yíng, Qí Gāozhǐ, Sòng Huádìng, Wèi Shìshū Qí, Zhèng Gōngsūn Duàn, men from Cáo, men from Jǔ, men from Zhūlóu, men from Téng, men from Xuē, men from xiǎo Zhūlóu, built the city at Qǐ.
The Lord of Jìn sent Shì Yǎng to pay a diplomatic visit.
The Prince of Qǐ came to form an alliance.
The Lord of Wú sent Zhǎ to pay a diplomatic visit.
Wú has no ruler, no minister;
why, then, does it have ruler and minister?
Because of the worthiness of Jìzǐ.
Why is Jìzǐ considered worthy?
Because he yielded the state.
How did he yield the state?
Xié, Yújì, Yímèi, and Jìzǐ were four who shared the same mother;
Jìzǐ was the youngest and most talented;
all the brothers loved him;
they all wished to establish him as ruler;
Xié said:
“Even now, if we were to forcibly give the state to Jìzǐ,
he would still not accept it.
Let us not give it to him but to our younger brother,
and have the brothers succeed one another as ruler,
and so eventually confer the state on Jìzǐ.”
All agreed, saying:
“Very well.”
Therefore, all who became rulers
regarded death lightly for the sake of valor.
At meals they always made vows,
saying:
“If Heaven wishes there to be a state of Wú,
may misfortune swiftly come upon me.”
Thus Xié died;
Yújì ascended.
When Yújì died,
Yímèi ascended.
When Yímèi died,
the one to whom the state should belong was Jìzǐ.
Jìzǐ was sent abroad and stayed away.
Liáo, being the eldest of the secondary sons,
moved to take the throne;
but when Jìzǐ was sent for and returned,
he arrived and was made ruler.
Hélú said:
“The reason the former lord gave the state to the younger brothers and not to you was
entirely because of Jìzǐ.
If we are to follow the former lord’s command,
then the state rightfully belongs to Jìzǐ;
if not,
then I am the rightful one to establish.
How can Liáo become ruler?”
So he sent Zhuānzhū to assassinate Liáo,
and transferred the state to Jìzǐ.
Jìzǐ would not accept, saying:
“You murdered my lord;
if I accept the state from you,
then I am usurping along with you.
You killed my brother;
if I were then to kill you,
it would only mean father and son, brother and brother, would kill each other endlessly.”
He went to Yánlíng
and never entered Wú again for life.
Therefore, the gentleman regarded his refusal as righteousness,
and his not killing as benevolence.
If Jìzǐ is so worthy, how is it that Wú has a ruler and a minister?
Because with Jìzǐ as a minister,
there should certainly be a ruler.
Who is Zhǎ?
Zhǎ is the name of Jìzǐ of Wú.
In the *Spring and Autumn Annals*, the worthy are not named;
why is he named here?
Because what is permitted for the Yi and Di barbarians is not the same as for us.
Jìzǐ is one who is worthy;
why is that not sufficient for Jìzǐ?
If one acknowledges a subject, the subject must serve;
if one acknowledges a son, the son must serve as son.
In the ninth month of autumn,
the funeral of Wèi Xiàn Gōng was held.
Qí Gāozhǐ fled into exile in Běi Yān.
In winter,
Zhòngsūn Jié went to Jìn.
In the thirtieth year, in spring, in the royal first month,
the Lord of Chǔ sent Wěi Pō to pay a diplomatic visit.
In the fourth month of summer,
the crown prince Bān of Cài murdered his ruler Gù.
On the jiǎwǔ day of the fifth month,
there was a fire in Sòng,
and Bójī died.
The Son of Heaven killed his younger brother Niánfū.
Prince Xiá fled to Jìn.
In the seventh month of autumn,
Shū Gōng went to Sòng,
and buried Sòng Gòngjī.
It is unusual to record the burial of an outer consort;
why is it recorded here?
Because it was concealed.
Why concealed?
There was a fire in Sòng;
Bójī perished in it.
Why was she given a posthumous title?
Because she was worthy.
Why is she said to be worthy?
There was a fire in Sòng;
Bójī survived it.
The officials reported again:
“The fire is here;
let us leave.”
Bójī said:
“No.
I have heard
that when a woman goes out at night,
if she does not see her nurse, she shall not descend the stairs.
The nurse has arrived,
but mother has not yet come.”
She stayed and was overtaken by the fire and died.
Liángxiāo of Zhèng fled to Xǔ in exile,
returned from Xǔ to Zhèng,
and was killed by the people of Zhèng.
In the tenth month of winter,
the burial of Cài Jǐng Gōng was held.
The traitor had not yet been punished;
why was the burial recorded?
Because this is the way a gentleman speaks.
The people of Jìn, Qí, Sòng, Wèi, Zhèng, Cáo, Jǔ, Zhūlóu, Téng, Xuē, Qǐ, and Xiǎo Zhūlóu gathered at Chányuān,
because of the disaster in Sòng.
What is meant by "because of the disaster in Sòng"?
The various lords gathered at Chányuān
all for the sake of Sòng’s disaster.
At the meeting, none said their purpose;
why is it stated here what their purpose was?
It was to record the matter of Bójī.
The lords assembled,
and then changed what Sòng had lost,
saying, "The dead cannot come back to life,
but your wealth can be restored."
This was a great matter;
why send someone of low rank?
It was a qīng.
If it was a qīng, why refer to him as a 'person'?
It is a demotion.
Why a demotion?
A qīng should not worry about the affairs of the lords.
In the thirty-first year, in spring, in the king’s first month.
In summer, in the sixth month, on Xīnsì day,
the Duke died in the Chǔ palace.
In autumn, in the ninth month, on Guǐsì day,
Zǐ Yě died.
On Jǐhài day,
Zhòngsūn Jié died.
In winter, in the tenth month,
the Lord of Téng came to join in the burial.
On Guǐyǒu day,
our lord, Duke Xiāng, was buried.
In the eleventh month,
the people of Jǔ killed their ruler, Mìzhōu.
In the first year, in spring, the king’s first month,
the Duke ascended the throne.

Shūsūn Bào had a meeting at Kuò with Jìn’s Zhào Wǔ, Chǔ’s Gōngzǐ Wéi, Qí’s Guó Zhuó, Sòng’s Xiàng Xū, Wèi’s Shí È, Chén’s Gōngzǐ Zhāo, Cài’s Gōngsūn Guīshēng, Zhèng’s Xuān Hǔ, people of Xǔ, and people of Cáo.
This Zhāo was the brother of the Lord of Chén;
why is he not called ‘brother’?
It is a demotion.
Why a demotion?
He was demoted for killing the heir Yǎnshī,
for it says, "Zhāo, younger brother of Lord of Chén, killed the heir Yǎnshī of Chén."
When dàfū kill each other it is recorded with personal names;
why, in this case, is the full name and family name used for a killing?
It signifies that he will later murder his lord.
Now, it is as such;
why would the language equate a kin-killer with a lord-killer?
There must not be a lord-killer among relatives;
if there is, he must certainly be executed.
Then why is he not demoted at the time of the lord-killing?
If one murders his kin,
then the crime is great,
and the *Chūnqiū* need not record a demotion,
but when the record is cut off and the crime is thus made manifest,
not demoting but cutting off the record shows the crime.
If only by demotion or severance does the crime appear,
then it is demoted and severed to make the crime manifest.
Now Zhāo’s crime is already great,
why is he demoted again here?
To make clear that Zhāo is guilty.
How is it shown that Zhāo is guilty?
It says that Chǔ, under the pretense of punishing Zhāo, destroyed Chén.
In the third month, the town Yùn was taken.
What is Yùn?
It is an inner town.
Why does it say "taken"?
It was not granted.
In summer,
Zhēn, brother of the Lord of Qín, fled to Jìn.
Qín had no dàfū;
why is this written?
Because he served in Jìn.
Why serve in Jìn?
With a state that has a thousand chariots,
but cannot contain its own younger brother,
therefore the gentleman calls this "fleeing."
In the sixth month, on Dīngsì day,
Zǐ Huá, Lord of Zhūlóu, died.
Jìn’s Xún Wú led troops and defeated the Dí at Dàyuán.
This is Dàlǔ;
why is it called Dàyuán?
The name of the land follows Zhōngguó;
the name of the town’s people follows its lord;
What is "yuán"?
High flat land is called "yuán",
low flat land is called "xí".
In autumn,
Jǔ Qùjí entered Jǔ from Qí.
Jǔ Zhǎn fled to Wú.
Shūgōng led troops to determine the fields at Yùn.
What is "determining the fields at Yùn"?
It was to make the border with Jǔ.
If it was to make the border with Jǔ,
why lead troops there?
Out of fear of Jǔ.
Buried Duke Dào of Zhūlóu.
In winter, in the eleventh month, on Jǐyǒu day,
the Lord of Chǔ, Juǎn, died.
Gōngzǐ Bǐ of Chǔ fled to Jìn.
In the second year, in spring,
the Lord of Jìn sent Hán Qǐ to visit.
In summer,
Shūgōng went to Jìn.
In autumn,
Zhèng killed its dàfū Gōngsūn Hēi.
In winter,
the Duke went to Jìn,
but turned back upon reaching the Yellow River.
Why does it say "turned back upon reaching the River"?
He did not dare to proceed.
Jìsūn Sù went to Jìn.
In the third year, in spring, in the king’s first month, on Dīngwèi day,
Quán, Lord of Téng, died.
In summer,
Shūgōng went to Téng.
In the fifth month,
Duke Chéng of Téng was buried.
In autumn,
the Lord of Xiǎo Zhūlóu came to court.
In the eighth month,

Duke Zhāo planned to assassinate the Jì clan,

“The Jì clan has acted without virtue
and has usurped the authority of the ducal house for a long time.
What do you think if I were to assassinate them?”
Zǐ Jiā Jū replied:

and the great officers have long usurped that of the lords.”
Duke Zhāo said:

Zǐ Jiā Jū replied:
“You have constructed two towers,
ride in a grand carriage,
hold a vermillion staff,
bear a jade-adorned halberd,
and perform the ‘Great Xià’ dance,

All these are rites belonging to the Son of Heaven.
Moreover, oxen and horses—
even those with weak sinews are gentle.
The Jì clan has long held the majority among the people;
you, my lord, should not bring them much disgrace.”
Duke Zhāo did not follow his advice,
and in the end assassinated them but failed.
He fled to Qí,

He bowed twice, touching his forehead to the ground.
Kèng Zǐ Jiā Jū said:

Zǐ Jiā Jū replied:

has cast you into great trouble, my lord;
you could not bear to punish me with ax and saw,
but granted me death.”
He bowed twice,
and touched his forehead to the ground.
Gāo Zǐ offered a basket of food and four strips of dried meat;

saying:
“Our humble lord has heard you, my lord, are outside;
you have yet to complete a meal,
and I dare to offer dry provisions to your followers.”
Duke Zhāo said:
“Your lord does not forget my late lord,
and extends it even to this mourner,
bestowing upon me great ceremony.”
He bowed twice, with head to the ground, and received it kneeling with his robe.
Gāo Zǐ said:
“Such ill-omened people;
my lord, do not disgrace your grand ceremony.”
Duke Zhāo perhaps made a sacrifice but did not taste the food.
Duke Jǐng said:
“I, an unworthy one, have some modest robes from my late lord,
which I have not yet dared wear;
some modest vessels from my late lord,
which I have not yet dared use;
I dare to request your acceptance.”
Duke Zhāo said:
“This mourner, lacking talent,
lost and failed to guard the altars of Lǔ,
and has shamed your service;
I dare not disgrace your grand ceremony,
and must decline.”
Duke Jǐng said:
“I, an unworthy one, have some modest robes from my late lord,
which I have not yet dared wear;
some modest vessels from my late lord,
which I have not yet dared use;
I earnestly request your acceptance.”
Duke Zhāo said:
“Since my ancestral temple remains in Lǔ,
although there are robes of my former lords,
I have not yet dared wear them;
although there are vessels of my former lords,
I have not yet used them;
I must firmly decline.”
Duke Jǐng said:
“I, an unworthy one, have modest robes of my late lord,
which I have not yet dared wear;
vessels of my late lord,
which I have not yet dared use;
I ask to use them to feast your followers.”
Duke Zhāo said:
“How can a mourner be mentioned?”
Duke Jǐng said:
“Who is a lord and yet cannot be mentioned?”
At this, Duke Zhāo wailed and wept,
and all the great officers wept as well.
When weeping was done,
they used people as cushion,
canopies as mats,
saddles as tables,
and greeted each other with the appropriate rites.
Kǒngzǐ said, “Their rites and their words are sufficient to be observed!”
In the tenth month, on wùchén day,
Shū Sūn Shě died.
In the eleventh month, on jǐhài day,
Duke Zuǒ of Sòng died at Qūjí.
What is Qūjí?
It is a town of Sòng.
When a feudal lord dies within his domain, it is not considered “outside,”
so why is it so recorded?
Because he died within his inner quarters.
In the twelfth month,
the Duke of Qí took Yùn.
If one seizes an outer town, it is not recorded;
so why is it recorded here?
Because he took it for the Duke.
In the twenty-sixth year, spring, the king’s first month,
Duke Yuán of Sòng was buried.
In the third month,
the Duke returned from Qí,
and lived in Yùn.
In the summer,
the Duke besieged Chéng.
In the autumn,
the Duke met with the Duke of Qí, the Lord of Jǔ, the Lord of Zhūlóu, and the Earl of Qǐ, and joined in oaths at Chuánlíng.
The Duke returned from the meeting,
and resided at Yùn.
In the ninth month, on gēngshēn day,
Zǐ Jū of Chǔ died.
In the winter, the tenth month,
the King of Heaven entered Chéngzhōu.
What is Chéngzhōu?
It is Eastern Zhōu.
Why does the text say “entered”?
To show he was not rejected.
Yǐn Shì, Shào Bó, and Máo Bó fled with Prince Cháo of the king to Chǔ.
In the twenty-seventh year, spring,
the Duke went to Qí.
The Duke returned from Qí,
and resided at Yùn.
In the summer, fourth month,
Wú assassinated their ruler Liáo.
Chǔ killed their grand officer Xì Yuǎn.
In the autumn, Shì Yāng of Jìn, Yuè Qí Lí of Sòng, Běigōng Xǐ of Wèi, men of Cáo, men of Zhūlóu, and men of Téng, met at Hù.
In winter, the tenth month,
the Earl of Cáo Wǔ died.
Kuài Lái of Zhūlóu fled here.
Who is Kuài Lái of Zhūlóu?
He is a grand officer of Zhūlóu.
Zhūlóu had no grand officer;
why, then, is it recorded?
Because of the proximity, it is written.
The Duke went to Qí,
the Duke returned from Qí,
and resided at Yùn.
In the twenty-eighth year, the king’s third month,
Duke Dào of Cáo was buried.
The Duke went to Jìn,
and encamped at Qiánhóu.
In the summer, on bǐngxū day of the fourth month,
Earl Níng of Zhèng died.
In the sixth month,
Duke Dìng of Zhèng was buried.
In the autumn, seventh month, on guǐsì day,
Lord Níng of Téng died.
In winter,
Téng Dàogōng was buried.
In the twenty-ninth year, in the spring,
the Duke returned from Qiánhóu,
and resided in Yùn.
The Marquis of Qí sent Gāo Zhāng to offer condolences to the Duke.
The Duke went to Jìn,
and encamped at Qiánhóu.
In summer, in the fourth month, on Gēngzǐ day,
Shū Ní died.
In autumn, in the seventh month.
In winter, in the tenth month,
the city of Yùn collapsed.
Towns are not usually said to “collapse”;
why does it say “collapsed” here?
Because it refers to the outer wall.
Why refer to the outer wall?
Because the ruler resided there.
In the thirtieth year, in spring, in the king’s first month,
the Duke was in Qiánhóu.
In summer, in the sixth month, on Gēngchén day,
the Marquis of Jìn, Qù Jí, died.
In autumn, in the eighth month,
Jìn Qǐnggōng was buried.
In winter, in the twelfth month,
Wú destroyed Xú,
and Xúzǐ Zhāng Yǔ fled to Chǔ.
In the thirty-first year, in spring, in the king’s first month,
the Duke was in Qiánhóu.
Jìsūn Yǐnrú met Jìn’s Xún Lì at Shìlì.
In summer, in the fourth month, on Dīngsì day,
the Earl of Xuē, Gǔ, died.
The Marquis of Jìn sent Xún Lì to offer condolences to the Duke at Qiánhóu.
In autumn,
Xuē Xiàn Gōng was buried.
In winter,
Hēi Gōng came to take refuge at Làn.
Why does the text not mention Zhūlóu?
Because it connects with Làn.
Why connect with Làn?
Because the descendants of the worthy should have land.
Who are called worthy?
It is Shū Shù.
Why is Shū Shù worthy?
Because he yielded the state.
How did he yield the state?
During the time of Zhūlóu Yán,
there was a daughter of Zhūlóu who became the consort of Lǔ;
was she the consort of Wǔgōng,
or of Yìgōng?
Xiào Gōng was young,
and Yán led the nine sons of the duke to debauchery within the palace,
and thereby brought in traitors;
was it Lǔ’s prince who did this,
or Zhūlóu’s prince?
The mother of the Zāng clan was the one who raised the duke.
When the ruler is young, there must be someone to raise him;
the concubine of a grandee,
the wife of a scholar—
but who exactly was the mother of the Zāng clan?
One who raises the ruler must take her own son to raise him.
The mother of the Zāng clan heard that there were traitors,
so she exchanged her son for the duke,
took the duke in her arms and fled.
When the traitors arrived,
they rushed to the duke’s sleeping quarters and killed him.
There were ministers Bào Guǎngfù and Liáng Mǎizǐ, who, upon hearing of the traitors,
rushed to the scene.
The mother of the Zāng clan said:
“The duke is not dead;
here he is—
I have exchanged my son for the duke.”
Then they carried Xiào Gōng and circled the capital, appealing to the Son of Heaven.
The Son of Heaven executed Yán and installed Shū Shù,
and restored Xiào Gōng to Lǔ.
Lady Yán was the daughter of Yùyíng, famed for her beauty in the state.
It is said:
“Whoever can kill Shāyán for me,
I will be his wife.”
Shū Shù killed Shāyán for her,
married her,
and had a son named Xū.
Xià Fù was the one involved with Yán.
Xū was young,
and both loved him;
at meals, they would always seat the two sons at their sides and feed them.
Whenever there were rare and marvelous dishes,
Xū would always seize them first and have his fill.
Xià Fù said:
“From the start,
before anyone has enough, Xū already has excess.”
Shū Shù realized this,
and said:
“Ah!
Truly, this is your state!”
He arose and yielded the state to Xià Fù.
Xià Fù accepted it but sought to divide it in half.
Shū Shù said:
“No!”
He divided it in three;
Shū Shù said:
“No!”
He divided it in four;
Shū Shù said:
“No!”
He divided it in five;
then he accepted it.
Gōng Hùzǐ, the father’s elder brother of Zhūlóu,
knew the old ways of Zhūlóu,
and said:
“How can a man be so praised as worthy in someone else’s state!”
At the time of the execution of Yán,
the Son of Heaven died,
and Shū Shù arose and offered the state to Xià Fù.
At that time,
the people of Zhūlóu always had to bear arms in Zhōu,
saying:
“Why was our Son of Heaven killed?”
Since it mingled with Làn, why does the text not mention Zhūlóu?
There had never yet been a Làn in the world.
Since there had not yet been a Làn,
why does it state that he fled to Làn?
Shū Shù was a worthy grandee;
if severed, it would mean Shū Shù did not wish to be severed;
if not severed, it would become a hereditary grandee;
yet by duty, a grandee cannot be hereditary,
so it was thus extended and made connected.
In the twelfth month, on the new moon of Xīnhài day,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In the thirty-second year, in spring, in the king’s first month,
the Duke was in Qiánhóu.
Kàn was seized.
What is Kàn?
It is a town of Zhūlóu.
Why is it not attributed to Zhūlóu?
Because it was to avoid naming it repeatedly.
In summer,
Wú attacked Yuè.
In autumn, in the seventh month.
In winter,
Zhòngsūn Héjì met with Jìn’s Hán Bùxìn, Qí’s Gāo Zhāng, Sòng’s Zhòng Jǐ, Wèi’s Shìshū Shēn, Zhèng’s Guó Cān, men of Cáo, Jǔ, Zhūlóu, Xuē, Qǐ, and Small Zhūlóu to build chéng Zhōu.
In the twelfth month, on Jǐwèi day,
the Duke passed away at Qiánhóu.
First year, spring, the king.
Why does Dìng lack the first month?
The first month is when the succession is properly assumed.
That Dìng lacks the first month means the succession was assumed later.
Why was the succession delayed?
Because Zhāogōng was outside,
and whether he would return or not was yet unclear.
Why was it unclear?
Because it depended on the House of Jì.
Dìng and Āi use much veiled speech;
if the one in charge was used to reading the text and inquired into its commentary,
they would not know their own guilt.
In the third month,
the Jìn people seized Sòng Zhòngjǐ at the capital.
What was Zhòngjǐ’s offense?
He did not repair the city walls.
What did he say at the capital?
Bó Tǎo.
If Bó Tǎo, then how did he refer to people?
He disparaged them.
Why did he disparage them?
Because he did not share the authority with the dàfū.
Why did he not share it?
In reality he did, but in form he did not.
Why, in form, did he not share it?
It is the principle of the dàfū that they may not exercise authority alone.
In the sixth month, on the day guǐhài,
the duke’s funeral arrived from Qiánhóu.
On the day wùchén,
the duke ascended the throne.
On the day guǐhài,
the duke’s funeral arrived from Qiánhóu,
so why did he only ascend the throne
on the day wùchén?
When the coffin was set upright between the two pillars,
then the accession took place.
Zǐ Shěnzi said:
“Once the ruler is established in the state,
then one may ascend the throne.”
If the accession does not have a fixed day,
why is it dated here?
Because the record is internal.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the day guǐsì,
we buried our lord, Zhāo Gōng.
In the ninth month,
a grand sacrifice for rain was held.
The Palace of Yáng was established.
What is the Palace of Yáng?
It was the palace of Yáng Gōng.
Why is it called “established”?
Because it should not have been established,
to establish the Palace of Yáng was not in accordance with ritual.
In winter, in the tenth month,
frost fell, killing the beans.
Why was this recorded?
To record anomalies.
This was a calamity affecting the beans,
so why was it recorded as an anomaly?
The anomaly is greater than the calamity.
Second year, spring, first month of the king.
In the summer, fifth month, on the day rénchén,
the Zhìmén gate and the two towers were destroyed by fire.
Why does it say “the Zhìmén gate and the two towers were destroyed by fire”?
Because the two towers were minor.
Then why not say “the Zhìmén gate was destroyed by fire along with the two towers”?
Because the main objects destroyed were the two towers.
If the main objects destroyed were the two towers,
why state them after?
Because the minor should not be mentioned along with the major.
Why is this recorded?
To record the disaster.
In autumn,
the Chǔ people attacked Wú.
In winter, in the tenth month,
the Zhìmén gate and the two towers were newly built.
Why is it said, “newly built”?
Because the repair was extensive.
If old repairs are not recorded,
why is this recorded?
It is a criticism.
What is criticized?
They did not devote themselves to the ducal house.
In the third year, spring, first month of the king,
the duke went to Jìn,
reaching the Yellow River and then returned.
In the third month, on the day xīnmǎo,
the ruler of Zhūlóu, Zǐ Chuān, died.
In the summer, fourth month.
In autumn,
buried Zhūlóu Zhuāng Gōng.
In winter,
Zhòngsūn Héjì and the ruler of Zhūlóu swore an alliance at Zhī.
In the fourth year, spring, second month of the king, on the day guǐsì,
the Marquis of Chén, Wú, died.
In the third month,

the duke met with Liúzǐ, the Marquis of Jìn, the Duke of Sòng, the Marquis of Cài, the Marquis of Wèi, the Viscount of Chén, the Earl of Zhèng, the Baron of Xǔ, the Earl of Cáo, the Ruler of Jǔ, the Ruler of Zhūlóu, the Ruler of Dùn, the Ruler of Hú, the Ruler of Téng, the Earl of Xuē, the Earl of Qǐ, the Ruler of Little Zhūlóu, and the official of Qí at Zhàolíng,
to invade Chǔ.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day gēngchén,
Cài Gōngsūn Guīxìng led troops and destroyed Shěn,
and escorted Shěn Zǐ Jiā back,
and killed him.
In the fifth month,
the duke and the feudal lords swore an alliance at Hàoyóu.
Qǐ Bó Wù died at the meeting.
In the sixth month,
Chén Huì Gōng was buried.
Xǔ moved to Róngchéng.
In autumn, seventh month,
the duke returned from the meeting.
Liú Juàn died.
Who was Liú Juàn?
A dàfū of the Son of Heaven.
When an outside dàfū dies, it is not recorded;
why, then, was it recorded?
Because he served as our ruler’s minister.
Buried Qǐ Dào Gōng.
Chǔ besieged Cài.
Jìn Shì Yǎng and Wèi Kǒngyǔ led troops to attack Xiānyú.
Buried Liú Wén Gōng.
The burial of outside dàfū is not recorded;
why, then, is it recorded?
Because he served as our ruler’s minister.
In the eleventh month of winter, on the day Gēngwǔ,
the Marquess of Cài, together with the son of Wú and the men of Chǔ, battled at Bó Jǔ,
the army of Chǔ was routed.
Why is the ruler of Wú referred to as "Zi"?
He is a barbarian, yet he is concerned for the Central States.
How is he concerned for the Central States?
The father of Wǔ Zǐxū was executed by Chǔ,
so he took his bow and fled from Chǔ,
seeking refuge with Hélǔ.
Hélǔ said:
"One who is to the utmost a gentleman,
to the utmost courageous,
I will raise an army for his sake and avenge his enmity against Chǔ."
Wǔ Zǐxū replied:
"Among the lords, none raises an army for a mere man,
and moreover, I have heard:
serving a ruler is like serving a father.
To violate the righteousness due to one's ruler
in order to avenge one's father,
I cannot do this."
Thus he desisted.
Duke Zhāo of Cài had an audience at Chǔ;
he had a fine fur coat,
Náng Wǎ coveted it,
but Duke Zhāo refused to give it to him,
so for this Náng Wǎ detained Duke Zhāo at Nán Yǐng
for several years,
and then allowed him to return.
When he returned,
he played a decisive role at the Hé.
He said:
"Among the lords of All-under-Heaven,
if there be one able to attack Chǔ,
I beg to be at the vanguard."
The men of Chǔ, hearing this, became angry.
Therefore they raised an army,
ordered Náng Wǎ to command and attack Cài.
Cài sought help from Wú,
Wǔ Zǐxū again said:
"Cài has committed no crime;
it is the men of Chǔ who are unrighteous.
If Your Lordship truly cares for the Central States,
then now is the opportunity."
So they raised an army and aided Cài.
He said:
"Serving the ruler is like serving a father;
in this matter, how can one avenge enmity?"
He said:
"If the father was not justly executed,
then the son may avenge him.
But if the father was justly executed,
and the son avenges him,
he follows the way of violence.
To pursue vengeance without removing harm,
when friends mutually defend one another
but do not take vengeance in each other's stead,
that was the way of the ancients."
Náng Wǎ of Chǔ fled to Zhèng.
On the day Gēngchén,
Wú entered Chǔ.
Why is Wú now not referred to as "Zi"?
Because it has turned against the barbarians.
How has it turned against the barbarians?
When the ruler lodges in the ruler’s quarters,
and the ministers in the ministers’ quarters,
for it is said, she was the mother of the king of Chǔ by marriage.
Fifth year, first month of spring, on the day Xīnhài, the first of the month,
there was an eclipse of the sun.
In summer,
grain was returned to Cài.
Who returned it?
The lords returned it.
Why does it not say the lords returned it?
So many that it cannot be recorded individually,
thus it is written as our act.
Yú Yuè entered Wú.
What is Yú Yuè?
What is Yuè?
"Yú Yuè"—the name could not yet be communicated.
"Yuè"—the name could then be communicated.
In the sixth month, day Bǐngshēn,
Jì Sūn Yǐnrú died.
In autumn, seventh month, Rénzǐ,
Shū Sūn did not dare to die.
In winter,
Shì Yǎng of Jìn led the army and besieged Xiān Yú.
Sixth year, first month of spring, day Guǐhài,
Yóu Sù of Zhèng led the army and destroyed Xǔ,
bringing the Lord Sī of Xǔ back.
In the second month,
the Duke attacked Zhèng.
The Duke returned from Zhèng.
In summer,
Jì Sūn Sī and Zhòng Sūn Héjì went to Jìn.
In autumn,
the men of Jìn seized the envoy of Sòng, Yuè Qílí.
In winter,
the inner city wall was built.
Jì Sūn Sī and Zhòng Sūn Jì led troops to besiege Yùn.
This Zhòng Sūn Héjì,
why is he called Zhòng Sūn Jì?
For having two names;
having two names is against propriety.
Seventh year, first month of spring.
In summer, fourth month.
In autumn,
the Marquis of Qí and the Earl of Zhèng swore alliance at Xián.
The men of Qí seized the envoy of Wèi, Běigōng Jié,
with which to attack Wèi.
The Marquis of Qí and the Marquis of Wèi swore alliance at Shāzé.
A great rain sacrifice.
Guó Xià of Qí led the army and attacked our western borders.
In the ninth month,
a great rain sacrifice.
In winter, the tenth month.
Eighth year, first month of spring,
the Duke attacked Qí.
The Duke returned from attacking Qí.
In the second month,
the Duke attacked Qí.
In the third month,
the Duke returned from attacking Qí.
Duke Lù of Cáo died.
In summer,
Guó Xià of Qí led the army and attacked our western borders.
The Duke met the Jìn army at Wǎ.
The Duke returned from Wǎ.
In autumn, seventh month, Wùchén day,
Marquis Liǔ of Chén died.
Zhào Yǎng of Jìn led the army and attacked Zhèng,
then attacked Wèi.
Buried Duke Jìng of Cáo.
In the ninth month,
buried Duke Huái of Chén.
Jì Sūn Sī and Zhòng Sūn Héjì led the army and attacked Wèi.
In winter,
the Marquis of Wèi and the Earl of Zhèng swore alliance at Qǔpú.
Honored the former lords in sacrificial rites.
What is honoring in sacrifice?
It is complying with the order of sacrifice.
Duke Wén reversed the rites,
in which three withdrew.
Duke Dìng complied with the rites,
and five defected.
There was a theft of the treasured jade and the great bow.
Who was the thief referred to?
It was Yáng Hǔ.
Who was this Yáng Hǔ?
He was the steward of the Jì clan.
If he was merely the steward of the Jì clan,
how could he have obtained the state treasures to steal them?
Yáng Hǔ monopolized the affairs of the Jì clan,
the Jì clan monopolized the state of Lǔ,
Yáng Hǔ detained Jì Sūn,
and the Mèng and Shū Sūn clans alternately provided food for him.
He looked up and inscribed a plank, saying:
"On such-and-such a month and such-and-such a day,
they plan to kill me at Pú Pǔ;
if you have the strength to save me, do so then."
When the day and hour arrived, he departed,
and the one heading south was Yáng Hǔ leaving;
he drove him.
He rode in his chariot.
Jì Sūn said to Lín Nán:
"For generations the Jì clan has had sons;
can you not save me from death?"
Lín Nán said:
"Though my strength is insufficient,
how would I dare not to make every effort?"
Yáng Yuè was Yáng Hǔ's younger cousin,
and served as the charioteer on the right.
Among the followers from the Yáng clan,
there were several dozen chariots.
When they reached Mèng Qú,
Lín Nán threw his driving whip to the ground,
Yáng Yuè got down to retrieve the whip,
Lín Nán lashed the horses,
and passed through the territory of the Mèng clan.
Yáng Hǔ pursued and shot an arrow at him,
the arrow lodging in the gate of the manor.
Nevertheless, the armoring began at Qín Rú.
The assassination failed, and they all withdrew back to their quarters outside the capital, everyone panting from the encounter.
Someone said:
"You attempted to assassinate the lord of a thousand chariots and did not succeed;
is it right to remain here?"
Yáng Hǔ said:
"If a mere child has taken the state,
what of true men?"
He looked up and said:
"There!
There!
Quickly, prepare the chariot."
Once the chariot was ready,
Gōngliǎn Chǔfù led an army and arrived;
only through humility did he manage to escape,
and from then fled to Jìn.
What was the treasure?
It was a white-divided jade disc,
a bow with embroidered inlay,
and a pure blue turtle.
In the ninth year, spring, King’s first month.
In the summer, fourth month, on Wùshēn day,
Duke Chài of Zhèng passed away.
The treasured jade and great bow were recovered;
why is this recorded?
Because they are the state treasures.
Their loss is recorded,
and their recovery is recorded.
In the sixth month,
Duke Xiàn of Zhèng was buried.
In autumn,
the Marquess of Qí and the Marquess of Wèi encamped at Wǔshì.
Lord of Qín passed away.
In winter,
Duke Āigōng of Qín was buried.
In the tenth year, spring, the king's third month,
peace was made with Qí.
In summer,
the Duke held a meeting with the Marquess of Qí at Jiá Gǔ.
The Duke returned from Jiá Gǔ.
Zhào Yǎng of Jìn led forces to besiege Wèi.
Men of Qí came to return the lands of Yùn, Huān, and Guīyīn.
Why did the men of Qí come to return the lands of Yùn, Huān, and Guīyīn?
Kǒngzǐ had visited Jì Sūn,
staying for three months without leaving;
as a result, the men of Qí returned these lands.
Shū Sūn Zhōuqiú and Zhòng Sūn Héjì led forces to besiege Hòu.
In autumn,
Shū Sūn Zhōuqiú and Zhòng Sūn Héjì led forces to besiege Fèi.
Yuè Shìxīn of Sòng fled to Cáo.
Prince Chí of Sòng fled to Chén.
In winter,
the Marquess of Qí, the Marquess of Wèi, and Zhèng Yóusù convened at Ān.
Shū Sūn Zhōuqiú went to Qí.
The Duke of Sòng’s younger brother Chén, along with Zhòng Sòng Tuó and Shí Kōu, fled to Chén.
In the eleventh year, spring,
the Duke of Sòng’s younger brother Chén, along with Zhòng Tuó, Shí Kōu, and Prince Chí entered Xiāo from Chén
and rebelled.
Summer, fourth month.
In autumn,
Yuè Shìxīn of Sòng returned from Cáo to Xiāo.
In winter,
peace was made with Zhèng.
Shū Huán went to Zhèng to preside over a covenant.
In the twelfth year, spring,
the Lord Dìng of Xuē passed away.
In summer,
Duke Xiāng of Xuē was buried.
Shū Sūn Zhōuqiú led forces to demolish Hòu.
Duke Mèng Kōu of Wèi led forces to attack Cáo.

If so, could Zhé's sense of justice justify his establishment?
The answer:
"He could."
How so?
He did not reject the command of the grandfather-king on account of his father's command,
but used the grandfather-king's command to reject his father's command;
this is the higher authority acting toward the lower.
He did not reject royal affairs in favor of family affairs,
but used royal affairs to reject family affairs;
this is the superior acting toward the inferior.

Why do gentlemen compose the *Chūnqiū*?
To rectify times of disorder,

Yet do we know whether it truly does this?
Perhaps the gentlemen delight in speaking of Yáo and Shùn's Way?
And in the end, is it not delightful to be a gentleperson recognized by Yáo and Shùn?
The meaning set by the *Chūnqiū* is to await future sages,
and the delight of gentlemen in its making is indeed in this.
